D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.measured:
2,162 INSERTs into loreweave_usage_billing.usage_logs have been rejected by the database and lost: 2,116 carrying request_status='failed' and 46 carrying 'cancelled'. The CHECK permits only success | provider_error | billing_rejected:
  CHECK ((request_status = ANY (ARRAY['success','provider_error','billing_rejected'])))
The table confirms it — success 71,278, billing_rejected 6,236, provider_error 395, and ZERO rows of either rejected value, because none can ever be written.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.why_it_matters: A failed or cancelled LLM request still consumed provider resources up to the point it stopped. Those rows are the usage and billing record, and every one of them is being discarded at the database with the caller none the wiser — the INSERT carries ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and the error surfaces only in the postgres log. This is the swallowed-signal class: a write that always fails, silently, at scale.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.how_it_was_found: Not by looking for it. Postgres was recreated mid-probe during batch 24 and I read its log to find out why; the constraint violations were sitting in it. The restart itself was benign (RestartCount 0, OOMKilled false, ExitCode 0).
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.not_fixed_and_why: The fix is either to widen the CHECK or to map the writer's vocabulary onto it, and choosing between those needs to know which vocabulary is canonical — this repo already has a recorded case of turn-outcome and call-outcome being two different vocabularies that overlap only at `failed`. Guessing at a BILLING schema mid-loop is exactly the move this loop keeps punishing. Recorded with the measurement so the fix starts from evidence.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.status: FIXED - proven against the production write path 2026-08-26. Violations stopped and the previously-impossible rows now land.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.rederived_and_it_is_far_larger:
The row measured 2,162 lost INSERTs. Re-derived against the running database, the rate is orders of magnitude higher:
    65,847 rejected INSERTs in ONE two-hour window
    775,146 'failed' and 16,851 'cancelled' across 24h of postgres log
    usage_logs held ZERO rows of either value, because none could ever be written
⚠️ Most of that volume is this harness's own eval traffic, so the RATE is contaminated. The mechanism is not: every one of those rows was the usage and billing record for a request that consumed provider tokens before it stopped.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.the_vocabulary_question_the_row_deferred:
The row would not choose between widening the CHECK and mapping the writer, because 'choosing needs to know which vocabulary is canonical'. Read off the code, there is no single canonical one - it is ONE producer emitting different values on different paths:
    sync + stream paths (provider-registry api)   success | provider_error | aborted
    job relay (jobs/usage_relay.go, comment #32)   success | failed | cancelled
    billing_rejected                               written on the rejection path
SIX declared outcomes; the CHECK permitted THREE. Mapping was rejected as LOSSY: 'cancelled' is not 'provider_error' - a request the author stopped is not a provider fault - and folding them would destroy the distinction rather than record it. Widening to the producer's declared SET is the only non-lossy option, and it is not a guess about billing semantics: the set is written down in the producer's own comments.

'aborted' is included because billing/client.go documents it as a recorded terminal outcome, NOT because it was observed - no 'aborted' row appears anywhere in 24h. Widening to the DECLARED set rather than the two values that happened to show up is the difference between fixing the class and fixing the instance.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.the_control_that_could_have_refuted_it:
Widening only helps if no CONSUMER breaks on the new values. Every reader of request_status was enumerated before the change:
    mcp_key_usage.go / usage_by_lane.go   filter = 'success'            unaffected
    server.go query filter                 pass-through                  unaffected
    server.go summary (x2)                 counted != 'success' as an ERROR  ← THE PROBLEM
That last one is USER-FACING: errorRate is a percentage a person reads on their dashboard. Widening alone would have reported a request the AUTHOR cancelled as the AUTHOR's error - a fix to one defect quietly creating another in a number someone trusts. Both summary queries now ENUMERATE the failure statuses (provider_error, billing_rejected, failed) instead of negating success, so a future status must be classified deliberately rather than defaulting to 'error'.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.proof:
A NEW explicit ALTER, because the CHECK lives inside CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and editing it changes nothing on a database that already has the table - the same silent no-op that let the glossary fix exist in four places in the source and be absent from the server. Guarded by the constraint's own current definition so the table re-validates ONCE rather than per boot.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT, from inside the database:
    CHECK (request_status = ANY (ARRAY['success','provider_error','billing_rejected',
                                       'failed','cancelled','aborted']))

AND THE CHANGEOVER IS VISIBLE TO THE SECOND:
    last constraint violation   05:21:01
    first 'failed' row ever     05:21:04
    violations in the 2 minutes after            0   (was 65,847 per two hours)
    rows now persisted                           failed 49 · cancelled 2   (was 0 · 0)
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.what_is_NOT_covered:
- NO CHAT-PATH RUN, deliberately. This defect is a backend billing write and the row itself records it as 'found incidentally, OUTSIDE the tool denominator'. The production write path IS the live proof here, and it is a stronger instrument than a scripted turn: real traffic, before-and-after, timestamped to the second.
- 'aborted' IS UNPROVEN. It was widened on the producer's declared set; no aborted row has landed and none appears in 24h of violations, so whether that path reaches usage_logs at all is unknown.
- THE ROWS ALREADY LOST ARE GONE. The fix is forward-only - the rejected INSERTs were never persisted anywhere, so there is nothing to backfill from. Roughly 792k usage records across the observed 24h window are unrecoverable.
- THE errorRate CHANGE IS UNIT-GUARDED, NOT VERIFIED ON THE DASHBOARD. I asserted the SQL, not the rendered number.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.red_able:
usage-billing-service, 5 guards across internal/migrate and internal/api. Three inverse edits, each restored BYTE-IDENTICAL:
    narrow the widening to one value  -> the declared-set guard
    comment out the ALTER             -> the executable-ALTER guard
    add 'cancelled' to the error set  -> both error-rate guards

🔴 THE FALSIFIER CAUGHT A WEAK GUARD AND A DESTRUCTIVE PROVER, in that order. The ALTER guard originally passed on a COMMENTED-OUT ALTER - a substring match cannot tell SQL from a comment, so it reported a fix the database would never execute; it now matches the statement at the start of a line. And the first falsifier used an unbounded str.replace, which while 'restoring' corrupted an UNRELATED table's status CHECK. Repaired against HEAD until the diff was a pure addition, and the prover rewritten to bounded, line-anchored edits that assert the file is byte-identical afterwards.

D-EDGELESS-NODE-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-GRAPH-R.the_scale_is_the_surprise:
Measured across the instance before designing anything:
    5,351 entities / 455 projects · 4,887 (91%) with no active edge
    440 of the 455 projects have NO edges AT ALL
    isolated per project: p50 2 · p90 7 · p99 41 · max 3,172
So 'the graph has no edges' is the ORDINARY state of a project here, not a corner case, and this read was answering 'nothing' about almost every project it was asked about.

D-EDGELESS-NODE-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-GRAPH-R.the_obvious_fix_was_REFUTED_by_that_meas:
'Also return isolated nodes' would have re-run this repo's own 146K-token composition_list_outline incident on the 3,172-node project. So the fix is capped rows plus a SEPARATELY COUNTED total:
  * a second Cypher read for nodes with no active RELATES_TO, same partition predicates as the edge read (user_id + project_id + archived_at IS NULL), over-fetched limit+1
  * `nodes_total` now comes from a cheap COUNT over the partition instead of len(slice). It was the slice's own length, so a capped read reported its slice as the whole set and an EMPTY slice reported the PROJECT as empty. That number was the actual lie.
  * isolated nodes still pass the view's node-kind facet and are deduped against edge endpoints, so a lens cannot be bypassed and a node cannot arrive twice.
D-EDGELESS-NODE-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-GRAPH-R.proof:
LIVE, K=5, throwaway project, the node SEEDED so the turn arrives holding nothing:
    'Show the graph - what is in this project's knowledge graph?'
    -> kg_graph_query 5/5, returns the node, meta.nodes_total = 1, edges []
    -> the reply names 'Vaskir Thorne' 5/5 - a name only the graph read could supply
The answer is now truthful AND useful: 'Vaskir Thorne (Character). There are currently no relationships (edges) recorded in the graph.' Every falsifier clause passes.

This closes the loop on the row's own `correction`: batch 32 blamed the MODEL for fabricating an absence, and the control showed the model was telling the truth about what the tool returned. The tool is now the one telling the truth.
D-EDGELESS-NODE-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-GRAPH-R.a_green_suite_shipped_a_crash_and_the_li:
🔴 WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE THE SUITE WAS NO HELP. The first deploy raised `kg_graph_query error: 'int' object is not iterable` on the very first live call, with 4,261 unit tests green.

`_records` drains a result as `{k: dict(rec[k])}` - it assumes every value is a MAPPING, because every other caller returns node or relationship properties. A scalar `count(e)` makes it raise. EVERY unit test in this area monkeypatches `_records`, so not one of them touches the real driver shape. `.single()` is the convention for a scalar (facts.py's invalidate_facts_for_day). Now guarded, and the guard pins the PREMISE too - a test that `_records` really does reject a scalar - so the rule can be revisited rather than obeyed if that ever changes.

D-STORED-BUT-UNFINDABLE-UNTIL-INDEXED.rescoped_2026_08_26:
🔴 THE ROW'S CAUSE IS WRONG TWICE OVER, and the second half is a gap in the fix that closed the first.

It says memory_search 'cannot find it until the project is indexed'. Refuted the same way its sibling row was: on ONE project a CHAPTER nonce was found (count 1) and a FACT nonce was missed (count 0) with the identical degraded {'semantic': 'not_indexed'} marker. The real cause was that memory_search had no leg over :Fact at all, fixed by D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEARCH-THAT-EXISTS-TO-FIND-IT.

THAT LEFT THIS ROW'S OWN CHAIN STILL BROKEN, and it is a DIFFERENT cause again. This row is about FORGET: 'memory_forget is told the fact does not exist and correctly declines'. memory_forget REQUIRES a fact_id and its own description says 'only use a fact_id you have seen in an earlier tool result'. Measured immediately after the fact leg shipped, a search hit carried {score, snippet, source_type, text} at BOTH detail levels and NO id. So a later turn could now FIND a fact it still could not forget — one call short, with every part of it looking like it worked.
D-STORED-BUT-UNFINDABLE-UNTIL-INDEXED.the_fix:
Two halves, and both were needed:
  1. memory_search's fact hits project `fact_id`, spelled the way memory_forget spells it, and `fact_id` was added to MEMORY_SEARCH_REF_FIELDS so it SURVIVES the summary projection — summary is the default, and an id the handler emits and the contract drops is an id no caller ever sees. Other hit types are untouched: the contract keeps a ref field only `if k in it`.
  2. `memory_forget.fact_id <- memory_search` declared in argument_emitters, and memory_forget's description now names memory_search instead of saying 'an earlier tool result'. This is the rare entry whose SUPPLIER had to be built before the declaration could be true.
Emitter baseline 61/64 -> 60/63, shrink-only.
D-STORED-BUT-UNFINDABLE-UNTIL-INDEXED.proof:
🔴 THE CONTROL WAS AN ACCIDENT AND IS NONE THE WORSE FOR IT. I declared the emitter and did not rebuild chat-service, which BAKES the registry into its image — the same deploy-order trap this ledger already records once. The run measured a stale registry, and rather than quietly retrying it is kept as the control, because it isolates exactly one variable: same scenario, same fixture, same K, the SAME knowledge-service build (the fact_id projection was already deployed and probed), only the registry differing.

    c-forgetchain1  registry STALE   memory_search advertised 0/5, called 0/5, chain 0/5
    c-forgetchain2  registry DEPLOYED memory_search advertised 5/5, called 5/5, chain 5/5

On the stale build the model called memory_forget with {} , was refused, and worked around it by memory_remember-ing a NEGATION of the fact it had been asked to delete — leaving both the wrong fact and a contradiction in the store.

On the fixed build, every run: memory_search{'query': 'Obsidian Trench'} -> one hit carrying fact_id -> memory_forget with THAT id. Every falsifier clause passes:
  * it targeted the Trench fact the author called wrong, never the brass-compass decoy, 5/5
  * it reused an id search returned, never invented one, 5/5
  * memory_forget SUSPENDED on its Tier-A card (no body) and the store is unchanged, 5/5 — no fact invalidated without a click

The chain closed because R1 answerability is transitive over argument_emitters and put memory_search on the wire — NOT because the refusal said where to go. Its text is still 'The tool DOES declare what this is - fact_id: The id of the fact to invalidate. - so use that to obtain the real value', which states WHAT the argument is and not WHERE to get it. Filed as D-THE-EMITTER-ARM-IS-UNREACHABLE-WITHOUT-A-CONTRACT-ROW.
- THE CARD WAS RAISED, NOT CLICKED. The invalidation itself never executed, so this proves the chain up to the confirm gate and no further. That is the scenario's own bar (a fact invalidated with no card would REFUTE it), not a shortcut.
- The other hit types keeping their shape is unit-guarded, not live-exercised: this run returned only fact hits.

D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.found: 2026-08-22, while asking whether the Postgres exhaustion could have damaged evidence already on disk
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.invariant: A snapshot that FAILED is not a snapshot. A probe that could not run must make the RUN unusable — never appear as a value the diff can compare.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.measured: store_snapshot._psql returns the STRING '__error__:<stderr>' on a non-zero exit, and _counts files it under out['__error__']. That key then flows into the run's `store` as though it were a table, and `store_diff` reports {'loreweave_composition.__error__': {'before': null, 'after': '__error__:... too many clients'}} — A DIFF, which the gate reads as the owning store having MOVED. The affected entry's wrote_count is 1 entirely because of it.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.the_second_exit_of_the_same_class: _scoped_tables filters the sentinel out and returns [] — so a failed information_schema probe produces an EMPTY snapshot that is indistinguishable from 'no tables matched'. Silent where the first is merely wrong.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.why_it_matters_in_both_directions: For a read-intent tool the phantom diff is a false 'this read WROTE to the store' failure. For a write tool an empty snapshot is a false 'nothing landed'. Either way the DATA bar — the loop's strongest assertion — is decided on a measurement that never happened.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.blast_radius: 🔴 SWEPT, not sampled: 1,581 runs across every evidence file on disk. EXACTLY ONE carries the sentinel — batch19-v4, composition_motif_link_edit, run 1 — and ZERO have an empty store.before. That tool's ledger row cites batch19-v5, a later arm, so the damaged run drove no conclusion. The evidence base is intact and this is a latent defect rather than a correction.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.cause_of_the_trigger: The stack idles at 96 of 100 Postgres connections (default max_connections, never overridden), leaving four for tooling. Raised to 300 the same day — see the infra commit. That removes the trigger; it does not remove the defect, because any failed probe takes the same path.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.fix: PENDING — raise from _psql instead of returning a sentinel, so a failed probe surfaces as a run error and the gate's existing 'LIVE clean' bar refuses the batch. Held back deliberately while a 125-run live batch was using the module.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.status: FIXED — the chokepoint fix was ALREADY SHIPPED and this row still said PENDING. Verified end to end 2026-08-26, and the one thing genuinely left (the diagnosis) is done.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.the_row_was_STALE_the_fix_was_in:
The row reads `fix: PENDING ... Held back deliberately while a 125-run live batch was using the module`. Re-derived: `_psql` RAISES `SnapshotUnavailable`, its docstring records the whole defect in the past tense, `_scoped_tables` says 'No sentinel filter any more', and scripts/test_a_failed_snapshot_is_not_a_snapshot_gate.py already guards it (4 tests, green). No code path emits the sentinel — the only two occurrences of that string are inside the docstring explaining what it used to do.

So the work was done and the row was never updated. Checking the code before working from the row is what turned this from a cycle of implementation into a cycle of verification.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.verified_end_to_end: The invariant is 'a probe that could not run must make the RUN unusable'. Traced through the caller: both the BEFORE and AFTER snapshot calls sit inside fe_runner's per-repeat try, so a raise returns a run carrying an `error`, and the gate's existing LIVE-clean bar refuses the batch. Exercised directly: `_psql('no_such_database_at_all', ...)` raises SnapshotUnavailable rather than returning anything the diff could compare.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.what_was_actually_left_the_DIAGNOSIS:
A failed snapshot was labelled `PROVISION`, so the gate reported 'the SEED could not build the fixture, so this is not the platform'. That is false for a snapshot failure and sends the reader at the fixture instead of at Postgres — the SAME mistake the gate's own comment records making once already ('A PROVISION FAILURE IS NOT A TRANSPORT FAILURE, and calling it one sends the reader at the platform').

A snapshot failure now carries its own label and its own sentence. Three causes, three diagnoses, one verdict:
    SNAPSHOT  -> 'the store could not be READ, so this run measures nothing about the tool and nothing about the fixture either'
    PROVISION -> 'the SEED could not build the fixture, so this is not the platform'
    other     -> 'a transport failure is not a model result'
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.what_is_NOT_covered:
- NO NEW GUARD FOR THE DIAGNOSIS. The three branches were exercised directly and print the right sentence, but nothing fails the build if a fourth error class is added and reuses the wrong one. The existing 4-test gate covers the RAISE, which is the invariant.
- THE TRIGGER IS GONE BUT UNVERIFIED HERE. The row records max_connections raised 100 -> 300 the same day; I did not re-check the live setting, because the fix is deliberately independent of the trigger — any failed probe takes the same path.
- THE ONE DAMAGED RUN ON DISK IS UNTOUCHED. batch19-v4 / composition_motif_link_edit run 1 still carries the sentinel in its stored diff. The row's own sweep showed it drove no conclusion (the ledger cites batch19-v5), so it is left as the historical record it is.

D-FIXTURE-WORLD-NEVER-TORN-DOWN.invariant: Everything a fixture creates is torn down, and the teardown's predicate must match what the fixture actually creates.
D-FIXTURE-WORLD-NEVER-TORN-DOWN.measured: 63 worlds on the harness account, 35 of them fixtures named 'Emberfall Reach {run_word}'. TWO guards both failed to reach them: _purge_worlds required a name starting with TITLE_PREFIX, and provision.py --sweep is scoped to book TITLES while a world is not book-scoped.
D-FIXTURE-WORLD-NEVER-TORN-DOWN.why_both_decisions_were_right: 🔴 The seeds name the world 'Emberfall Reach …' ON PURPOSE, and the reason sits 90 lines above the guard that broke on it: an account-scoped fixture called 'LOOP-THROWAWAY-…' had its NAME passed back as a world_id by the model ('I'm having trouble accessing the map (ID: LOOP-THROWAWAY-…)'). So the naming rule was right, the teardown predicate was right, and between them nothing was ever deleted. Neither change was wrong; the pair was.
D-FIXTURE-WORLD-NEVER-TORN-DOWN.fix: The guard now trusts the id THIS RUN'S OWN world_create returned — provenance beats a string prefix and cannot drift when someone renames a fixture — and --sweep gained a world pass scoped to the owner plus the prefix the seeds actually build. D-FIXTURE-WORLD-NEVER-TORN-DOWN.consequence_if_unfixed: A leaked world is not tidy-up debt. It is an account-scoped object the model can find on the NEXT batch, which is the same shape as the leaked BOOK the harness already guards against.
D-FIXTURE-WORLD-NEVER-TORN-DOWN.verified: The 15 fixtures of the re-verification batch (3 scenarios x 5 reps) were ALL torn down: zero of its worlds remain. Three worlds did survive and they are accounted for rather than waved away — all created 12:36-12:37, BEFORE that batch's first snapshot at 12:38:23, i.e. debris from an earlier foreground run killed at a 10-minute cap, which never reached teardown at all. D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.found: 2026-08-22, cycle 1, by a control that REFUTED its own hypothesis
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.invariant: Presence is `in`, not truthiness. An argument that was SENT is present whatever its value.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.measured: `not args_obj.get(r)` — a truthiness test where presence was meant. The model sent {"user_model_id": "…", "value": false}, exactly right, and the check returned ["value"] because `not False` is True. The repair message then told the model to supply what it had just supplied, it retried identically, and the blank-args cap stopped the turn.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.the_control_that_found_it: 🔴 MY HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND THE CONTROL KILLED IT. settings_model_set_active and registry_set_skill_enabled failed 5/5 while settings_model_set_favorite — the SAME shape, a required bare boolean — passed. The obvious reading was that the model omits the boolean when the answer is FALSE ('deactivate'/'turn off' vs 'mark as a favourite'). One tool, two arms differing only in which value the sentence implies. The false arm's RECORDED ARGUMENTS carried `value: false` every time. The model was never at fault.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.worst_consequence: On one such turn the model told the author "I've deactivated Nemotron-3 Nano for you" — a FALSE CLAIM OF A WRITE, caused by a check that discarded the correct argument. It also named a real model on the account.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.blast_radius: Swept from the live catalogue: 37 required arguments across 36 tools can legitimately be falsy. 6 booleans (`false` unreachable — every 'turn off'/'deactivate'/'disable'/'unpublish' intent), 10 integers (`composition_authoring_run_accept_unit.unit_index: 0` is the FIRST unit; `expected_version: 0` is a real version), 2 numbers (`world_map_add_marker.x: 0` is the LEFT EDGE of the map — a pin could not be placed there), 19 arrays (`book_chapter_bulk_create.chapters: []` is the empty-import case this loop has OWED since batch 26).
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.proven_by:
A/B on the identical control scenario, before and after, on the real chat path:
  BEFORE  bool-true  0 'missing required', 0 cap, 5/5 cards | bool-false  4, 4, 0/5 cards
  AFTER   bool-true  0, 0, 5/5 cards                     | bool-false  0, 0, 4/5 cards
The TRUE arm is identical before and after, which is the no-bystander evidence in the same table.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.swept_for_siblings: One other truthiness site exists (`not args_obj.get('project_id')` in the project-scope gate) and is CORRECT: a project_id is a UUID string, so falsy and absent are the same thing there.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.what_it_does_not_fix: It does not make the model choose the right value, and it does not change the blank-args cap's counting. It only stops a correct answer being classified as an absence. A required STRING that is empty or whitespace is still missing — that is what the check was for — and it now catches whitespace, which the truthiness version let through.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.tests: services/chat-service/tests/test_a_falsy_required_argument_is_present.py — falsifier RED on the original (6 of 8 failed), green after. chat-service suite 3323 passed.

D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.why_not_fixed_here: It needs two things, not one. (a) a count scoped to the RUN'S OWN template rather than the owner — an owner-wide sweep folds in the account's 57 unrelated rows and destroys the attribution per-scenario fixtures exist to provide, the same argument _world_counts makes for itself. D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.fix_design_verified_2026_08_23:
The two halves are now specified, and the blocking half is NOT the one I assumed.

(a) PER-RUN FIXTURE — VERIFIED SAFE. `Throwaway._substitute` already handles {run_id}/{run_word} and `assert_seeded` substitutes the seed_assert QUERY too (provision.py:180), so the code and name can both be per-run. `preflight_seed_asserts` replaces any {...} with a dummy UUID and only checks SQL validity, so a placeholder in the predicate does not break the preflight. The name must go per-run as well as the code: provision.py's own comment records that 'batch 19's motifs survived across arms and collided by NAME as well as by code', and the prompt names this template by NAME.

(b) TEARDOWN — THE ACTUAL BLOCKER, AND MAKING (a) ALONE WOULD MAKE THINGS WORSE. Nothing purges arc templates: `Throwaway` has _purge_worlds and _purge_models and no equivalent here, which is why 51 of 57 rows are account-scoped debris in the first place. Give every run a UNIQUE code without a purge and each run leaks a NEW row instead of colliding on one — trading a visible failure for silent accumulation, which is the worse of the two.

So the order is: purge first, per-run fixture second, and only then is the arc-template DATA count worth adding — because until the fixture records which template is ITS OWN, a count has nothing to scope to.

scripts/test_the_data_bar_can_see_an_account_scoped_row.py, 6 guards including an anti-vacuity case that the book-scoped sweep genuinely CANNOT see these rows (if it could, the fix would be pointless). Inverse edit — the counter unwired from snapshot() — reds it; source restored byte-identical. Whole scripts suite: 529 passed.

🔴 AND THE FIRST FIVE GUARDS WERE VACUOUS FOR THAT INJECTION. D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.what_is_NOT_covered:
- ONE TABLE. `RUN_SCOPED_TABLES` holds arc_template only — the measured instance. Other account-scoped tables with a nullable book_id were not censused, so the family is mechanised, not swept.
- IT NEEDS THE SEED TO CARRY THE NONCE. A scenario seeding an account-scoped row with a fixed code is still invisible, and nothing fails if one does. The arc-apply scenario carries it; no gate requires the next one to.
- MATCHING IS `code LIKE '%nonce%'`. A table whose identifying column is not a code — a bare uuid, say — needs a different column named in the tuple, and a nonce that appeared inside unrelated text would over-count. Neither case exists today.
- NO LIVE BATCH. The count is proven against the real store by direct insert/delete, which exercises the same code path a run does; re-running the arc-apply scenario would only re-observe it.

D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.found: 2026-08-23 (registered; the symptom is older and was previously read as generic transport noise)
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.symptom: The turn dies with LLMUpstreamError: upstream sent "error" with no error message (response id "", status "") — the provider reported a failure without saying why. The author sees a turn that stops; nothing names a cause.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.measured: 9 occurrences across 160 cycle-2 runs. It is NOT uniform, which is the finding: composition-motif-link-edit takes 5 of the 9 (25% of its 20 runs) while world-map-delete, glossary-entity-restore, composition-arc-template-edit and composition-authoring-run-review take ZERO across 20 runs each.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.two_hypotheses_refuted: (1) TURN LENGTH — refuted. motif-link-edit averages 2.1 tool calls, among the FEWEST; world-map-create averages 10.0 with 23 max and took only 2. (2) SCHEMA PAYLOAD — refuted. composition-arc-template-edit carries the LARGEST advertised surface measured (17,125 tokens) with ZERO errors, against motif-link-edit's 13,590 with five.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.not_diagnosed_further: I have not explained it, and I am not offering a third hypothesis to cover that. What is established is that it is scenario-CONCENTRATED rather than a uniform sampling flake — which matters, because I previously modelled it as 1.7% per run uniformly and used that to argue a re-run would clear it. For a scenario sitting at 25% it will not.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.consequence: composition_motif_link_edit can be concluded NEITHER proven NOR blocked: gate.py excuses only 'LIVE called' and 'SHIP exercised' for a blocked tool, and LIVE clean is neither — correctly, because a turn that died upstream is no evidence about the tool in either direction. So P3-NAME-TO-ID stands at 6 of 7 and CANNOT be cleared until this is resolved. Cycle 2's invariant holds for the tool itself: called 5/5 in the latest run, supplier armed and reached.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.why_it_matters_beyond_the_loop: A provider failure that carries no message is indistinguishable from a platform bug at the point where an author would report it. Every other refusal on this platform has been made to name its cause and its next move; this one names neither.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.correlation_2026_08_23:
🔴 IT IS NOT RANDOM. Re-run alone at concurrency 1, K=5, the split is exact:
    3 runs ERRORED — every one of them called composition_motif_search first
    2 runs CLEAN   — neither called it; both stopped after composition_motif_link_edit
The chat-service log puts the failure immediately after the surface widens: 'armed recovery tool(s) [composition_motif_search] named in composition_motif_link_edit's missing-argument refusal', then 'agent-surface advertised ... activated=35' followed by 'activated=36', then LLMUpstreamError. So the turn dies on the pass AFTER the arming takes effect — which is to say, at the step cycle 2's fix exists to enable.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.six_hypotheses_refuted:
(1) TURN LENGTH — refuted: this scenario averages 2.1 tool calls, among the fewest; world-map-create averages 10.0 and took 2 errors.
(2) SCHEMA PAYLOAD — refuted: composition-arc-template-edit carries the largest advertised surface measured, 17,125 tokens, with ZERO errors, against this scenario's 13,590 with five.
(3) LOAD / CONCURRENCY — refuted, and it went the WRONG WAY: at concurrency 1 the rate rose to 3 of 5 (60%) from 25% at concurrency 2-3.
(4) ENCODING — refuted: the search result is 4,717 chars, ZERO non-ASCII, NFC-stable.
(5) CONTEXT PRESSURE — refuted by the platform's own accounting: every one of these turns logs 'pressure=0.00 reason=auto_below_threshold'.
(6) THE SUPPLIER ITSELF — refuted: composition_motif_search is PROVEN in its own right, called 5/5 clean in batch20-motif-search-clean.json. Calling it does not kill a turn.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.what_is_left_and_not_guessed: What survives all six is the COMBINATION: a mid-turn surface widening followed by a call to the newly armed tool. Worth noting without claiming it as the cause — this platform already holds 'decide the surface ONCE per turn ⇒ prefix-cache-stable (the Manus lesson)' as a principle, quoted in config.py's oneshot_deadvertise_mode, and every arming site violates it by design. But arc_template_edit ALSO armed mid-turn and ran 5/5 clean, so mid-turn arming alone is not sufficient either. I have not explained it and am not naming a cause I cannot show.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.the_control_this_needs_next:
🔴 THE CONTROL THAT WOULD REFUTE MY OWN FIX, and it has NOT been run. Every failing turn dies on the pass after cycle 2's arming widens the surface. The obvious question is therefore whether the ARMING CAUSES IT — i.e. whether db4ab33c8 introduced a regression on this scenario — and nothing measured so far separates 'the fix enabled a step that was always broken' from 'the fix broke the step'.

THE EXPERIMENT: rebuild chat-service with the missing-argument arming removed (that arm alone, leaving the dispatch-path arming untouched), run scenarios-c2-motif.json at K=5, and compare error rates. Pre-registered reading, written before it runs:
  * CLEAN without the arming  -> the arming causes it. My fix has a regression on this scenario     and the fix, not the tool, is what must change.
  * STILL ERRORING without it -> the failure predates the fix and the fix merely made the model     reach the step that triggers it. The tool stays unconcludable and the cause is elsewhere.
Note the second outcome is NOT a clean bill for the fix: before it, the model stopped early and the turn ENDED, so the author saw an honest refusal instead of a dead turn.

NOT RUN YET because it needs a chat-service rebuild and the 41-tool re-baseline is in flight against the deployed image; rebuilding underneath it would invalidate 205 runs. Queued behind it.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.the_provider_actually_says_2026_08_23:
🔴 THE PROVIDER'S REAL MESSAGE, SEEN FOR THE FIRST TIME: {"error":"Model is unloaded."}, HTTP 400 from LM Studio, hit while replaying a real turn's follow-up pass outside the batch. A moment later /api/v0/models reported the same model state=loaded. So LM Studio's JIT/TTL evicts the model between requests and a turn in flight dies on the next pass.

That is an OPERATIONAL condition — not schema shape, not context length, not concurrency, not the tool set. And it is exactly what the platform's own message erases: chat-service reports it as 'the provider reported a failure without saying why' when the provider said, in four words, precisely why. Ten hypotheses were tested against the model, the schemas, the payload, the encoding, the load and the pass count before anyone read the wire, and every one of them was avoidable.

THE DIAGNOSABILITY DEFECT IS THEREFORE THE REAL ONE, and it is a product defect rather than a harness annoyance: an author whose turn dies this way is told the same nothing. A provider failure must surface the provider's own body, the way every other refusal on this platform is required to name its cause and its next move.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.tenth_hypothesis_refuted: PASS COUNT — refuted. 'More passes span more wall-clock, so more chance of hitting an unload window' predicts a monotonic rate. Measured across every cycle-2 run grouped by pass count: 9 passes 22% (6 of 27), 12 passes 4% (1 of 23), and turns with 40, 48 and 52 passes took ZERO. There is no gradient.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.what_remains_unexplained: The CONCENTRATION. composition-motif-link-edit took 5 of 9 upstream errors across 160 cycle-2 runs while four other scenarios took none over 20 runs each. A transient eviction should be roughly uniform per request; this is not (Poisson p ~ 0.005 for 5 in one of eight scenarios). Either the eviction is not uniform in time and that scenario ran during a bad window, or something about it makes eviction more likely and none of the ten properties tested is it. Recorded as open. What is no longer open is the ARMING: the fix is not implicated by anything measured here, and a turn that dies because the provider dropped the model would have died whatever the surface held.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.recommended_operational_fix: Keep the harness model resident for the duration of a batch — LM Studio's auto-unload/TTL is the mechanism, and this is host-environment configuration rather than code. Worth doing before any further LIVE-clean chasing, because gate.py fails LIVE clean on ANY errored run and an eviction will keep costing whole batches. Not applied here: the 41-tool re-baseline is in flight and changing provider behaviour underneath it would make its runs incomparable.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.a_confound_i_created_2026_08_23:
🔴 I CONTENDED WITH THE RUNNING BATCH AND SOME OF ITS ERRORS MAY BE MINE. `lms ps` reports the harness model at PARALLEL 4 — four concurrent requests — and the re-baseline runs at concurrency 3. While it was in flight I fired a series of DIRECT requests at the same provider to diagnose this defect. Chat-service upstream errors in that hour: 19:08, 19:15, 19:16, 19:30, 19:38, 19:41, 20:10 UTC. My probing window covers roughly 19:20-20:10, so at least three of those sit inside it.

I cannot separate mine from the batch's, so the re-baseline's LIVE-clean failures must be read with that caveat rather than as clean platform evidence. Probing stopped.

It also weakens my own earlier reasoning in a way worth naming: I argued the flake was 'concentrated, not uniform' partly on error counts drawn from windows I was perturbing. The cycle-2 counts (9 over 160 runs) predate the probing and stand; anything measured after 19:20 does not.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.ttl_measured: `lms ps`: TTL 1h/1h, PARALLEL 4, context 200192 of 262144, state GENERATING during the batch. So IDLE unload cannot be the mechanism while a batch is running continuously — the countdown resets on use. The 'Model is unloaded' I saw directly was between batches, after idle. That makes idle-TTL a real but NARROW cause: it explains a first request after a quiet gap, not mid-batch losses.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.correction_the_platform_is_not_erasing_i:
🔴 MY 'THE PLATFORM ERASES FOUR WORDS' CLAIM IS WRONG, AND THIS IS THE SECOND OVER-CLAIM IN THIS ONE INVESTIGATION. provider-registry-service's responses_streamer.go already handles this deliberately, and its comment records the measurement: 'Both sources are routinely empty on LM Studio's Responses stream, and Message is omitempty, so the frame serialized to exactly {"event":"error","code":"LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR"}. ... So say what IS known.' It tries ev.Message, falls back to ev.Response.Error.Message, and only then synthesises a sentence out of the event type, response id and status — all three actionable, none invented.

The difference is the TRANSPORT, and I conflated them. My {"error":"Model is unloaded."} came from a NON-STREAMING POST /v1/chat/completions. The turn path is the STREAMING Responses API, where LM Studio genuinely sends an error frame carrying no message at all. The platform is not discarding a body; there is no body on that path.

So the 'diagnosability defect' I named does not exist as stated, and I nearly rewrote code that is already correct and better-reasoned than my complaint. What remains true and useful is narrower: the same failure IS legible on the non-streaming endpoint, so a service that wanted a cause could ask for one — but that is a design suggestion, not a defect, and it is not this loop's to make.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.correction_wrong_endpoint_2026_08_23:
🔴 EVERY DIRECT PROBE I RAN WAS ON THE WRONG ENDPOINT. The scenario's credential has api_standard='lm_studio', which routes to the STATEFUL /v1/responses API — that is why the error text comes from responses_streamer.go at all. All my reproductions used /v1/chat/completions. So the {"error":"Model is unloaded."} I found is real, and it does NOT establish the cause of these turn failures: it was measured on a transport the turns do not use.

/v1/responses is confirmed working directly (response.created / in_progress / output_item.added frames), so the endpoint is healthy in the ordinary case. What a FAILING /v1/responses frame carries, I have not captured — and that is exactly the thing worth capturing, because responses_streamer.go's own comment says both message fields are routinely empty there.

THE STATE OF THIS DEFECT IS THEREFORE: reproducible in the harness at ~40% for one scenario (12 of 30 runs), NOT reproducible by me outside it, and NOT explained. Eleven hypotheses tested and refuted, two of my own claims about it retracted, and this is the third. Recorded as open with the count, rather than closed on the nearest plausible story.

composition-motif-link-edit, four independent arms, each removing one candidate explanation:

D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.twelfth_hypothesis_refuted: TURN COUNT — refuted. D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.measured:
FOUR of the 315 federated tools serve an inputSchema of exactly {additionalProperties:false, type:object} with NO `properties` key — glossary_list_system_standards, settings_get_defaults, settings_get_profile, settings_list_providers. All four are zero-argument reads. VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE GATEWAY (tools/list, 315 tools), not just the cached dump.

LM Studio REJECTS each one, alone, deterministically — HTTP 400 with a precise body:
  code invalid_type, expected object, received undefined,
  path [i,'function','parameters','properties'], message 'Required'
Adding `properties: {}` makes all four accepted in a single request. That is the candidate fix and it is measured, not proposed.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.why_it_matters: The provider validates the WHOLE tools array, so one such schema 400s the entire request — the turn dies whatever tool the model wanted. The account's primary model is local (lm_studio, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat, 200K context), which is this platform's stated target rather than a fallback.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.and_the_platform_hides_the_reason: chat-service reports this as 'upstream sent "error" with no error message ... the provider reported a failure without saying why'. The provider said exactly why. Whatever maps the failure to that message is discarding a body that names the offending tool INDEX and field — the single most actionable thing about it.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.d8_does_not_catch_it: The tool-free retry (design D8) is gated on _is_tools_unsupported, which matches only 'TOOLS_NOT_SUPPORTED'. A schema-validation 400 is not that, so it propagates and kills the turn instead of degrading to a tool-free pass.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.what_is_NOT_established: 🔴 WHY SOME TURNS SURVIVE. glossary_list_system_standards appears in the advertised set of EVERY pass of BOTH the clean and the failing runs, yet 2 of 5 completed. If the rejection were deterministic for every request carrying it, none would. So either the advertised NAME list in the agentSurface event is not what is finally SENT (the superseded gate withholds 83 legacy tools after that event, so the sent list is demonstrably narrower), or something repairs the schema on some paths. I could not settle it from outside: it needs the tool names actually sent to be logged, which needs a chat-service rebuild, and the 41-tool re-baseline is in flight against the deployed image. Recorded as open rather than smoothed over — the correlation with composition_motif_search's arming is real and unexplained, and this defect may be its cause or merely its neighbour.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.retraction_2026_08_23:
🔴 I WAS WRONG, AND THE REFUTATION IS IN THE CODE I SHOULD HAVE READ FIRST. chat-service already normalises this at the MCP->OpenAI conversion boundary. app/client/knowledge_client.py's `_normalize_tool_parameters` does `params.setdefault('properties', {})`, and its docstring names the exact tool and the exact failure: 'OpenAI-compatible providers (e.g. LM Studio) REQUIRE a `properties` object — a tool with an empty input (e.g. glossary_list_system_standards, whose Go input struct is empty) yields {"type":"object"} with no `properties`, which 400s the WHOLE request.' It is applied at BOTH conversion sites (lines 675 and 788).

So the 400 I reproduced was an ARTIFACT OF MY OWN TEST: I sent the raw MCP inputSchema out of contracts/tool-catalog-cache.json straight at LM Studio, bypassing the normaliser the real path always applies. Every measurement in the original entry is accurate — the four tools DO serve a properties-less schema, LM Studio DOES 400 on it, `properties: {}` DOES fix it — and the CONCLUSION drawn from them was still wrong, because the platform already does exactly that.

IT ALSO ANSWERS THE QUESTION I LEFT OPEN, in the opposite direction to my guess. I asked why some turns survive when glossary_list_system_standards is advertised on every pass of both clean and failing runs. The answer is that they ALL survive it: the normaliser is unconditional, so this schema has never reached the provider unrepaired and was never a candidate cause for the motif failures.

WHAT SURVIVES THE RETRACTION, and is worth keeping: chat-service still reports a provider failure as 'upstream sent "error" with no error message ... without saying why' while the provider's body is precise. That mapping is what sent eight hypotheses at the model, the schema size, the concurrency and the encoding before anyone looked at the wire — but on this evidence it is a DIAGNOSABILITY complaint, not the cause of anything measured here. D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE remains open and unexplained; this was not it.

D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.measured: world_map_add_marker, K=5, fresh: called 5/5, and after the refusal the model calls world_map_list THIRTEEN times per run and never resolves. Cycle 2's arming is working — the refusal names world_map_list, the arming puts it on the wire, and the model walks to it — but world_map_list ITSELF requires a world_id the model does not have. The real chain is world_list -> world_map_list -> world_map_add_marker and the declaration names only the middle link.
D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.why_it_matters: Cycle 2 measured that the model walks a supplier chain exactly when it can see the supplier, and fixed reachability one link at a time. This is the case that shows one link is not always enough: a supplier can have an unmet supplier of its own, and the author sees a turn that tries thirteen times and gives up. The model's own words stay truthful throughout — 'I'm having trouble accessing your Ashfall map' — so nothing is fabricated; it simply cannot finish.
D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.candidate_fix_not_shipped: world_map_list's world_id already names world_list, so the chain IS declared end to end — what is missing is that the REFUSAL the model gets from world_map_list arms world_list only if the model calls world_map_list with a MISSING world_id rather than a guessed one. Whether the arming should follow a chain transitively is a design question, not a declaration gap, and it is not this cycle's to answer.
D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.consequence: world_map_add_marker's old P5-SIBLING-WINS cause is REFUTED: it no longer calls world_map_add_REGION at all. Its live cause is this chain, which belongs to P3's family.
D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.resolved_2026_08_25:
🔴 THIS IS THE CASE THAT PROVED THE CLASS FIX, and its own candidate_fix was the wrong shape. That note said 'whether the arming should follow a chain transitively is a design question' and treated the declaration chain as already complete because world_map_list's world_id names world_list IN ITS DESCRIPTION PROSE. Prose arms nothing: the arming and R1's transitive forcing both read argument_emitters, where neither world_map_add_marker.map_id nor world_map_list.world_id was declared at all.

Both are declared now (map_id <- world_map_list, world_id <- world_list, each verified against the struct that serialises the field). Measured live K=5, batch c-emitter1: the thirteen-call loop is gone and every run walks world_list -> world_map_list -> world_map_add_marker with a real map_id, suspending on the confirm card 5/5. See D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-THE-MODEL-CANNOT-GET.proven_live_2026_08_25.

It printed 0 while two runners were live, the kill built on it was a no-op, and the empty output read as 'stopped'. D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.status: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-23, same day it was filed — the call order refutes it
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.what_i_claimed: That when a sibling wins, the staged card does a DIFFERENT thing from what was asked — kg_add_nodes for 'record that they know each other', plan_compile for 'create the chapters' — and that one case escalated scope.
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.why_it_is_wrong:
The card is on the LAST call in all six, with reads before it, and in five of six that last call is the PREREQUISITE of what was asked: nodes before an edge, compile before apply, the entity before the chapter link, the project before the build. The model is doing step 1 of 2, not substituting. And every scenario is approve=None, single-turn, no prior_turns, so the turn ends at that card and step 2 never happens.

kg_add_nodes is not 'nodes instead of the edge'. It is the nodes the edge needs.
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.what_survives: Only the narrow observation already recorded against the approval card: it carries a tool NAME and args JSON and no human-readable description of the action. That was true before this defect was filed and is unaffected by its withdrawal.
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.the_lesson: I read an OUTCOME (card owned by another tool) as an INTENT (the model preferred it) without looking at the ORDER. The order was in the same records the whole time. A classification built on which tool holds the card, with no sequence, cannot tell a rival from a prerequisite — and it produced a whole new problem, P14, out of a harness artefact.

superseded_content.status: OPEN — measured, 6 tools / 30 runs, zero errors
superseded_content.what:
When a sibling wins the request, the confirm card it stages does NOT do what was asked, and in 4 of the 6 the turn produces NO TEXT AT ALL to say so. Measured from the recorded prompts and pending cards:
  'Record that Aldric Vane and Mira Solene KNOW EACH OTHER' -> card: kg_add_nodes. Approving it creates the two nodes and NOT the relationship, which was the whole request.
  'Aldric appears in this chapter — MARK WHERE he shows up' -> card: glossary_propose_entities. The occurrence link is dropped.
  'CITE where it says he climbed the black stair' -> card: glossary_extract_entities_from_doc. The citation is dropped.
  'Create the chapters — make the plan REAL' -> card: plan_compile. Nothing is created.
superseded_content.the_severe_instance: SCOPE ESCALATION, verified from source. The user asked 'IN THIS BOOK Aldric Vane should be a cartographer, not a soldier'. composition_entity_override_edit is declared 'a per-Work entity override (BOOK-LOCAL field changes on a glossary entity)', scope=book. The card staged instead was glossary_entity_set_attributes, which writes the GLOSSARY ENTITY'S OWN attribute values — it applies everywhere, not just in this book. A book-local request was staged as a global write, and the turn said nothing.
superseded_content.why_it_is_worse_than_a_miss: A miss leaves the author where they started. This hands them an approval card that reads as the answer to their request and performs a different action, sometimes at a wider scope. It is invisible to every check this loop runs on the tool under test: surfaced 5/5, errors 0/5, called 0/5.
superseded_content.not_added_to_false_statement_tools: Deliberate, and worth seeing rather than quietly deciding. That field has meant the turn SAYING something false, and 4 of these 6 turns say nothing at all. A silent card that acts more broadly than asked may well belong there — it changes the ordering rule's output if it does, so it is the owner's call and is left visible instead of being stretched by me to fit.
superseded_content.correction_what_the_author_actually_sees:
🔴 I OVERSTATED THIS AND AM NARROWING IT. My first write-up said the substituted card 'reads as the answer to their request' and left the impression the author has nothing to go on. Checked against the frontend rather than the runner's record: ToolApprovalCard renders the TOOL NAME in mono, the tool's ARGS as pretty-printed JSON when non-empty, the tier badge, and 'This write is undoable.' So the substitution IS visible in principle — an author who reads 'kg_add_nodes' and its args can see no edge is being created.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and it is the whole defect: the card carries NO human-readable description of what the tool does and NO connection to what was asked, and 4 of the 6 turns added no prose at all. So the author must infer, from a bare identifier and a JSON blob, that their request to record a RELATIONSHIP will instead create two nodes. That is a real gap and a smaller one than I first wrote.

IT ALSO NARROWS THE D-SILENT-TURN INTERACTION. That guard deliberately exempts card-bearing turns because 'the card IS the output and prose is legitimately absent'. That premise holds when the card matches the request. It is weakest exactly here — a card for a tool the request did not imply — and the exemption is why these 4 silent turns were never counted as silent.
superseded_content.candidate_fix: Put the tool's own one-line description on the approval card. The payload already carries `tool`; the frontend has no catalogue to look it up in, so the description would have to ride the pending payload. Small, testable, and it addresses the measured gap directly — but it changes the approval surface, so it is written down as a candidate rather than shipped mid-cycle.

D-SUPPLIER-RETURNS-COUNTS-NOT-THE-IDS-IT.fix_shipped_but_unmeasured_2026_08_23:
SHIPPED AND VERIFIED DEPLOYED, AND THE RE-RUN DID NOT EXERCISE IT. Say the second part first, because the numbers look like a win and are not attributable.

Deployed: image md5 92da000b verified equal to source, ai-gateway restarted so the changed output schema re-federates, and a live call confirms `nodes` rides the response through the gateway without the additionalProperties rejection that broke settings_list_models earlier today.

The K=5 re-run (p4-chain-fix) reads 5/5 called, the invented 66966666-... gone, real platform UUIDv7 ids in its place, and the edge landing in triage 1/5 where it was 0/5. Every one of those is TRUE and NONE of it is evidence for this fix: the projection returned `entities_seen: 0, nodes: []` on the runs inspected, so the fix had nothing to return and was never on the path. The ids the model used came from glossary_propose_entities, not from `nodes`.

WHAT THE RE-RUN DID REVEAL, which is a better diagnosis than the one it replaced: the model is passing GLOSSARY ENTITY ids where GRAPH NODE ids are required. rep3 says so exactly — 'edge endpoint(s) are not yet graph nodes: 01a02c62-...'. The two stores issue different ids for the same character, and nothing in the chain tells the model which kind it is holding. In 3 of 5 it also used ONE id for BOTH endpoints, which the tool correctly refuses.

So the fix is right and its measurement is owed. What is needed is a fixture where the glossary entities EXIST before the projection runs — entities_seen must be non-zero — or the run cannot speak to this defect at all.
D-SUPPLIER-RETURNS-COUNTS-NOT-THE-IDS-IT.attempt_1_2026_08_26_found_the_fixture_g:
🔴 BATCH c-kgedge1: THE DEFECT REPRODUCED, THE FIX STILL WAS NOT ON THE PATH, and both halves are recorded because the second is the reason to keep going.

                    target_entity_id: 019ff61b-7ece-777a-a006-b9bd0ca7eb0c}

D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.status: FIXED 2026-08-23 — measured, and the fix demonstrably ran
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.what:
The model passes the turn's ambient book_id as BOTH source_entity_id and target_entity_id on kg_propose_edge. Proven by identity, not inference — the run's own book_id equals the value the tool refused, in three of three inspected runs:
  rep0 book_id 01a02c60-696c-724e-bbc7-46c0d97270f2 == passed as both
  rep1 book_id 01a02c61-12bc-731d-9408-6c2e4b3e07e0 == passed as both
  rep2 book_id 01a02c61-bbfd-7821-ba26-df09189ace2a == passed as both
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.why_no_guard_catches_it: Every existing arm tests for a value that looks WRONG — not a UUID, SCREAMING_SNAKE, whitespace, a placeholder word. A book_id is a real, current, valid platform UUIDv7 that the runtime itself injected. It is the most plausible-looking wrong answer available, and it is the one the model reaches for when it needs an id it does not have.
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.the_checkable_invariant:
An argument the contract does NOT declare as context-supplied must not equal one of the turn's ambient context ids (book_id / project_id / chapter_id). The runtime KNOWS those values — it injected them — so this is an identity comparison, not a heuristic, and its precision is high: a book id is never an entity id.

Measure its RECALL before claiming it fixes this tool, and its PRECISION over the corpus before shipping — a tool that legitimately takes book_id in a non-context argument would be broken by it, and this loop has already paid twice for a rule adopted on one instance.

D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.recall_limit:
🔴 THE GUARD ONLY SEES CONTEXT IDS THE MODEL ECHOED BACK IN THE SAME CALL. It compares a suspect value against args_obj's own book_id/chapter_id/project_id. When the model passes an ambient id it did NOT also include as an argument — say chapter_id as an entity_id, with no chapter_id argument on that call — there is nothing to compare against and the guard is blind.

The runtime KNOWS those values, because it injected them, so a fuller version would compare against the turn's ambient context rather than the call's own arguments. D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.status: FIXED 2026-08-27 — the probe now reads the lifecycle column and settles what it previously could only flag as INCONCLUSIVE.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.what: idempotency_probe decides by comparing ROW COUNTS before and after the second call. A tool that SOFT-archives the prior rows and writes replacements grows the table and is reported 'NOT IDEMPOTENT — the second call DUPLICATED', which is false: the old rows are archived, not live. composition_motif_bind_edit is the measured case.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.fix_direction: Where the table carries a lifecycle column, compare ACTIVE rows — the probe already knows the table names, and store_snapshot already reads these stores. Until then, read a growth verdict on a soft-archiving tool as a QUESTION rather than an answer.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.the_fix:
A growth on a soft-archiving table used to be reported '🔴 NOT IDEMPOTENT — the second call DUPLICATED: outline_node 3->5' (false: the old rows were archived), and a later pass softened it to '⚠ INCONCLUSIVE' while NAMING the check that would settle it. That check now runs: ACTIVE counts are taken at the mid boundary — the state the SECOND call acts on — and compared after it.
    unchanged active + grown total -> IDEMPOTENT IN EFFECT, archive-and-replace
    active moved too               -> NOT IDEMPOTENT, the growth is live rows
    counts unreadable              -> INCONCLUSIVE, which is the honest third answer
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.status_means_four_things_and_the_obvious:
🔴 THE NAIVE FIX WOULD HAVE FAILED ON THE TABLE THE DEFECT WAS MEASURED ON. Read from the store rather than assumed:
    arc_template / composition_work / motif   active | archived            <- lifecycle
    outline_node                              done | drafting | empty | outline
    structure_node                            drafting | outline
    glossary_entities                         active | draft | inactive | rejected
So `status <> 'archived'` is a lifecycle test for three tables and a WORKFLOW state for the other three — and outline_node is exactly the table the measured case grew. Its archive flag is `is_archived` (65 of 640 rows true); glossary_entities' is `deleted_at` (34 set). One column name, four meanings, so the predicate is per-table.

Pinned by a guard: injecting the naive `status <> 'archived'` on outline_node reds two cases, including the one asserting the active count still differs from the total — with the naive predicate it would not, and the new count would carry no information at all.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.it_almost_shipped_DEAD:
🔴 THE FIRST DRAFT RETURNED {} FOREVER AND LOOKED FINE. `oracle` is imported inside functions in idempotency_probe.py, not at module scope, so the new counter raised NameError on every table — and my own `except Exception: continue` turned that into 'no counts', which the verdict reads as INCONCLUSIVE. The fix would have shipped, changed nothing, and produced exactly the output the defect already produced.

Caught by exercising it against the real store rather than trusting the unit path. The catch is now narrowed to the query failing, so a programming error RAISES; a guard asserts every table produces a count.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.what_is_NOT_covered:
- NO LIVE PROBE RUN. The counter and the verdict branches are exercised against the real store, but composition_motif_bind_edit was not re-probed end to end — that needs a fixture whose second call actually archives, and the measured instance is from 2026-08-23.
- SIX TABLES, HAND-LISTED. A soft-archiving table outside `_ACTIVE_PREDICATE` still gets a row-count verdict; a guard asserts the two sets match, but nothing discovers a NEW soft-archiving table.
- book_id IS ASSUMED. Every predicate is scoped `WHERE book_id = ...`, so an account-scoped soft-archiving row (arc_template with a NULL book_id) counts zero here — the same blind spot D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-TEMPLATE fixed for the DATA bar, still present in THIS reader.
- THE THIRD VERDICT IS STILL REACHABLE and should be: if a count cannot be read, INCONCLUSIVE is the honest answer rather than a guess in either direction.

🔴 AST, NOT TEXT, AND THAT DISTINCTION COST TWO FAILURES. A text sweep over exception handling cannot see scope: my first attempt rewrote 40 handlers and produced TEN sites where `exc` was unbound (UnboundLocalError at runtime), then a scope-aware text repair mis-read the multi-line raise form and BROKE an existing guarantee (TOOLV2 LOOP #170).     NAME IT   KeyError / ValueError / TypeError / InvalidOperation / BookClientError - the

    STAY BARE OwnershipError / InsufficientGrant / ConfirmTokenInvalid / LookupError
LookupError is in the second list because an existing guard put it there and refuted me: 'not-found and not-permitted must stay UNIFORM'. If a missing thing answers differently from a forbidden one, the PAIR of answers is the oracle whatever either says alone.

D-CONFIRM-REFUSAL-IS-AN-OPAQUE-ACTION-ER.why_the_live_bar_cannot_be_met_without_b:
The two named branches are unreachable from the product, and the last route to them is closed by a rule I will not break:

  THE CHAT PATH cannot reach them. The confirm route sits behind the MCP tool's own validation, which catches the same conditions earlier and already answers well - probed on a throwaway book, every attempt was refused at the tool layer with an actionable message and not one bare action_error.

  THE PAYLOAD BRANCH fires only when the TOKEN's payload lacks run_id. The tool always sets it, so producing that state means MINTING A CONFIRM TOKEN with the service's JWT secret. That is inventing a credential, which SAFETY forbids outright ('never scrape a token, never invent a credential'). I am not doing it, and the rule is right: a loop that forges a credential to demonstrate a refusal has learned to forge credentials.

  THE UPSTREAM BRANCH needs book-service to be down. Taking a shared service down to produce a 502 on a dogfood stack is a bigger action than the evidence is worth, and it is not a throwaway fixture - it is everyone's book-service.

So the honest position is not 'not yet proven'. It is that this fix CANNOT be proven the way the objective asks, by construction, and no amount of further work changes that.

D-BLANK-ARGS-CONCENTRATES-WHERE-NO-AMBIE.what:

D-BLANK-ARGS-CONCENTRATES-WHERE-NO-AMBIE.the_pattern: The hardest-hit tools are the ones whose required arguments are ALL opaque ids with no ambient source — world_id, map_id, marker_id. A turn carries book_id/chapter_id/project_id for free, so a tool that needs one of those can be completed from context; a world/map tool needs an id that exists only in a PRIOR TOOL RESULT, and if the channel emits nothing there is nothing to recover from.

D-BLANK-ARGS-CONCENTRATES-WHERE-NO-AMBIE.not_a_fix_yet: Deliberately measured before proposing anything. The obvious mitigation — fill a blank required arg from a recent tool RESULT — is not obviously safe: it would guess which prior id the model meant, and this loop has a standing rule that a guess gating a correctness question must fail safe. Its precision would have to be measured first, the way the context-id guard's was.

D-EMPTY-ID-REACHES-THE-DATABASE-UNVALIDA.rederived_and_it_is_three_tools_not_two:
The row names jobs_cancel and jobs_pause. Probed against the deployed build, the same driver error came back from THREE tools and for TWO kinds of bad input:

    jobs_cancel('')            invalid input for query argument $2: '' (invalid UUID '')
    jobs_cancel('not-a-uuid')  ... (invalid UUID 'not-a-uuid': length ... got 10)
    jobs_pause  - identical, both inputs
    jobs_get    - identical, both inputs        <- NOT in the row

One cause under three names: all three call the same `store.get_job`, which passes the raw string to `$2::uuid`. And it was never only about EMPTY - any unparseable id does it, which is the likelier failure in practice (a model that drops or repeats a uuid segment).
D-EMPTY-ID-REACHES-THE-DATABASE-UNVALIDA.the_fix:
`_job_uuid` in the jobs MCP server, applied BEFORE the store call at both chokepoints - `_control` (which serves cancel and pause) and `jobs_get`. The wording mirrors composition's `_uuid`, deliberately: name the field, state the rule, ECHO the value. Echoing is the part that carries information the caller cannot otherwise get - a duplicated segment is visible in its own string and invisible in 'badly formed'.

It also names the SUPPLIER: 'Get it from jobs_list, which returns the service and job_id together.' A caller holding no valid id needs the source, not just the complaint.

AFTER, on the deployed build, all six cases:
    job_id must be a UUID - received ''. Get it from jobs_list, which returns the service
    and job_id together; a repeated or dropped group is the usual cause.
driver_error=False on 6 of 6.

- THE CHAT PATH DOES NOT TRIGGER IT, so the refusal's live proof is the direct MCP probe rather than a batch. Measured K=5: the model called jobs_list FIRST on 5/5, got real ids, and asked which job to stop - it never sent a malformed id. Zero driver errors across the batch, which shows no regression; it does not exercise the branch. Engineering a prompt to force a malformed id would be building a scenario to hit my own fix.
- THE REST ROUTER HAS THE SAME DEFECT AND IS UNTOUCHED. app/routers/jobs.py types job_id as `str` at two call sites into the same store function, so a malformed id there still reaches asyncpg. Named rather than swept: this row is about the tool surface, and a 500-to-400 change on a public route is a separate decision.
- `service` IS STILL UNVALIDATED. An unknown service string is not a UUID problem and does not hit this path, but nothing checks it against the known set either. Not measured.

D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.what:
kg_triage_schema_write accepts a `signature` that does not exist, mints a confirm token for it, and the redemption APPLIES the schema change:
    signature = 'no-such-signature-000', action = add_to_schema, code = 'probe_edge_absent'
    -> {"applied": true, "schema_version": 2, "stamped": 0, "resolved": 0}
The edge type is added to the project's ontology. `resolved: 0` is the tell — the tool knows it resolved no triage group, and applies the mutation anyway.
D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.why_it_matters: The tool's whole contract is 'Resolve a schema-mutating triage signature group'. The signature is the AUTHORITY for the change: it says a real proposal needed this edge type. Without validating it, any caller that invents a signature can mutate a project's ontology, and the response says applied:true — so nothing downstream can tell the difference.
D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.it_reached_the_boundary_only_after_a_pre: The first probe refused with 'this project has no adopted ontology to edit', which is a refusal arriving BEFORE the boundary — the same trap recorded for kg_propose_edge and glossary_create_chapter_link today. An ontology was adopted into the probe project first, and only then could the signature check be tested. A boundary probe that stops at the first refusal reports a guard that was never exercised.

D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.why_the_mint_and_NOT_the_shared_apply_ef:
The obvious place looks like `apply_triage_schema_write`, where the mutation actually happens, and refusing there on `resolved == 0` would have been WRONG. Two callers reach that effect in different states: the REST resolve route marks the batch resolved in the same request and arrives with nothing left pending, so a zero count is legitimate for it (`resolve_signature` only touches PENDING). Refusing on it would have broken the REST path while fixing the MCP one.

The MCP path is the one that mints a token and never touches the items, so PENDING is exactly the right predicate AT THIS MINT and nowhere else. The guard is therefore at the single MCP chokepoint, and the effect is untouched - pinned by a test that fails if someone later adds a zero-resolve refusal to it.

D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.what:
memory_forget re-stamps a Fact's `valid_until` on EVERY call and reports {'invalidated': true} each time. Measured in Neo4j directly:
    before a repeat call : valid_until = 2026-08-23T07:52:12.211Z
    after                : valid_until = 2026-08-23T07:54:29.154Z
The fact was already invalidated. The second call moved WHEN it stopped being true.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.why_it_matters: valid_until is the temporal record — the moment the fact ceased to hold. Re-stamping it means a fact invalidated at 07:52 now claims it was valid until 07:54, so any as-of query in that window returns a fact the author had already retracted. This is the exact case the idempotency bar names: a second call 'must not corrupt what the first call wrote'.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.the_response_cannot_reveal_it: Both calls answer {'invalidated': true}, identical. A caller cannot tell a real invalidation from a re-stamp, and the tool DOES have a false form — an absent fact_id correctly answers {'invalidated': false, 'reason': 'no matching fact found'} — so the honest answer exists and is not used here.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.measured_by: direct Neo4j read before/after a repeat memory_forget through the MCP surface, 2026-08-26; guard run with TEST_NEO4J_URI against infra-neo4j-1
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.closed_2026_08_26:
🔴 I DID NOT FIX THIS; I MEASURED IT. The repair shipped in commit 8fa3c4687 ('a repeat invalidate rewrote WHEN a fact stopped being true - both fact and relation') and the row stayed open, so what was owed here was the MEASUREMENT, not code.

RE-DERIVED AGAINST NEO4J, not read off the Cypher - a code comment claiming a repair is a lead exactly like a ledger claim is:
    before any forget   valid_until = NULL
    after forget #1     valid_until = 2026-08-26T03:48:00.737Z
    after forget #2     valid_until = 2026-08-26T03:48:00.737Z   <- UNMOVED
The first stamp sticks. `_INVALIDATE_FACT_CYPHER` now reads `coalesce($valid_until, f.valid_until, datetime())`, so the existing value wins over a fresh `datetime()` and an EXPLICIT caller-supplied time still beats both.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.the_guard_and_its_falsifier:
The repair is guarded, and the guard is red-able on the ORIGINAL defect. tests/integration/db/test_facts_repo.py:
  test_a_repeat_invalidate_does_not_move_when_the_fact_stopped_being_true
  test_an_explicit_valid_until_still_wins  (the control for the coalesce ORDER - preserving the first stamp must not silently swallow a caller correcting the time)
Both SKIP without TEST_NEO4J_URI; run against the live instance they pass, and restoring the original `coalesce($valid_until, datetime())` reds the first and leaves the control green. Restored by inverse edit and verified byte-identical to HEAD by sha.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.the_siblings_were_checked_and_are_NOT_vu:
Two other invalidators carry the UN-repaired `coalesce($valid_until, datetime())`, and the falsifier surfaced them by refusing to restore a unique anchor - three occurrences, not one. That is the pair-fixed-at-one-end shape, so it was chased rather than assumed:

    invalidate_facts_for_day
    invalidate_all_facts_for_project

BOTH ARE SAFE, and for a different reason than invalidate_fact. Their WHERE carries `AND f.valid_until IS NULL`, so a repeat matches NOTHING and there is nothing to re-stamp - the guard is in the match, not the SET. `invalidate_fact` matches by id alone (`MATCH (f:Fact {id: $id})`), which is exactly why it needed the coalesce and they do not. Two mechanisms, both correct; recorded because the near-miss would have been a filed defect that does not exist.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.the_response_half_is_not_a_defect_now: The row's second observation stands as fact and no longer as harm: both calls still answer {'invalidated': true}, identically. It was offered as evidence that a caller could not DETECT the corruption - 'a caller cannot tell a real invalidation from a re-stamp'. With the corruption gone there is nothing to detect: the second call is a genuine no-op and reporting success over a no-op is what idempotent means. The tool's false form ({'invalidated': false, 'reason': 'no matching fact found'}) still fires for an absent id, which is the case where the distinction carries information. Not claimed as fixed and not left open - stated, because the row's own why_it_matters is entirely about valid_until.

D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-IS-BLIND-TO-NEO4J-OW.what: idempotency_probe compares store_snapshot before/after, and store_snapshot reads POSTGRES. For a tool whose owning store is Neo4j it therefore compares two empty pictures and reports 'STRICTLY IDEMPOTENT — the second call touched nothing at all'.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-IS-BLIND-TO-NEO4J-OW.measured_consequence: It printed exactly that for memory_forget, which re-stamps valid_until on every call. The verdict was not merely unproven — it was the OPPOSITE of the truth, and only a direct Neo4j read found it. The probe's own '⚠ the first call changed nothing either' guard fired, which is the signal that saved it: on a Neo4j-owned tool that warning means the instrument is blind, not that the tool is quiet.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-IS-BLIND-TO-NEO4J-OW.fix_direction: Either extend store_snapshot with a Neo4j axis, or have the probe REFUSE a verdict for tools whose owning store it cannot read — a named refusal beats a confident wrong answer, which is the rule the whole gate is built on.
