D-AN-ENGLISH-ERROR-CARRIED-AN-UNGLOSSED-.what:
Three refusals read 'NOT_A_DERIVATIVE — overrides exist only on a dị bản' (and the archive/spec twins). The sentence is English; 'dị bản' is the product's Vietnamese term for a what-if derivative. A model - and an English-reading author - cannot act on it: it names the precondition in a vocabulary the rest of the message does not use.

The term is KEPT, because it is the platform's own domain word and appears in eleven tool descriptions. What was added is the gloss and the way out: 'a dị bản (a DERIVATIVE Work — create one with composition_create_derivative; composition_derivative_edit only UPDATES an existing one)'.

IT WORKED, MEASURED: with the gloss deployed, all five runs read the refusal and went on to call composition_list_derivatives - a tool none of them had touched before - looking for one.
D-AN-ENGLISH-ERROR-CARRIED-AN-UNGLOSSED-.and_i_got_the_pointer_wrong_first: 🔴 MY FIRST GLOSS NAMED composition_derivative_edit AS THE CREATOR. It is not: it does op=update_spec / archive / restore, 'AFTER derive'. The creator is composition_create_derivative. So I shipped, into an error message, exactly the defect this loop filed against the platform - a refusal naming a tool that cannot do what the sentence says. Caught on the next run's output and corrected in all three strings. The lesson is the one already in the ledger: a pointer in a refusal is load-bearing and must be checked against the catalogue, not written from memory of a name.

D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.status: FIXED 2026-08-24 — all three cases closed and PROVEN AT THE BOUNDARY by scripts/toolloop/override_ship_probe.py against real throwaway books.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.what:
composition_entity_override_edit op=add creates an override for a target_entity_id it never checks. Three cases that should refuse all SUCCEED:

  ABSENT   target_entity_id = a fresh UUIDv4 (no such entity; the platform's own ids are UUIDv7, so it is not even shaped like one of ours) -> {'success': true, 'override': {...}}
  FOREIGN  another BOOK's entity offered to this book's derivative -> succeeds, creating an override that points at an entity from a different book
  EMPTY    overridden_fields = {} -> succeeds, creating an override that overrides nothing

What DOES hold: the canonical project is refused (NOT_A_DERIVATIVE), and a duplicate add is refused with a clear, actionable message ('OVERRIDE_EXISTS - an override for this entity already exists; update it instead').
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.how_bad: Not a cross-USER leak, and that distinction matters: both books in the probe belong to the same owner, so this is referential integrity across BOOKS rather than a tenancy breach. What it produces is override rows whose target does not exist or belongs elsewhere - data that reads as a real override to anything downstream and resolves to nothing. The EMPTY case is the cheapest to argue about and the easiest to fix: an override with no fields is a row that can only confuse.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.why_it_was_invisible_until_today: The tool had never completed a single call in this loop, so its boundary had never been reached. It was blocked first as a SIBLING-WINS failure (my misdiagnosis - the prompt asked for the sibling's scope), then on an undocumented argument shape, then on a missing derivative, then on an ambient project_id that is the wrong Work. Each fix exposed the next layer, and the boundary was the fifth. A tool that cannot be called cannot be audited.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.what_was_fixed_and_why_only_that:
FIXED: overridden_fields={} is now refused with EMPTY_OVERRIDE, and the refusal shows the shape it wants (e.g. {"occupation": "cartographer"}) - which matters, because the previous version of this argument was being sent as a LIST by 4 of 5 runs. Pure local validation, no cross-service call, no failure mode to decide.

🔴 NOT FIXED, AND DELIBERATELY: the ABSENT and FOREIGN cases need an existence check against glossary-service. The only client available is documented at the top of its own module - "every method returns [] / None on any failure and never raises - a glossary outage degrades the pack, it does not 500 a generate." Turning that into a GATE means choosing what happens when glossary is down: reject every override (fail-closed, and writes stop during an unrelated outage) or accept them (fail-open, which is exactly today's bug). That is a product decision about degraded behaviour, not a lint, and this loop has a standing rule that a guard which cannot distinguish "invalid" from "unverified" must say so rather than pick silently.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.theory_2026_08_24_before_the_fix:
🔴 MY OWN DEFERRAL RESTED ON A PREMISE THAT IS FALSE, AND I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN REPEATING IT.

The entry above says the ABSENT and FOREIGN cases 'need an existence check against glossary-service' whose client is 'documented to return [] / None on any failure and never raise', so making it a gate would be a fail-open/fail-closed product decision. The first half of that is quoted from the module docstring and is true of the DEGRADE-SAFE methods. It is not true of the client.

app/clients/glossary_client.py already carries:
  * GlossaryClientError(status, code, detail) - a real exception type;
  * seed_entities_or_raise, whose docstring states the exact principle this case needs: it 'RAISES GlossaryClientError on any non-2xx instead of degrading to []' for a gate 'which must never record a mutation as applied when it actually failed.'

So the codebase has already answered this question for a mutation gate, and did so before I declared it undecidable.

THE SURFACE IS ALSO ALREADY THERE, and it answers BOTH open cases with one call. entities_by_ids(book_id, entity_ids) is a BOOK-SCOPED by-id read returning identity for a known id set. An id that does not exist and an id belonging to ANOTHER book are both simply absent from this book's items - so ABSENT and FOREIGN get the same refusal, which is what H13 wants anyway: no existence oracle for another book's entities.

And work.book_id is in hand at the call site - composition_entity_override_add already passes it to derivatives.add_override.

THE FIX: entities_by_ids_or_raise, mirroring seed_entities_or_raise exactly, then at op=add
    200 and the id is present   -> proceed
    200 and the id is absent    -> refuse (ABSENT and FOREIGN, identically worded)
    raises                      -> refuse with a DISTINCT code saying it could not VERIFY,
                                   naming the outage rather than the argument

THE ONE RESIDUAL CHOICE, stated rather than buried: what to do when glossary is unreachable. I am refusing, and here is the reasoning so it is cheap to reverse. This loop's standing rule is that a guard which cannot distinguish 'invalid' from 'unverified' must SAY SO rather than pick silently - with the raising variant it CAN distinguish, and the third branch says exactly which one it hit. Fail-open is today's bug. It is a WRITE, not a read, so an outage costing an override is recoverable while a bad override is not.

REFUTED IF: entities_by_ids returns [] for an entity that DOES exist in the book (then the check rejects valid overrides and is worse than the bug), or the endpoint is not reachable from the override path's context. Both are tested before the fix is trusted.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.fixed_2026_08_24:
THE PROBE, re-run against the deployed build on two throwaway books torn down in a finally:

    case         before      now
    absent       SUCCEEDED   refused  TARGET_NOT_IN_THIS_BOOK
    tenancy      SUCCEEDED   refused  TARGET_NOT_IN_THIS_BOOK   (identical wording)
    empty        SUCCEEDED   refused  EMPTY_OVERRIDE            (closed 2026-08-23)
    canonical    refused     refused  NOT_A_DERIVATIVE
    idem_first   -           SUCCEEDED  <- THE CONTROL: a real entity still writes
    idem_repeat  -           refused  OVERRIDE_EXISTS

ABSENT AND FOREIGN GET THE SAME WORDS ON PURPOSE. entities_by_ids is book-scoped, so an entity that does not exist and one belonging to another book are alike absent from this book's items. Telling them apart would be an existence oracle for a book the caller may not own, which is the property H13 exists to protect.

THE MECHANISM: `entities_by_ids_or_raise`, mirroring `seed_entities_or_raise` exactly, then at op=add — id present, proceed; id absent, refuse; client raises, refuse with a DISTINCT TARGET_UNVERIFIED that says nothing was written and the argument may be fine. That third branch is why the raising variant is used at all: the degrade-safe `[]` cannot tell 'not there' from 'could not ask', and would have reported an outage as a bad argument.

🔴 WHAT UNBLOCKED THIS WAS CHECKING MY OWN DEFERRAL, NOT NEW INFORMATION. The entry above says these cases were 'an owner decision' because glossary's client 'never raises'. That sentence is quoted from the module docstring and describes its DEGRADE-SAFE methods; the same file already carried GlossaryClientError and seed_entities_or_raise, whose docstring states the principle this case needed — a gate 'which must never record a mutation as applied when it actually failed'. The codebase had answered the question before I called it undecidable, and I had read the docstring instead of the module.

THE ONE CHOICE THAT REMAINS MINE, stated so it is cheap to reverse: refusing when glossary is unreachable. Reasoning — fail-open IS the bug being closed; this is a WRITE, so an outage costing an override is recoverable while a bad override is not; and the standing rule that a guard which cannot distinguish 'invalid' from 'unverified' must SAY SO is satisfied by the separate code rather than by picking silently. If the owner prefers fail-open, the change is one branch.

VERIFIED BEFORE BUILDING ON IT, which was the recorded refutation criterion: against a real throwaway entity, entities_by_ids returned it by id; a fresh UUID returned []; a mixed pair returned 1 of 2. So the check cannot reject a valid override.

12 tests, 11 proven RED first (the twelfth is the bystander that the degrade-safe twin still returns [] — correctly green both ways). Composition suite 3792 passed.

D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.status: OPEN - BLOCKED on DQ-T47. The premise re-derived and CONFIRMED 2026-08-26; the harm is smaller and differently shaped than this row assumed, and one hypothesis of mine was refuted by my own control before it could be shipped.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.what:
propose_edit declares exactly two operations - PROPOSE_EDIT_OPERATIONS = ['insert_at_cursor', 'replace_selection'] - and BOTH are defined in terms of editor state: where the caret is, and what the author has selected.

The turn's context carries neither. chat-service's EditorContext model is book_id, chapter_id and an optional chapter_title. There is no selection, no range, no cursor, and no flag saying whether anything is selected at all. So a model asked to 'make the opening line darker' cannot know whether replace_selection would replace THAT line or something else the author happens to have highlighted - or nothing.

Measured K=5, zero errored runs: the model reads the chapter, finds the real opening line, and offers three rewrites in prose. That is a defensible answer to a request whose affordance it cannot confirm is applicable, and it is the reply the author actually gets.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.why_the_earlier_reading_was_incomplete: 🔴 I FILED THIS AS 'PROSE WINS OVER THE AFFORDANCE', with the note that the competition is the model's own prose rather than another tool. That is what the transcript looks like and it is not the cause. The tool's DESCRIPTION is already as clear as a description can be - 'The edit is shown to the user with an Apply button and is NOT applied automatically - the user reviews it first' - so this is not a case of the model failing to understand the tool. It is a case of the turn not carrying the state the tool operates on.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.what_it_means_for_the_selection_family: It also sharpens the bound recorded on P5. Two tools were used to argue that 'a description can supply a FACT the model lacks and cannot override a PLAN it already has': composition_build_cast_and_graph, where the warning is in the tool's first line and the model still hand-rolls the pipeline, and this one. The second example is now withdrawn from that argument - here the model is not overriding a plan, it is declining an operation it cannot ground. glossary_build still stands on its own.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.recommendation_for_owner: Either EditorContext carries the selection (or at minimum a has_selection flag and the selected text), so the model can tell replace_selection from a guess - or propose_edit gains an operation that names its target explicitly (replace the text 'X', insert after paragraph N) and does not depend on invisible state. NOT MY CALL: the first changes a request contract every FE surface sends, the second changes a tool's operation set.
theory_2026_08_24_the_two_operations_are:
🔴 MY OWN DIAGNOSIS IS HALF WRONG. I wrote that 'its two operations act on editor state the turn does not carry' and treated them as one case. Read from the tool's own schema in services/ai-gateway/src/mcp/propose-edit-tool.ts — source, not catalogue, so this is unaffected by the stale-snapshot retraction:

    required: ['operation', 'text']
    insert_at_cursor  = insert `text` at the user's cursor
    replace_selection = replace the user's currently selected text with `text`

NEITHER takes a selection or a cursor as an ARGUMENT — the client resolves both at Apply time. But they differ in what they PRESUPPOSE:
  * replace_selection presupposes a selection EXISTS. With none, calling it is a guess about what would be replaced, and declining is defensible — which is what the measured runs do.
  * insert_at_cursor presupposes only a cursor, which an editor turn always has, and the model supplies nothing but prose. It is fully groundable from a turn carrying just book_id and chapter_id.

So the blocker is not the TOOL and not the CONTEXT — it is that the measured prompt asks for a REPLACEMENT ('make the opening line of this chapter darker'), which is the half that needs the state the turn lacks.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.theory_refuted_if:
The model still does not call propose_edit when the ask is an INSERTION. Then groundability was never the blocker and the remaining candidate is that prose wins regardless of what is asked — which is the reading I first recorded, then withdrew, and would have to restore with this evidence behind it.

Checked before spending the batch: R1 forces propose_edit ALONE for all three phrasings — the original, 'Add a paragraph here …', and 'Insert at my cursor …' — against the LIVE catalogue. So surfacing is not the variable; the ask is the only thing changing.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.rederived_2026_08_26_the_premise_holds:
Both halves check out against live code, so the row is not stale:
    chat-service models.py EditorContext = book_id, chapter_id, chapter_title|None
    ai-gateway propose-edit-tool.ts  PROPOSE_EDIT_OPERATIONS = ['insert_at_cursor','replace_selection']
No selection, no range, no cursor, no has_selection. The model picks between two state-dependent operations while carrying none of the state.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.what_the_FE_actually_does_measured_not_a:
The two wrong guesses are NOT symmetric, and neither corrupts the manuscript:

  replace_selection with NOTHING selected -> handle.replaceSelection returns false on `if (empty)`, ProposeEditCard toasts 'Select the text to replace, then Apply.', RETURNS before submitToolResult - so the run stays suspended and the user can select and Apply again. The human gate catches it, and the human is exactly who can see the selection.

  insert_at_cursor with text SELECTED -> the prose is inserted at selection.from, i.e. immediately BEFORE the selected span. No error, and no damage: the selected words stay contiguous.

So the platform already degrades defensibly in both directions. What remains is a wasted round trip and a card that can read oddly - a contract question, not a data-loss bug.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.a_hypothesis_of_mine_that_the_control_re:
🔴 I BUILT A FIX FOR A BUG THAT DOES NOT EXIST, AND MY OWN FALSIFIER SOLD IT TO ME. Reading `insertContentAt(selection.from, text)` I concluded the insert lands INSIDE the selected words, and a headless-Tiptap probe seemed to confirm it:
    'The old sentence.' + select 'old sentence' + insert -> 'The XXold sentence.'
I changed the helper to insert at selection.TO, wrote 5 guards that went red on the revert, and the whole frontend suite (851 files / 6386 tests) stayed green.

THE LIVE BROWSER KILLED IT. Driving the real Studio editor with a real triple-click selection, the defective build produced 'INSERTEDPROSEThe old sentence stands here.' - the text at the paragraph START, nothing split. Position 5 is the BOUNDARY before 'old', not a point inside it: from <= to always, so `from` inserts ADJACENT to the selection and never within it. My guard's `not.toContain('XXold')` was asserting ADJACENCY and I read it as SPLITTING. A green-then-red guard proved only that I had changed the behaviour, not that the old behaviour was wrong.

Reverted in full - source and both guards. `to` may well be the nicer semantics (the caret sits at the focus end after a drag), but that is a preference, and shipping a preference as a defect fix is how a ledger fills with changes nobody can justify later.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.what_this_buys_the_owner_decision: THE FE ALREADY HAS THE SELECTION. TiptapEditorHandle.getSelection() returns {from, to, empty, text} and ProposeEditCard already calls it twice (once at mount to snapshot the rewrite for hunk review, once at apply to abort on a moved selection). So option (a) does not need new editor plumbing - only for chat-service's EditorContext to carry what the browser is already reading, additively, exactly the way chapter_title was added ('older FEs simply never send it'). That materially lowers the cost of the option this row assumed was the expensive one.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.what_is_NOT_covered:
- THE POPOUT SURFACE IS A THIRD CASE and is untouched: inside a popped-out Compose window getEditorTarget() is always null, so replace_selection is refused outright with 'Rewrites need to be applied from the docked editor'. Whatever the owner decides about the selection, that surface has no selection to report at all.
- NO K>=5 CHAT BATCH WAS RUN. Nothing was fixed to prove, and measuring how OFTEN the model guesses the wrong operation needs a fixture where a selection genuinely exists - which the harness cannot create, because it drives no editor.
- HOW OFTEN THE WRONG GUESS HAPPENS IS THEREFORE UNMEASURED. The decision below rests on the operations being unguessable in principle, not on an observed rate.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.measured_by: live browser, real Studio editor, throwaway book (E2E insert-selection, trashed): Playwright against a host vite dev server on the working tree, 2026-08-26

D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.status: OPEN - established 2026-08-24 from batch c-planapply3, 4 of 5 runs, zero errored runs.
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.what:
A turn ends telling the author that work is still in progress. It is not: the turn is over, nothing is queued, and no later message will arrive.

    rep 1  'I am working on resolving this now ... I'll let you know as soon as the structure is live.'
    rep 2  'I'm going to attempt to re-establish the connection ... One moment while I fix this.'
    rep 3  'I am going to take a moment to pull the detailed outline ... I'll update you as soon as the chapters are ready'
    rep 4  'I'm going to attempt to re-propose the plan ... One moment.'

Each is a promise of asynchronous continuation from a synchronous turn. The author is left waiting on an update that cannot come, and the store never moved.
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.why_it_is_not_the_same_as_the_defect_tha:
Here it was provoked by plan_bootstrap_apply leaving the wire mid-journey - the model wanted to act, could not, and narrated an intention instead of reporting a failure. But the falsehood does not depend on that cause. ANY turn that ends mid-intention can produce it, and the platform has no guard that reads a reply for a promise it cannot keep.

It is close kin to D-NARRATED-WRITE, which catches a claim that a write HAPPENED. This is the future tense of the same error, and the existing guard does not cover it: 'I have created the chapters' and 'I am creating the chapters, one moment' are both false when the store is unmoved, and only the first is caught.
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.recommendation_for_owner: The detection shape is the same one D-NARRATED-WRITE already uses, extended to the future tense, and it has the same risk: a text-matching guard that fires on a legitimate reply is worse than the defect. NOT WRITTEN, because the honest remedy is probably upstream - a turn that cannot act should say so - and that is a decision about what the assistant may say, which this loop has repeatedly found is not its call. Recorded so the population is countable.

D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.status: FIXED - proven live 2026-08-26, batch c-owedheld3, K=10, zero errored runs, against c-owedheld2 (K=10, same scenario, same fixture) as the baseline.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.what:
When a required argument is declared supplier `context` or `plan`, _missing_args_message emits:

    'plan_bootstrap_apply' is missing ['proposal_id'], and this is NOT yours to invent: the
    runtime supplies it from the current context or an active plan, and has none right now.
    Call plan_bootstrap_propose first, then call this with the id it returns.

Every clause is true of the RUNTIME. None of it is true of the TURN. Measured trail from session 01a03042-07d5-7d8b-b3f9-90484821867f:

    seq 2  plan_bootstrap_propose  ok=true   -> proposal_id 01a03042-1cdc-7637-a75c-fff992d15cc6
    seq 4  plan_bootstrap_apply    ok=false  args={'book_id': ...}   proposal_id OMITTED

The id was in the transcript, returned by a successful tool call two messages earlier. The model dropped it, was told the runtime owns it, and then re-called plan_bootstrap_propose - this time without its own required run_id - and hit a second refusal: 'keeps being called with missing/blank required arguments this turn - STOP.'
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.why_the_wording_is_the_suspect_and_not_t:
🔴 n=3. That is too thin to ship a change to a message every `owed` tool shares, and I am not going to. What makes it worth recording at this size is that the sentence is WRONG IN A DIRECTION: 'NOT yours to invent' is correct and load-bearing - fabricating a UUID is the failure this text exists to prevent - but 'the runtime supplies it ... and has none right now' tells a model holding the value that the value is not its business. The two clauses give opposite instructions to a model that has just been handed the id.

THE FIX SHAPE, unwritten: when the declared emitter has already returned this argument in THIS session, the refusal should say so and quote it, rather than describing where the runtime would otherwise have looked. The tool-call history holds it; the message builder currently takes only (tool, missing, contract, tool_def_props) and cannot see it, so this is plumbing plus a branch, not a reword.

TO JUSTIFY IT: rerun with K high enough to separate 1-in-3 from noise, across more than one `owed` tool. This defect is what that measurement would be for.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.what_was_measured_to_justify_it:
The n=3 above was too thin to ship, and the row said so. It was widened before any code was written, by sweeping loreweave_chat.chat_messages per SESSION rather than per turn:

    of 15 `owed` refusals, 4 (27%) fired while the session had ALREADY been handed that
    exact id - plan_compile.run_id twice, plan_bootstrap_apply.proposal_id twice.

PRECISION, measured before the branch existed: in all four the session held EXACTLY ONE value for the key. Where it holds more than one the branch says nothing, because 'the' id would be a guess - which is the same fabrication this text exists to prevent, pointed the other way.

🔴 A FIRST SWEEP OF THE SAME QUESTION REPORTED ZERO CASES ACROSS 1290 TURNS. It scanned each turn in isolation, and the instance spans two: turn 1 proposes and returns the id, turn 2 says yes and omits it. Per-turn, the refusal reads as correct every time.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.the_fix:
Two parts, and the second is the one that reaches the recorded instance.

1. `_missing_args_message` gained an `owed` branch that quotes the held value and DROPS the runtime-owns-it clause, keeping 'do NOT invent one' and adding 'do not call the supplier again to re-fetch what you were already given' - the second wrong move, which the baseline runs below show the model taking.
2. `db/tool_call_history.ids_returned_under_key` - a cross-turn reader over the SERVER's own record. The call site unions it with the turn's own tool messages and applies one precision guard to the union.

The owed predicate now lives in `_owed_args`, used by both the message and the call site, so the call site can skip a per-argument query for `body` or `items` without keeping a second copy of the rule that is free to drift from the one the message branches on.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.why_part_2_exists_and_it_is_the_whole_le:
🔴 PART 1 SHIPPED ALONE FIRST AND FIRED ZERO TIMES IN TEN LIVE RUNS. Unit tests green, deployed sha verified, in-container check green - and the branch never ran.

It scanned the turn's message list for role='tool' entries. Those exist only WITHIN a turn, appended live and not yet persisted. Across turns there is nothing to find: chat_messages holds ZERO role='tool' rows, because a tool RESULT is stored on the ASSISTANT row in a `tool_calls` JSONB column. Rehydration therefore returns user/assistant text and no results at all.

So the conversation covers THIS turn and the server's record covers the PRIOR ones, and this defect needs the prior one. `tool_call_history` already existed and its own docstring names the question - 'what have I already done?', answered from the SERVER's memory instead of the model's - which is where the reader belongs and where it went.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.proof:
SAME SCENARIO, SAME FIXTURE, SAME K, ONE VARIABLE - whether the cross-turn source is read.

    c-owedheld2  (conversation only)   old wording fired on reps 0, 3, 6
    c-owedheld3  (both sources)        new wording fired on reps 0, 2, 3

WHAT THE MODEL DID NEXT, which is the only thing that matters:

    BASELINE 0/3 recovered.

D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.what:
composition_motif_link_edit's `book_id` is OPTIONAL and silently selects between two incompatible endpoint rules, in MotifRepo.create_link:

    book_id OMITTED   both endpoints must be motifs the caller OWNS
    book_id SUPPLIED  both endpoints must be `book_shared AND book_id = $book`

Measured, on the 2 runs that got past the approval gate: the model resolved both motifs to their REAL seeded ids, passed the correct direction and kind, AND passed the ambient book_id. The seeded motifs are the caller's own, private, and NOT book_shared - so `_in_book()` is false for both endpoints and the repo raises LookupError('both endpoints must be shared motifs in this book').

The tool then discards that sentence: `except LookupError: raise uniform_not_accessible()`. The model is told 'not found or not accessible' about two motifs it had just successfully listed by id. There is no path from that message back to the working call, and both runs stopped.
D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.why_the_model_passed_book_id:
`book_id: str | None = None  # both (shared-tier variant)` is a BARE ANNOTATION with no Field description. The emitted schema is {anyOf: [string, null], default: null, title: 'Book Id'} - nothing about modes.

The comment immediately above it flags this exact class for the two motif ids - 'REQUIRED-IN-PRACTICE IDS WITH NO DESCRIPTION ... a bare annotation gave chat-service nothing to quote' - and those two were fixed. book_id was left bare beside them.

The tool's own description does carry it ('both endpoints must be YOUR own motifs, or pass book_id to link two SHARED motifs of that book'), one clause deep in a dense paragraph, against a standing habit that every composition tool takes the ambient book.
D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.the_fix_and_why_this_one:
TWO CANDIDATES. (a) describe book_id at the argument level. (b) make the REFUSAL actionable.

(b) is load-bearing and (a) is cheap, so both - but the reason (b) has to exist is a bound this loop already measured: a description can supply a FACT the model lacks, and cannot override a PLAN it already has. The model's plan here IS 'pass the ambient book_id', so a description may lose to it. A refusal fires exactly when the plan was wrong.

THE H13 UNIFORM MESSAGE IS NOT WRONG IN GENERAL - it exists so a refusal is not an existence oracle for objects the caller does not own. But in this branch, when the caller OWNS BOTH ENDPOINTS, saying 'these are your own motifs, omit book_id to link them' leaks nothing: they already own them and already hold their ids. So the narrow fix keeps the oracle property exactly and makes only the recoverable case recoverable.
D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.refuted_if: The model still fails after the refusal names the remedy - then the message is not what was missing and the cause is the mode-switch itself, which would want a different tool shape. Or the seeded motifs turn out NOT to be the caller's own, in which case the actionable branch never fires and the uniform message was correct all along.

D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.status: FIXED 2026-08-24 (mechanism shipped + tested); the live re-run is what proves it.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.what:
chat-service's `_inject_context_ids` fills a known session context id when the tool's schema declares it and the model omitted it. It rests on an assumption that is true of almost every tool and not of all of them: that a context id merely SCOPES a call, so supplying one the model forgot can only help.

composition_motif_link_edit breaks it. Its `book_id` selects between two incompatible endpoint rules:
    book_id OMITTED   both endpoints must be motifs the caller OWNS
    book_id SUPPLIED  both endpoints must be `book_shared AND book_id = $book`

So the loop the model was in could not be escaped:
    1  it calls with the ambient book_id     -> refused, its own motifs are not shared there
    2  the refusal says call again WITHOUT book_id   (reached the model 4 of 4 calls)
    3  it calls again WITHOUT book_id        -> THE RUNTIME PUTS IT BACK
    4  same refusal, twice more              -> the repeat-breaker ends the turn

PROVEN DIRECTLY, not inferred from the transcript: calling the deployed `_inject_context_ids` with this tool's real schema and no book_id returns the args WITH book_id filled.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.why_it_took_three_batches_to_see:
Each layer looked like the cause and each was real but downstream. c-motiflink4 said the scenario never granted the Tier-A approval, which was true. c-motiflink5 said the refusal was H13's uniform 'not found or not accessible', which hid an actionable message the repo had already written - also true, and fixing it made the remedy VISIBLE. Only then could the last layer show itself, because until the model was told what to do, nobody could see that doing it changed nothing.

🔴 A REMEDY A REFUSAL NAMES HAS TO BE REACHABLE, OR IT IS WORSE THAN NO REMEDY: it cost the model two extra attempts and then the turn. The first fix was necessary and, alone, would have made the failure look like the model ignoring advice.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.the_fix:
`_meta.mode_selecting_args` — a tool names the arguments whose ABSENCE IS MEANINGFUL, and any consumer that backfills context ids skips them. Added to require_meta in the shared loreweave_mcp kit (validated, additive), declared as ['book_id'] on composition_motif_link_edit, honoured in _inject_context_ids for both directions: never fill one the model omitted, and never correct one it supplied - both are the model's call.

7 tests, 4 proven RED first. Three hold the new behaviour; the rest are the control that every OTHER tool still gets its ids filled, because the measured blocker that function exists for - a mid-tier model cannot reliably transcribe a UUID - has to keep being solved. A malformed declaration falls back to the old behaviour rather than taking the turn down.

🔴 THE DECLARATION TEST PASSED VACUOUSLY AT FIRST. It resolved parents[3] instead of parents[2], looked for a path that does not exist, and returned early on `if not src.exists()` - so it went GREEN against a tree with the declaration removed. A skip-on-missing guard is how a check stops checking; it now asserts the path exists.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.generality: One tool declares this today, and the class is wider: any optional argument whose presence selects a code path rather than a scope. The rule to apply when reading a tool is that an argument the runtime may supply must be one the caller could also have supplied and meant.

D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.status: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-24 by D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-DOMAIN-SELECTION. Its own half is fixed - the refusal names the lookup, and composition_list_derivatives accepts book_id. What remains is that the named tool is withheld from the turn by domain selection and the hot-seed budget.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.what:
composition_entity_override_edit needs the DERIVATIVE Work's project_id. A book's AMBIENT project is its CANONICAL Work - a different Work - so the ambient value is not merely a different scope, it is the wrong object, and the tool refuses it with NOT_A_DERIVATIVE.

_inject_context_ids fills project_id when the model omits it, verified directly against the deployed function: given no project_id it returns the ambient one. So a model that omits the argument INTENDING to look the derivative up first has the canonical id put in its hand before it can.

Measured c-override7, all 5 runs: NOT_A_DERIVATIVE, and in two of them the override call is the FIRST tool call of the turn - before composition_package_tree or composition_list_derivatives - so the model had not yet read any project id from anywhere.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.why_this_is_not_the_recorded_cause:
🔴 THE FIELD IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED, EXPLICITLY, AND IT IS NOT ENOUGH. Since 2026-08-23 project_id carries 'The DERIVATIVE Work's project_id - NOT the book's canonical/ambient project ... get it from composition_list_derivatives, whose entry has is_canonical=false. Passing the ambient project is the common mistake and is refused with NOT_A_DERIVATIVE.' The note recorded then says the tool worked 5/5 after that change; it now fails 5/5 on the same scenario.

That is consistent with the injection being the cause and the description never having been the fix: _inject_context_ids fills only a MISSING argument, so a run where the model happens to supply the derivative id succeeds and a run where it omits one fails. Stochastic, and the earlier 5/5 is then luck rather than evidence.

It is the same shape as D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITCHES-THE-MODE, for a different reason: there, supplying the argument changed the code path; here, the value supplied is the wrong Work.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.the_fix:
The mechanism shipped for the motif case already does this - a tool declares arguments a consumer must NOT fill. The field is being RENAMED from `mode_selecting_args` to `no_context_fill` in the same change, because 'mode selecting' names only the first reason and would misdescribe this one. One declaration, one consumer, one hour old: it will never be cheaper to rename, and a shared-kit field with a misleading name outlives the mistake.

The rule both cases share: AN ARGUMENT THE RUNTIME MAY SUPPLY MUST BE ONE THE CALLER COULD ALSO HAVE SUPPLIED AND MEANT.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.refuted_if: With project_id declared no-fill the model still passes the canonical id. Then it is reading it from context rather than being handed it by the injection, the description is losing to that, and the remedy is elsewhere. This is a clean experiment either way, which is why it is worth running rather than reasoning about.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.attempt_1_failed_2026_08_24:
🔴 DECLARING project_id no_context_fill DID NOT WORK, AND IT BROKE THE CHAIN. Recorded rather than quietly reverted, because the way it failed is the finding.

The experiment ran exactly as designed and its first half CONFIRMED the theory: with the declaration in place the recorded args show pid=NO, so the runtime had indeed been supplying the canonical id, and the tool now ASKS ('op=add requires project_id and target_entity_id') instead of being handed the wrong Work. c-override8, K=5: NOT_A_DERIVATIVE went from 5/5 to 1/5, and one run wrote entity_override - the first override to land in this series.

THE OTHER FOUR GOT WORSE IN A NEW WAY. Starved of any project id, the model put the ONE uuid it held into every slot:

    composition_entity_override_edit  target_entity_id = 01a03106-f55c-...
    composition_list_derivatives      project_id       = 01a03106-f55c-...   <- the entity id
    composition_package_tree          book_id          = 01a03106-f55c-...   <- the entity id
    composition_list_outline          project_id       = 01a03106-f55c-...   <- the entity id
  (the fixture's real book is 01a03106-f312-..., a different id entirely)

Every one refused 'not found or not accessible', and the turn died on the repeat-breaker. The cross-wiring guard D-FJ-20 cannot catch this: it fires only when the model puts ANOTHER OF THE TURN'S CONTEXT IDS in a slot, and an entity id is not one.

WHY THE DECLARATION WAS TOO BLUNT: composition_list_derivatives requires project_id and takes nothing else - 'Pass ANY Work's project_id from the book.' The ambient canonical id is a PERFECTLY GOOD input to it. It is wrong only in the override tool's own slot. Suppressing the fill on that tool removed the model's only exposure to the canonical id, so the very lookup the refusal wanted became impossible.

THE REAL CAUSE, which this attempt uncovered by removing the layer above it: NOT_A_DERIVATIVE names the WRONG REMEDY. It says 'create one with composition_create_derivative' - and the scenario's seed has ALREADY created one. The model is told to make a second derivative when it should be told to FIND the existing one with composition_list_derivatives, which the message never mentions.

That is precisely the second gap P3-NAME-TO-ID's cleared_note names: the arming path fires on MISSING arguments, so a well-formed-but-unusable value passes the breaker, dies at the domain layer, and the domain refusal is on its own - and this one points the wrong way.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.where_it_stands_2026_08_24:
🔴 THREE FIXES, AND THE WRITE RATE DID NOT MOVE: 1 of 5 in c-override8, c-override9 and c-override10 alike. What changed is the FAILURE MODE, each time to a better one:

  c-override7   NOT_A_DERIVATIVE 5/5 - the model is handed the canonical project and stops.
  c-override8   project_id no longer backfilled. The model, starved of any project id, puts the
                target_entity_id into project_id AND book_id on three other tools. WORSE.
                Reverted; recorded as attempt_1_failed.
  c-override9   the refusal now names composition_list_derivatives instead of _create_. The
                model calls it immediately - the message and its arming work - and passes the
                turn's BOOK id, which the runtime recognises as cross-wired and forwards anyway.
  c-override10  that id is now DROPPED, so the tool asks for project_id instead of 404ing. The
                model has nothing to answer with and hits the blank-args breaker.

THE CAUSE THAT REMAINS, named: THE DERIVATIVE'S project_id IS UNOBTAINABLE ON THIS TURN. composition_list_derivatives requires project_id and declares NO other argument ('Pass ANY Work's project_id from the book'), the turn carries no project_id at all, and the model cannot produce one - it has tried the book id, the entity id, and the book's TITLE. Every layer above this is now correct and the chain is still unwalkable.

RECOMMENDED FIX, not shipped: populate context_ids['project_id'] with the book's CANONICAL project. It is derivable server-side from the book, it is exactly what composition_list_derivatives wants, and with it in the ledger the cross-wire correction can SUBSTITUTE rather than merely drop. The override tool would still be handed the canonical id and still refuse - correctly, and now with a refusal that points at the working lookup. NOT DONE THIS CYCLE because it changes what every turn carries, which is wider than one tool and wants its own measurement.

ALTERNATIVE worth pricing first: give composition_list_derivatives a book_id argument. It is a READ that lists a book's Works, and requiring a Work's id to find the book's Works is a chicken -and-egg the model demonstrably cannot solve.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.fix_chosen_2026_08_24_before_the_code:
OF THE TWO REMEDIES PRICED, TAKING THE NARROWER ONE: give composition_list_derivatives a book_id.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT ONE AND NOT MERELY THE SMALLER ONE — read the handler:
    meta = await _book_or_deny(works, tc, _uuid(project_id, 'project_id'), VIEW)
    rows = await works.resolve_by_book(meta.book_id)
It takes a project_id, uses it ONLY to find the book, and then lists BY BOOK. The book id is what the function actually wants; the project_id is a lookup key for it. So requiring a Work's id to enumerate a book's Works is a chicken-and-egg the tool imposes on itself, and the model has demonstrably failed it three ways - passing the book id, the target entity id, and the book's TITLE.

AND book_id IS THE ONE ID THE TURN ALWAYS HAS. context_ids carries it on every turn; project_id only on studio/editor turns. So _inject_context_ids fills it with no further change, and the cross-wire correction gains something to substitute rather than only something to drop.

THE OTHER REMEDY - populating context_ids['project_id'] with the book's canonical project - is left unshipped. It would work, and it changes what EVERY turn carries to fix one tool's lookup, which is a wider blast radius for a narrower gain. Recorded so the owner can still prefer it.

SHAPE: project_id and book_id both optional, EXACTLY ONE required. book_id gates on the book directly (VIEW); project_id keeps the existing resolve-then-gate path byte-for-byte, so no current caller changes behaviour. Neither supplied is a refusal that names both.

REFUTED IF: with book_id accepted and auto-filled the model still cannot complete the chain - then the blocker is not the lookup's signature and the remaining candidate is that the model cannot carry the derivative's project_id from the list into the retry, which is a different problem and would want the id-ledger rather than an argument.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.fix_result_2026_08_24:
composition_list_derivatives NOW ACCEPTS book_id (exactly one of book_id | project_id; the project_id path unchanged byte-for-byte; 6 tests, 5 proven RED). Verified deployed and federated - a no-args call over MCP returns the new 'give EXACTLY ONE' refusal.

AND THE TOOL DID NOT MOVE. c-override11, K=5, zero errored runs: override rows written 0 of 5, against 1 of 5 in each of the three batches before it. At n=5 that difference is noise and I am not claiming a regression from it - what IS visible in the trace is that the model stopped calling composition_list_derivatives at all this time and went to composition_list_outline instead, where the drop then starved it.

SO THE CHAIN IS NOW WALKABLE AND THE MODEL IS NOT WALKING IT. Four fixes deep, each proven RED-first and suite-green, and the write rate is 0-1 of 5 throughout. The refutation criterion recorded before this fix has been met: 'with book_id accepted and auto-filled the model still cannot complete the chain - then the blocker is not the lookup's signature.' It is not the signature.

WHAT THAT LEAVES, stated as the next cycle's starting point rather than as a conclusion: the remaining candidate named in that same criterion is that the model cannot carry the derivative's project_id from the list INTO the retry. That is an id-ledger question, not an argument-shape one, and it wants its own measurement - starting from whether composition_list_derivatives is even advertised on the pass where the model gives up.

D-A-CROSSWIRED-ID-IS-DETECTED-AND-SENT-A.status: FIXED 2026-08-24 (mechanism shipped + 9 tests, 1 proven RED); it did NOT move the tool it was found under, and that is recorded below rather than glossed.
D-A-CROSSWIRED-ID-IS-DETECTED-AND-SENT-A.what:
_inject_context_ids corrects an argument when the model puts one of the turn's own ids in another id's slot. The correction sat behind `if not val or key not in props: continue` - so when the turn had NO id of that kind to substitute, the whole key was skipped, INCLUDING the detection.

Measured c-override9, K=5: the turn carries no project_id (it is populated only on studio/editor turns), the model sent composition_list_derivatives{project_id: <this turn's BOOK id>}, and `is_crosswired('project_id', book_id)` returns True - checked directly against the deployed function. The runtime KNEW the id was the wrong kind, had nothing to put in its place, and forwarded it anyway. The model got back 'not found or not accessible', retried the same call twice, and died on the repeat-breaker.

FIXED by dropping it: the runtime must not SEND an argument it knows is wrong. The tool's own missing-argument refusal then fires, which names the declared supplier and arms it. The evidence standard is unchanged and high - `is_crosswired` is true only for an id THIS TURN published under a DIFFERENT name, the same standard the existing branch already treats as sufficient to OVERWRITE a value.
D-A-CROSSWIRED-ID-IS-DETECTED-AND-SENT-A.known_gap: A NON-UUID is still forwarded when there is no substitute. The branch above it replaces a mistranscribed value with the turn's known id, but that needs a value to use; with none, my new branch requires is_crosswired, which matches only UUIDs. Measured in the same batch: one run sent the BOOK'S TITLE as project_id ('LOOP-THROWAWAY-composition-entity-override-edit-...') and it went out. A project_id that is not a UUID is knowably wrong without any ledger, so this is closable; it is recorded rather than fixed because it was found after the change was tested and deserves its own falsifier.
D-A-CROSSWIRED-ID-IS-DETECTED-AND-SENT-A.narrowed_after_its_own_side_effect_2026_:
🔴 THE FIX HAD A SIDE EFFECT AND THE RUN THAT PROVED IT WAS THE ONE MEANT TO TEST SOMETHING ELSE. Batch c-override11: composition_list_outline had its cross-wired project_id dropped, declares NO emitter for it, and so was refused 'missing required argument(s)' with nowhere named to go. The model blank-retried into 'keeps being called with missing/blank required arguments' — a WORSE failure than the opaque 404 the drop replaced.

The justification for dropping was always that the refusal which follows NAMES A SUPPLIER and arms it. Where no emitter is declared that justification simply is not there, so the drop is now conditional on one existing. Checked against the live contract: composition_entity_override_edit declares project_id <- composition_list_derivatives (drop applies); composition_list_outline declares nothing (forward as before). Both are asserted in the tests so the premise cannot rot silently.

WORTH KEEPING AS A PATTERN: a guard that makes a failure LOUDER is not automatically an improvement. It is an improvement only where the louder failure carries somewhere to go.

D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.status: FIXED (mechanism shipped + 12 tests, 2 proven RED on the CONDITION) and its EFFECT IS UNDEMONSTRATED — c-override13 is 0 of 5 and the arming log line never appeared. A deeper cause was found underneath it; see below.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.what:
Arming - putting a tool the refusal NAMES onto the wire so the model can obey - happens at exactly ONE site in stream_service: inside the MISSING-REQUIRED-ARGUMENTS interception. `_tools_named_in_refusal` is defined once and called once, there.

A tool that DISPATCHES SUCCESSFULLY and reports its refusal in the RESULT BODY - the {'success': False, 'error': ...} shape used all over composition-service - never reaches that site. Its message can name any tool it likes and nothing is armed.

MEASURED, from chat_messages.advertised_tools over the five runs of c-override12:
    composition_entity_override_edit  advertised 5 of 5
    composition_list_derivatives      advertised 0 of 5   <- the tool its refusal names
The model was told 'Call composition_list_derivatives and pass it THIS SAME project_id' on every run, and the tool was on the wire on none of them. It called composition_list_canon_rules, composition_list_outline and composition_package_tree instead - the composition reads it COULD see - and every one refused.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.it_was_predicted_and_then_measured:
This is gap 2 of P3-NAME-TO-ID's cleared_note, written earlier the same day: 'the arming path fires on MISSING arguments. A model that supplies a well-formed but unusable value passes the breaker entirely and fails at the domain layer, where no supplier is named and none is armed.' That was reasoning from the code; this is the number.

It also explains why five separate fixes to composition_entity_override_edit moved the failure mode every time and never the outcome. Each one made the refusal MORE correct - name the lookup, not the create; drop the id you know is wrong; accept the book_id the model actually has - while the tool being named stayed invisible. A better instruction to walk through a door that is not there.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.why_not_fixed_here:
Arming on dispatch results changes what every refusing tool on the platform can put on the wire, mid-turn, across every provider. That is a surface-budget question (the hot seed is capped) and a safety question (a refusal is model-visible text, and `_tools_named_in_refusal` already restricts to catalogue names for exactly that reason). It deserves its own cycle, its own falsifier and its own K=5 - not a sixth change appended to this one.

RECOMMENDATION: run the same arming the missing-args branch does, on a dispatch result whose body reports failure, with the same catalogue-name restriction. The measurement that would prove it is already built: advertised_tools per turn, which is how this was found.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.correction_2026_08_24:
🔴 I WROTE 'ARMING HAPPENS AT EXACTLY ONE SITE' AND THAT IS FALSE. There are TWO: the missing-required-arguments interception, and D-FJ-4 on the dispatch result. I found the second only because a test I had written to assert the overstatement PASSED against the unfixed tree - the count was never the defect.

The cause of the error is worth keeping: I grepped `_tools_named_in_refusal` with `head -5`, saw the definition, two comment mentions and the missing-args call, and stopped reading. The third call was on line 7376, past the cut. A truncated search that answers the question you asked is the most convincing way to be wrong.

THE SUBSTANTIVE FINDING SURVIVES AND IS NARROWER THAN THE OVERSTATEMENT. D-FJ-4 was gated on `if not ok`, and `ok` is the ENVELOPE's status - the CALL succeeded, the body says the request did not. So NEITHER site fired for a refusal reported in the result body, which is the {'success': False, 'error': ...} shape composition-service uses throughout. The measurement is unchanged: composition_list_derivatives advertised 0 of 5 while the tool naming it was advertised 5 of 5.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.fixed_2026_08_24:
FIXED at the EXISTING D-FJ-4 site rather than a new one. It now computes a refusal text from either an envelope error or an explicit body-level `success is False`, and arms off that.

My first attempt added a THIRD site beside it. That was wrong twice over: it duplicated the envelope case, and it armed SILENTLY - without the '[SYSTEM] … is now available to you on this turn' note that D-FJ-4 appends, which is the part that actually tells the model the tool is callable. Arming a tool the model is never told about is a mechanism with no reader. Removed; a test now asserts there are exactly two homes and that the note is present.

ONLY AN EXPLICIT `success is False` COUNTS. Most read tools never set the key, and treating a missing `success` as failure would scan every ordinary result for tool names - asserted as a control, along with non-dict payloads and a genuine success.

The two safety properties are inherited unchanged from the helper, not restated: `_tools_named_in_refusal` matches only CATALOGUE names with whole-word matching (a refusal is model-visible text), and `_arm_tools` respects `context_length`. That is why this is the same guard applied to the same class of message rather than a new policy - which is also why the 'wide blast radius' I used to defer it did not survive reading the code, exactly as the glossary deferral did not.

12 tests, 2 proven RED on the CONDITION (an earlier version asserted the site COUNT and passed against the unfixed tree - a test that cannot fail is a test that is not testing).

D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.three_diagnostic_runs_did_not_close_it_2:
🔴 I RAN THREE TARGETED DIAGNOSTIC CYCLES AND THE LAST HOP IS STILL OPEN. Recording that as a stop rather than continuing to spend build-deploy-run cycles on it.

WHAT THE DIAGNOSTIC PROVED (it is permanent observability now, not scaffolding):

And for those, arming nothing is CORRECT: the refusal names only the tool that refused, which `exclude` removes.

WHAT IT DID NOT EXPLAIN: composition_entity_override_edit refused with NOT_A_DERIVATIVE in SIX sessions across the three runs - recorded ok=false, source=tool, the text present in chat_messages.tool_calls - and produced NO line from ANY of the three diagnostic branches. THAT IS A HYPOTHESIS AND I AM LABELLING IT ONE. The measurement says where it is NOT; it does not say where it is. The next reader should start by finding every path a tool result can take between mcp_execute_tool and `working.append`, not by re-running the batch.

WHAT THIS COST, worth recording as a pattern: three cycles of build + deploy + K=1..2 run, each ~15 minutes, to learn where the code is not. A single log line at the TOP of the dispatch step - 'result for %s: ok=%s payload=%s' - would have answered it in one. D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.ANSWERED_2026_08_24_BY_READING_NOT_RUNNI:
THE MISSING LOG LINE IS EXPLAINED, and it cost nothing to find once I did what I had written down: enumerate the paths a tool result can take, instead of running the batch again.

THERE ARE FOUR mcp_execute_tool CALL SITES. Two are in the main loop (7126 and its helpers). TWO ARE IN `resume_stream_response` - 11067 and 11198 - and that second one is where an APPROVED Tier-A tool actually executes.

The resume dispatch is a far thinner path:
    _ok = bool(envelope.get('success'))
    _tool_payload = envelope.get('result') if _ok else {'error': envelope.get('error')}
    working.append({...})
    _chunk = {..., 'ok': _ok, 'error': envelope.get('error')}
    instrument.stamp_tool_call(_chunk, source=instrument.SOURCE_TOOL, ...)
No arming. No cross-wire correction. No repeat-breaker. That `_chunk` is exactly where the chat_messages.tool_calls record's `ok=false, source=tool` and the NOT_A_DERIVATIVE text come from - so the evidence I kept re-reading was written by the very path that has no arming.

AND IT EXPLAINS THE SPLIT IN THE DIAGNOSTIC PERFECTLY. Every tool that DID log is Tier R - composition_list_outline, composition_list_canon_rules - and runs in the main loop. composition_entity_override_edit is Tier A: it suspends for approval and executes on resume. I instrumented the main loop and measured a tool that never goes through it.

🔴 THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THIS SESSION THE RESUME PATH HAS BEEN THE ANSWER. Earlier: 'R1 answerability was inert on every resumed turn' because _emit_chat_turn was called without request_text. The general fact is worth more than either instance: THE RESUME PATH IS SYSTEMATICALLY MISSING THE MAIN LOOP'S GUARDS, and every guard added to the main loop should be asked of it.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.fix_shape_not_shipped:
Arming at the resume dispatch is necessary and NOT sufficient, and the reason is in the code's own comments. After dispatching, resume re-enters _stream_with_tools and RE-DERIVES ITS SURFACE FROM SCRATCH - 'a resume re-derives its surface from scratch (WS-3)'. `susp.pinned_step_tools` exists precisely to carry an exemption across that boundary, 'because dropping the exemption here would strand a rail at its FIRST confirm gate'.

So the shape is: resolve the tools named in the resumed tool's refusal, and carry them across the re-derivation the way pinned_step_tools already carries a rail's steps.

BUT THE MEASURED WITHHOLDING IS domain_not_selected AND hot_seed, and filter_intent_gated_setup_tools - where pinned_step_tools is applied - is the INTENT GATE, a different filter. Pinning there may exempt the wrong one. Which of the three filters must honour a refusal-named tool is the question to answer BEFORE writing this, and answering it means reading the surface builder, not running another batch.

NOT SHIPPED. It is a change to how a resumed turn chooses its surface, and I have already learned this cycle what happens when I change surface selection on a hunch: c-override8, where suppressing one backfill starved the model of the only id it had.

D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.status: OPEN - found 2026-08-24 from chat_messages.withheld_tools, 5 of 5 turns.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.what:
composition_entity_override_edit's refusal names composition_list_derivatives. That tool is WITHHELD from the turn for two independent reasons, recorded by the platform itself:

    domain_not_selected | domain not in this turn's hot set (book, glossary, knowledge, story)
    hot_seed            | did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)

Five of five turns, both reasons. The turn's hot set does not include composition's divergence domain at all, and even if it did the tool did not fit the seed budget.

So the instruction 'Call composition_list_derivatives' is issued into a turn that selected a different set of domains entirely. Arming exists to rescue exactly this - but arming is a mid-turn correction layered on top of a selection made at turn start, and the measurement says the rescue did not happen.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.why_it_matters_beyond_this_tool: It is P1-SURFACE's invariant reaching a case R1 cannot cover. `answerable_tools` forces a tool onto the wire when the AUTHOR'S REQUEST matches its declared synonyms. Here the tool is needed because of a REFUSAL - the platform's own words, mid-turn - and no author phrasing would ever have named it. A surface chosen from the request cannot anticipate the tools the request's failure will require.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.recommendation_for_owner:
Two shapes, both wider than one tool. (a) Treat a tool named in a refusal as budget-exempt for the remainder of the turn, the way D-RAIL-NEXT-STEP-EXEMPT already treats a rail's next step - the precedent exists and is narrow. (b) Let a declared emitter pull its consumer's domain into the hot set: composition_entity_override_edit already declares project_id <- composition_list_derivatives, so the platform knows the pair before the turn starts.

(b) is the one I would price first: it acts at SELECTION time rather than patching the selection afterwards, and it uses a declaration that already exists and is already verified.

D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.status: OPEN - BLOCKED on DQ-T41, which is what this row has always been: a recommendation for a decision, not work. Re-derived 2026-08-26 and the measurement holds; the tie POPULATION is now measured too, and it is four times smaller than the raw count suggests.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.what:
composition_generate's blocked reason calls this a genuine tie — 'R1 is deliberately not a ranking, so when several tools declare the same words they all arrive and the choice falls back to the model.' Measured, the tie is MANUFACTURED by the matcher, twice over.

1. NORMALISATION COLLAPSES DISTINCT DECLARATIONS. `_answer_norm` strips articles, so three tools that declared DIFFERENT phrases become identical:
       composition_generate      'write chapter'      -> 'write chapter'   len 13
       book_chapter_create       'write a chapter'    -> 'write chapter'   len 13
       book_chapter_save_draft   'write the chapter'  -> 'write chapter'   len 13
   The article is load-bearing and the authors used it that way: 'write A chapter' is the CREATE tool, 'write THE chapter' is the edit-existing tool. Stripping it destroys the distinction they encoded, and manufactures an exact three-way tie at length 13.

2. THE LOOP BREAKS ON THE FIRST MATCH, SO THE DISCRIMINATING TERM IS DISCARDED. composition_generate declares NINE synonyms and the request matches TWO of them:
       index 2  'write chapter'   matched by 3 tools in the catalogue
       index 5  'cowrite'         matched by EXACTLY 1 tool in 315   <- never reaches the ranker
   `for syn in synonyms: ... break` stops at index 2. So a tool's contribution is whichever synonym happens to sit earliest in its list — declaration ORDER decides the match, which no author would expect to matter — and the one term that identifies this tool uniquely, in a prompt that says 'with the cowrite engine' outright, is thrown away before ranking begins.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.recommendation_for_DQ_T41:
DQ-T41 asks what precedence should break an exact tie. On this evidence the more useful question is why the ranker is being handed a tie at all.

RANK BY SPECIFICITY, NOT LENGTH. The current key is `-len(normalised_synonym)`, and length is a poor proxy for how much a phrase identifies a tool: 'cowrite' (7 chars) is matched by 1 tool in 315; 'write chapter' (13 chars) by 3. A count of how many catalogue tools match the same normalised synonym is computable from the catalogue at the same moment, needs no new declaration, and is exactly the signal a tie-break wants.

It resolves the other recorded instances the same way and without a domain-vs-generic rule: jobs_cancel's 'stop the translation' would still tie translation_job_control on length and lose on specificity, because the domain tool's vocabulary is matched by fewer tools. A precedence rule stated as 'longer synonym wins' resolves NEITHER instance, since both are exact ties.

PREREQUISITE, and it is small: collect a tool's BEST matching synonym rather than its first. As written the ranker cannot see 'cowrite' at all, so no tie-break — length, specificity or otherwise — can use it.

NOT SHIPPED. This is a change to how EVERY request selects its surface, and it is DQ-T41's own question. The measurement is the contribution; the decision is the owner's.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.what_it_does_not_explain: It does not explain why the model then picks book_chapter_save_draft over the others once all five are on the wire — that is a choice among tools it can see, and this loop's rule is that a surface finding does not become a model finding without its own measurement. What is now known is that the surface handed the model a tie it did not have to.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.rederived_2026_08_26:
The collapse is exactly as recorded, run against the deployed matcher:
    'write chapter'      -> 'write chapter'   len 13
    'write a chapter'    -> 'write chapter'   len 13
    'write the chapter'  -> 'write chapter'   len 13
    'cowrite'            -> 'cowrite'         len  7
Three distinct author-written phrases become one key, and the 7-char phrase that identifies ONE tool loses a `-len` ranking to the 13-char phrase that identifies three.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.the_tie_population_measured_and_it_is_25:
The row argues about tie-breaking without ever saying how many ties there are. Censused over all 1,472 declared synonyms on the live 316-tool catalogue, normalised through the shipped `_answer_norm`:

    1,353 distinct normalised synonyms
       97 shared by more than one tool          <- the raw tie population
       25 shared by more than one LIVE tool     <- what the model actually faces
       72 dissolve because one side is LEGACY   <- dropped from every turn since 2026-08-25

So three quarters of the apparent ties are with tools the model can never see. That matters for DQ-T41's cost side: the decision governs 25 phrases, not 97, and the ones that remain are concentrated in the book/composition overlap:
    'write chapter'     book_chapter_create · book_chapter_save_draft · composition_generate
    'table contents'    book_list · book_list_chapters · book_structure_read
    'read scene'        book_read · book_scene_get · composition_get_outline_node
    'reorder chapters'  book_chapter_reorder · book_structure_edit
    'draft scene'       book_chapter_save_draft · composition_generate

The row's own instance is in the surviving set, so it is a real tie and not an artefact.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.what_is_NOT_covered:
- MY LEGACY EXCLUSION IS PYTHON-ONLY. 68 legacy tools were read from Python registrations; the Go services (book, glossary, catalog, agent-registry, provider-registry) were not scanned, and several of the 25 survivors are book_* tools which live in Go. So 25 is an UPPER bound on the live tie population — the true figure is that or lower.
- THE SPECIFICITY PROPOSAL IS STILL UNTESTED. Ranking by how many catalogue tools share a normalised synonym is computable and would resolve the recorded instances on paper. Nothing was measured: no batch was run with it, and after two description changes measured WORSE today, a matcher-ranking change is exactly the kind of thing this loop should not ship on reasoning alone.
- THE NORMALISATION ITSELF IS UNTOUCHED. `_answer_norm` stripping articles is what manufactures the collapse, and the authors used the article deliberately ('write A chapter' vs 'write THE chapter'). Changing it would alter matching across all 1,472 declarations, which is a far wider blast radius than a tie-break rule and is not what DQ-T41 asks about.
- IT STILL DOES NOT EXPLAIN THE MODEL'S CHOICE once all the tied tools are on the wire. That remains a model finding without its own measurement, exactly as the row says.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.measured_by: _answer_norm exercised directly against the deployed chat-service, 2026-08-26; synonym census over the live 316-tool federated catalogue (1,472 declarations); legacy set read from the Python MCP registrations

D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-24. The strongest instance of P5 arm (b) in the loop, and the remedies are owner decisions.
D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.what:
composition_build_cast_and_graph runs a whole pipeline — its first line says so: 'You do NOT pick per-entity tools: this ONE tool runs the whole pipeline — it plans WHAT to build (a worklist), builds each entity in its own focused step, files them as review drafts, then projects them into the graph and proposes their relationships.'

The model runs glossary_extract_entities_from_doc -> glossary_propose_entities instead, on 5 of 5 runs, and SUCCEEDS at the surface goal: glossary_entities moves 5/5. What the author loses is not the cast — they get that — but the worklist, the deep profiles, the review drafts and the proposed relationships.

🔴 AND THE ANSWERABILITY LAYER IS DOING EVERYTHING IT CAN. Measured against the deployed matcher and the live catalogue for this exact prompt:
       R1 forces: ['composition_build_cast_and_graph']   — EXACTLY ONE TOOL, via 'build the knowledge graph' (21 chars)
   Neither competitor declares anything that matches the request: glossary_extract_entities_from_doc's vocabulary is all 'extract entities from a document' / 'parse my notes', and glossary_propose_entities' is all 'create a new entity' / 'bulk create entities'. They are on the wire because the GLOSSARY DOMAIN is in the hot set, not because anything decided they answer this request.

So this is not a tie, not a ranking problem, and not a surfacing problem. The platform favours the right tool as strongly as its design permits — sole forced tool — and the model chooses the parts it can also see.
D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.it_corrects_the_recorded_numbers: 🔴 The blocked reason on file says 'answerable_tools ranks this tool FIRST for its own prompt (synonym length 23, against kg_build 21)'. Measured now: the match is 21 characters, not 23, and kg_build is NOT in the answerable set at all — the set has exactly one member. The old numbers made this look like a near-run ranking; it is not close, and that makes the finding STRONGER rather than weaker.
D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.why_the_obvious_remedies_are_not_mine:
SUPPRESS THE PARTS. They arrive by domain seeding, and the glossary domain is correctly hot for a glossary request. Removing them would break every job that legitimately needs one entity created — the tools are not wrong, they are wrong FOR THIS REQUEST, and nothing on the surface knows which request it is looking at.

GIVE IT A WORKFLOW. The platform already has the mechanism and states it in the system prompt: 'If the user's request matches one of these, call workflow_load FIRST and follow its steps IN ORDER — do NOT improvise your own tool sequence for a job a workflow already covers.' That is this failure named exactly. But no workflow covers this job: `glossary-bootstrap` is ONTOLOGY setup ('Set up a book's world categories' — list standards, adopt, confirm, read back), not entity building. Checked in loreweave_agent_registry.workflows rather than assumed.

So when no workflow matches, the directive PERMITS improvising — and the model did exactly what the platform allows. Authoring a workflow changes what every user sees in workflow_list, which is a product surface, not a lint.

RECOMMENDATION, in order of what I would price first: (1) a one-step workflow whose step IS composition_build_cast_and_graph, because the rail mechanism already exists and is designed for precisely 'a job a workflow already covers'; (2) nothing else — a description warning is already there, in the tool's FIRST LINE, and did not prevent it on 5 of 5 runs, which is the bound this loop has now measured twice.

D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.what:
`answerable_tools` ranks over the FEDERATED catalogue. Consumer-local meta tools are advertised alongside federated ones but are not in it — `_CONSUMER_LOCAL_META_TOOLS` in stream_service holds find_tools, tool_list, tool_load, workflow_list, workflow_load and run_subagent, each with its own tool def built in chat-service rather than fetched from the gateway.

So R1 cannot see them. It cannot rank one, cannot deprioritise one, and cannot know that one DUPLICATES a federated tool it is busy forcing onto the wire. A consumer-local tool that overlaps a federated one wins unconditionally.

MEASURED, for 'What workflows are available to me?' against the deployed matcher and the live catalogue:
       R1 forces: ['registry_list_workflows']      <- the SOLE forced tool
       workflow_list:  NOT IN THE FEDERATED CATALOGUE
and the model calls workflow_list on 5 of 5 runs. Both return count=12 with identical slugs, so the author is answered correctly — which is why this cost nothing visible and stayed invisible.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.it_corrects_the_recorded_reason: 🔴 The blocked reason says workflow_list is 'in the ALWAYS-ON CORE'. It is not: ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES, read from the deployed service, is exactly (tool_list, tool_load, confirm_action, web_search). workflow_list is advertised by a different route — its def lives in workflow_runner.WORKFLOW_LIST_TOOL and it is dispatched inside stream_service. The CONCLUSION was right (it is always reachable and R1 cannot outrank it) and the mechanism named was wrong, which matters because the fix differs: nothing about ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES would change this.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.recommendation_for_owner:
TWO LEVELS, and I would price the first.

1. THIS TOOL. registry_list_workflows declares no `superseded_by` — the inverse of DQ-T2's complaint about 55 tools that declare deprecation and name no successor. Here is a tool superseded IN PRACTICE that says nothing. Marking it `visibility='legacy', superseded_by='workflow_list'` is the mechanism the kit already provides, and it would remove it from discovery on both federation surfaces. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE, which is why it is the owner's: a legacy tool is excluded from the agent's discoverable set, so it can never again be PROVEN by a live run — the honest outcome is that it leaves the denominator as deprecated rather than sitting blocked forever.

2. THE CLASS. `answerable_tools` should rank over the tools actually ADVERTISED, not only the federated catalogue, or its ranking stays blind to every consumer-local competitor. That is a change to the matcher's input rather than its rules, and it would let R1 at least SEE the duplication it is currently ranking against.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.the_mechanism_re_verified_2026_08_26:
Still true, read from the deployed source:
    _answerable = answerable_tools(request_text, list(catalog_index.values()))
`catalog_index` is the FEDERATED index; the consumer-local defs (WORKFLOW_LIST_TOOL, WORKFLOW_LOAD_TOOL, LOAD_SKILL_TOOL, …) are `_add`ed to the OUTPUT list and never enter it. So R1 cannot rank, deprioritise or even see them.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE ROW'S OWN SET: it lists six consumer-local tools as invisible to R1. Checked against the live 313-tool catalogue, `tool_list` and `tool_load` ARE federated (the public MCP gateway publishes them), so R1 can see those two. The genuinely invisible set is find_tools (retired, DIS-3), workflow_list, workflow_load and run_subagent — and of those only the workflow pair has a federated twin at all. The class is two pairs wide, not six.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.the_harm_is_REFUTED_on_both_pairs:
🔴 THE ROW SAYS 'a consumer-local tool that overlaps a federated one wins unconditionally'. Measured on both overlaps, it does not:

  LIST PAIR — workflow_list vs registry_list_workflows. Batch c-regwf6, K=20, the shipped state: the FEDERATED tool answered 20 of 20 and workflow_list 0 of 20, with 0/20 wrong answers. The row's 5-of-5 measurement was taken on 2026-08-24, BEFORE workflow_list's payload claim was corrected; that correction moved the model off it entirely.

  LOAD PAIR — workflow_load vs registry_get_workflow. Batches c-wfload1 and c-wfload2, K=5 each, asking for one workflow's steps. NEITHER tool was called, 0 of 10 — the workflow was bound to the turn, so its rail already carried the step list. The answer was CORRECT: the reply named 'see-rules, list-chapters, read-a-chapter', which is verbatim the registry's own steps for canon-check, and the model then called those three steps' tools.

So on one pair the federated tool wins outright, and on the other neither is reached because the information arrives by a third route. The blindness costs nothing that can be measured today.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.the_recommendation_is_RETRACTED_and_woul:
Level 1 recommended marking registry_list_workflows `visibility='legacy', superseded_by='workflow_list'` — retiring the FEDERATED tool in favour of the consumer-local one, on the evidence that the model always chose the local one.

That evidence is now inverted. registry_list_workflows answers 20 of 20 and answers CORRECTLY, while workflow_list — invited to self-filter — was measured naming non-studio workflows on 4 of 5 and dropping real ones on 4 of 5. Marking it legacy would have dropped it from every turn catalogue (the 2026-08-25 widening drops EVERY legacy tool) and left the surface with only the tool that gets the answer wrong.

This is the second recommendation in this loop that a later measurement reversed. Both were written from a single K=5 batch, and both looked obvious.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.what_is_NOT_covered:
- LEVEL 2 IS NOT DONE AND IS NOT RECOMMENDED BLIND. Passing the advertised set into answerable_tools instead of the federated catalogue is a small change to the matcher's INPUT, and it buys nothing measurable today: R1 has no de-duplication rule, so SEEING a consumer-local competitor would not change what it forces. Making an unmeasured change to the surface-selection layer to fix a harm that no longer reproduces is the move this loop keeps catching itself in.
- THE BLINDNESS IS STILL THE RIGHT THING TO REMEMBER. If a consumer-local tool is ever added that overlaps a federated one AND is better at the ask, R1 cannot express that, and nothing warns anybody. That is why this row is withdrawn rather than deleted.
- run_subagent HAS NO TWIN and was not examined; find_tools is retired (DIS-3) and its presence in _CONSUMER_LOCAL_META_TOOLS was not checked for staleness.
- MY FIRST PROBE CHOSE ITS OWN ANSWER. c-wfload1 asked 'What are the steps of the canon-check workflow?' and the model matched the WORDS and answered from composition_list_canon_rules — every workflow slug names a domain, so the slug collided with a domain tool's vocabulary. c-wfload2 disambiguated the ASK without naming a tool and got the same tool choice with a correct answer, which is what separates 'my prompt collided' from 'the workflow tools are unreachable'. Without that control I would have reported a tool-selection defect that was mine.
