D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-24 across THREE tools. The clearest statement of P5 arm (b) the loop has, and it bounds what answerability can ever fix.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.what:
`answerable_tools` forces a tool onto the wire when the request matches its declared vocabulary. It is ADDITIVE by design — 'deliberately not a ranking' — so it can put the right tool in front of the model and cannot take a wrong one away. The competitors arrive by DOMAIN SEEDING, which answerability never consults.

MEASURED ON THREE TOOLS, each time with R1 forcing the correct tool as the SOLE member of the answerable set:

  composition_build_cast_and_graph   forced alone via 'build the knowledge graph' (21).
      Model ran glossary_extract_entities_from_doc -> glossary_propose_entities, 5/5.
      Neither competitor declares anything matching the request.
  registry_list_workflows      forced alone. Its twin workflow_list is CONSUMER-LOCAL and not
      in the federated catalogue at all, so R1 cannot even see it. Model used the twin 5/5.
  translation_job_control      forced alone via 'stop translation' (16) on the domain
      question. Model called jobs_cancel + jobs_summary, 5/5, and called the tool under test
      ZERO times.

So the answerability layer is doing everything its design permits in all three, and losing in all three. The failure is not that the right tool is missing — it is present, forced, and alone in the set — but that the wrong ones are equally present and more familiar.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.the_attempt_that_failed:
🔴 I REWORDED translation_job_control's PROMPT TO ITS OWN DOMAIN QUESTION AND IT DID NOT WORK. Recorded because the reasoning was sound and the result refutes it.

The scenario read 'Cancel job — stop translation for this book's running translation job.' Measured, that phrasing makes the tool match BOTH 'cancel job' (10) and 'stop translation' (16), and the matcher BREAKS on the first hit — so it contributed 10 and tied jobs_cancel exactly, while its longer exclusive match was discarded. The prompt front-loaded the generic tie-maker.

'Stop the translation for this book.' forces translation_job_control ALONE — jobs_cancel matches nothing. Batch c-tjc3, K=5, zero errored runs:
        surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, suspended 3/5
        every run: jobs_cancel + jobs_summary
and jobs_cancel then failed on 'missing required argument(s): [job_id]' — the model could not even complete the tool it preferred.

THE HYPOTHESIS WAS THAT AN UNAMBIGUOUS ANSWERABLE SET WOULD DECIDE THE CHOICE. It does not. The precedent I was following — settings_provider_inventory, where asking only the tool's own question moved it from 0/5 to 4/5 — does not generalise: there the sibling ANSWERED THE OTHER HALF of a two-part question, so removing that half removed the competition. Here the sibling answers the SAME question, badly, and stays on the wire regardless of what is asked.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.what_it_means_for_DQ_T41:
It narrows the decision. A precedence rule — by specificity, by domain, however stated — changes which tools are FORCED. On this evidence that is not the binding constraint for these three, because the right tool was already forced alone and lost anyway.

A rule that only reorders the answerable set would not have moved any of them. What would is a rule that lets a forced tool SUPPRESS a domain-seeded sibling for that turn — which is a much larger claim about the surface, and squarely the owner's.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.OVERSTATED_2026_08_24:
🔴 OVERSTATED, and retracted in part the same day. It cited THREE tools as "R1 forcing the correct tool as the SOLE member of the answerable set" and losing anyway. Re-measured against the LIVE catalogue rather than the frozen snapshot I had been using: only registry_list_workflows is actually forced alone. composition_build_cast_and_graph forces FOUR (itself, kg_add_nodes, kg_build, kg_graph_query) and translation_job_control forces BOTH itself and jobs_cancel.

WHAT STILL STANDS: for composition_build_cast_and_graph the two tools the model ACTUALLY used (glossary_extract_entities_from_doc, glossary_propose_entities) are not in the answerable set, so a domain-seeded competitor did beat a forced tool there. And R1 IS additive by construction — that is a property of the code, not of these measurements. What is withdrawn is the claim that three separate tools were each forced ALONE and lost, which was the strength of the argument. See D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZEN-CATALOGUE.

D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.status: FOUND AND RETRACTED 2026-08-24, same day. The instrument was stale; three of my own 'corrections' corrected records that were RIGHT.

In cycle 3 I needed a catalogue to run `answerable_tools` against, and built one from contracts/agent-runtime-baseline/tools-list.snapshot.json — a FROZEN baseline, as its path says. I then reused that same file for five cycles without once asking whether it matched the running system.

Compared against the live catalogue (315 tools in both, no additions or removals — which is exactly why the staleness was invisible):
    jobs_cancel   snapshot: ['cancel job','stop job','abort job','kill job',

                  LIVE:     ...the same SIX, PLUS 'stop the translation', 'stop it',

    propose_edit  snapshot: no synonyms

The second is my OWN change from cycle 1 of this session, which I then failed to see.
D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.what_it_falsified_of_mine:
THREE CORRECTIONS I PUBLISHED ARE THEMSELVES WRONG, and the records they corrected were right:

1. translation_job_control (cycle 6). I wrote that my earlier move note 'cites synonyms that do not exist' and that 'the 16-character tie I recorded does not happen'. It does. Live: 'Stop the translation for this book.' forces BOTH, translation_job_control via 'stop translation' (16) and jobs_cancel via 'stop the translation' (16 after the article is stripped). DQ-T41's second instance is REAL, and the generic tool did colonise the domain tool's vocabulary exactly as first recorded.

2. composition_build_cast_and_graph (cycle 4). I wrote 'R1 forces EXACTLY ONE tool' and 'kg_build is NOT in the answerable set at all'. Live it forces FOUR — composition_build_cast_and_graph, kg_add_nodes, kg_build, kg_graph_query — so the original note's 'length 23 against kg_build 21' was describing something real and my correction was not.

3. propose_edit (cycle 7). I read 'synonyms: None' off the frontend def and concluded R1 forces nothing for it. Live, R1 forces propose_edit and nothing else. Cycle 1's measurement was right.

WHAT SURVIVES, re-checked against the live catalogue rather than assumed:

The mechanism is real on both tools.

  * the c-tjc3 RUN ITSELF: K=5, called 0/5, jobs_cancel every run. Live data, still valid — but its FRAMING was wrong. I built that arm believing R1 would force translation_job_control alone. It forces both. So the arm never tested what I said it tested, and 'an unambiguous answerable set does not decide the choice' is NOT supported by it.
  * D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REMOVES-NO-WRONG-ONE is OVERSTATED: of the three tools I cited as 'forced alone and lost', only registry_list_workflows actually was.
D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.why_it_was_invisible:
The snapshot and the live catalogue have the SAME 315 tools, with no additions and no removals. Every sanity check I would naturally run — does the tool exist, is the count right, does the name resolve — passes. Only the _meta of two tools had drifted, and one of those drifts was my own edit earlier the same session.

The file is named `contracts/agent-runtime-baseline/tools-list.snapshot.json`. It says BASELINE and it says SNAPSHOT. I read the path when I wrote the loader and used it anyway because it was the convenient shape.

THE RULE I ALREADY HAD AND DID NOT APPLY: verify the deployed thing matches the source before diagnosing anything from its behaviour. I applied it to service images four times this session — checking each rebuild carried my change — and never once to the catalogue I was measuring WITH.

D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.status: FIXED in the harness 2026-08-24; the live re-measure is what proves it.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.what:
INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOLS — glossary_adopt_standards, glossary_propose_kinds, glossary_plan, glossary_propose_batch, glossary_book_sync_apply — are filtered out of the TURN CATALOG itself unless the turn carries world-setup intent. The signal is the `glossary_shaping` skill, which skill_registry injects when `"glossary" in enabled_skills`.

The gate is deliberate and was measured: 'the co-writer proactively rebuilt a newcomer's ontology on a plain "write a chapter 1" turn: three prior fixes failed because hot-seed + find_tools exclusions don't cover tool_load, which loads ANY catalog name.' Its stated principle is that guidance and capability move as ONE signal.

🔴 THE FRONTEND SENDS enabled_skills ON EVERY MESSAGE. This harness never did — `enabled_skills` appears nowhere in scripts/toolloop — so every batch it has ever run observed only the GATED half of that signal. Those five tools could not be measured at all: not because the product cannot reach them, but because the instrument could not construct the state the product requires.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.why_this_is_the_instrument_and_not_the_p:
glossary_book_sync_apply's recorded reason says 'THE INTENT GATE REMOVES IT FROM THE CATALOG, AND R1 CANNOT PUT IT BACK ... whether that is correct is DQ-T31'. Both halves stand: R1 genuinely cannot rescue an intent-gated tool, and whether a request that NAMES a tool should reach it anyway is still the owner's question.

What was missing is the OTHER half of the same design — that the tool IS reachable when the author signals world work, which is exactly what pinning the glossary skill means. A harness that can only ever send the gated case can only ever report the gate.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.the_fix:
`enabled_skills` is now a scenario field, threaded through send_turn into the message body — the same field the FE sends. Additive: a scenario that omits it behaves exactly as before, so no existing batch changes meaning.

It does NOT decide DQ-T31 and does not soften the gate. It lets a scenario say which skills the author has pinned, which is a property of the AUTHOR's session that the harness was simply unable to express.

D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.status: OPEN - the row's BLOCKER is REFUTED (2026-08-26): a divergence CAN be seeded within the safety rules, and was, 5/5. With a real diff on the table the tool is still not called - for a different reason, filed as D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACHED-THE-WIRE.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.what:
glossary_book_sync_apply applies a DIFF between a book's adopted standards and the system standards. With the gate satisfied and the tool advertised 5 of 5, the model does exactly the right thing on every run: calls glossary_book_sync_available first, finds the diff EMPTY, and tells the author so — 'there are currently no upstream changes to apply. Your story bible is up to date with the latest standards.'

called 0/5 is therefore CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, not a failure. There was nothing to apply.

The scenario's own seed_assert says as much and always did: 'Standards adopted, nothing upstream changed since.' The fixture was never built to create a divergence — which nobody could see while the gate kept the tool off the wire entirely.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.why_a_divergence_cannot_be_seeded_within:
Probed directly on a throwaway book, torn down after: adopting a NARROW slice ({genres:['universal'], kinds:['character']}) and then calling glossary_book_sync_available returns {"updates": []}. A partial adopt does not leave the rest pending, so the obvious cheap divergence does not exist.

What WOULD create one is the SYSTEM standards changing after the book adopted — and system standards are shared across every book and every user of this deployment. Writing them to make a test pass is a larger violation than the dogfood book this loop already refuses to touch: it would change what every other author's sync sees. I am not doing it.

RECOMMENDATION: a test-only way to seed a divergence scoped to ONE book — a system-standard version pinned per book, or a fixture hook that records the book as adopted at an older revision. Until then this tool cannot be exercised, and that is a property of what the fixture can safely build rather than of the tool.
retracted_2026_08_24:
🔴 THE SECOND HALF OF THIS DEFECT'S NAME IS WRONG AND I AM RETRACTING IT. I wrote that 'what WOULD create a divergence is the SYSTEM standards changing — and system standards are shared across every book and every user of this deployment... I am not doing it', and recommended a test-only per-book mechanism as an owner decision.

THE PER-BOOK MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AS A PLAIN COLUMN. Read from the diff query (book_sync_handler.go, syncGenresAvailable):
    WHERE bg.book_id=$1 AND bg.deprecated_at IS NULL AND bg.source_ref IS NOT NULL
      AND ( (sg.genre_id IS NULL AND ug.genre_id IS NULL)
         OR COALESCE(sg.content_hash, ug.content_hash) IS DISTINCT FROM bg.source_hash )
A row is 'available' when the upstream content_hash differs from `bg.source_hash` — and source_hash is a column on book_genres (and book_kinds), keyed by book_id. It is the BOOK's record of what it adopted. Both sides of the comparison are writable; I only ever considered the shared one.

So a divergence is seedable by touching ONE ROW of the throwaway book's own book_genres — isolated by construction, torn down with the book, and invisible to every other book and user. The safety objection was real about the route I had in mind and simply did not apply to the route that exists.

THE FIRST HALF STANDS: with an empty diff the model does the right thing — it calls glossary_book_sync_available, finds nothing, and says the story bible is up to date. called 0/5 was correct behaviour against a fixture with nothing to apply.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.theory_2026_08_24:
Seed a divergence by updating source_hash on the throwaway book's OWN adopted rows, after the adopt step creates them. Then glossary_book_sync_available should report updates, and the tool under test becomes reachable for the first time.

REFUTED IF: sync_available still returns {"updates": []} after the seed (then source_hash is not the axis the diff turns on and I have misread the query), or the rows come back with a status the apply path refuses (e.g. everything reads 'retired' because the JOIN fails rather than the hash differing) — which would mean I seeded the wrong KIND of divergence and must say so rather than accept a green run.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.the_blocker_was_REFUTED_2026_08_26:
The row concluded: 'what WOULD create one is the SYSTEM standards changing - and system standards are shared across every book and every user of this deployment ... I am not doing it.' The refusal was right; the PREMISE was wrong.

book_sync_handler.go states the rule symmetrically, in its own header:
    update available  <=>  source resolves live AND its hash != book.source_hash
`source_hash` is a column on the BOOK's row - 'the standard's content_hash at copy time'. So the diff is a comparison between two sides and perturbing EITHER creates it. One of those sides is book-scoped.

TWO SAFE METHODS, both measured:
  1. Book-scoped SQL: UPDATE the throwaway book's own book_kinds.source_hash. Probed - updates went from [] to 2. Nothing shared is touched. (SELECT ran first, per the rule.)
  2. THE PRODUCT'S OWN PATH, which is what the scenario uses: create a RUN-UNIQUE user-tier kind, adopt it into the throwaway book, then glossary_user_patch it. An author editing their own standard is exactly the journey this tool exists for. Probed - updates [] -> 1, with mine={name:'Loop Kind X'} vs theirs={name:'Loop Kind X RENAMED'}.

🔴 THE SCOPING IS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, and it is why method 2 is not the violation the row feared: patching an EXISTING user standard would diverge every other book of this account that adopted it, INCLUDING the dogfood book. A standard created for this run is adopted by exactly one throwaway book, so nothing else can see the divergence.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.what_the_live_run_then_showed:
batch c-booksync1, K=5, zero errored runs:
    glossary_book_sync_available called 5/5 and returned a REAL diff on every run
    the model reported it correctly: 'there is one update available ... Would you like me to apply this change?'
    glossary_book_sync_apply: surfaced 0/5, called 0/5

So the row's own reading - 'called 0/5 is CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, there was nothing to apply' - no longer holds. There IS something to apply, the model FOUND it, and it could not act because the tool was not on the wire. The cause moved from the FIXTURE to the SURFACE, which is a different cause and is filed as its own row rather than folded in here.

    plan_run_id          01a02fb6-f4b2-...   a REAL UUIDv7, not a placeholder
So this is NOT the D-UNDECLARED-REF/model_ref class ('default' as an id). Every validator in _execute_authoring_run_create passes on this payload, which leaves exactly one raise: svc.create -> plan_runs.get_for_book(book_id, plan_run_id) -> None -> LookupError('plan run not found') -> HTTPException(400, {'code':'action_error'}) with NO message.

AND THE MODEL'S OWN EXPLANATION IS A CONFABULATION. Run 1 answered 'the plan_run_id I used was actually the book_id itself'. The stored payload shows it was not. A model's account of its own failure is not evidence.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.theory:
A CROSS-WIRE, not an invention. The same id 01a02fb6-f4b2 was also sent as `book_id` to composition_package_tree, which failed 'not found or not accessible'. One id in two different id-shaped slots is a cross-wire; and a UUIDv7 stamped ~150ms after the fixture book cannot be fabricated by a model — the timestamp is in the id. So f4b2 is a REAL id provisioning created.

  H1  f4b2 is the fixture's project_id (composition_work, minted right after the book).
      Predicts BOTH observations: not a book -> package_tree 'not accessible'; not a plan run ->       LookupError. Store.before confirms a composition_work row exists.
  H2  f4b2 is the SEEDED plan run's id. REFUTED by the 400 itself: the seed_assert proves a       compiled plan run exists ON THIS BOOK, and get_for_book filters on nothing but (id,       book_id), so if f4b2 were it the create would have SUCCEEDED.
  H3  a third provisioning artifact.
H1 is the one the evidence supports; H3 stays open until the ids are compared.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.refuted_if: The seeded plan run's id EQUALS what the model sent (then the fault is in book scoping, not a cross-wire), or the model's plan_run_id differs from the fixture's project_id (then it is H3 and the source must be named before anything is fixed).
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.why_this_was_not_decidable_before: THE INSTRUMENT DISCARDED THE ONLY IDS THAT INTERPRET THE PAYLOAD. provision.py records `fx.project_id` and `fx.seeded` (every seed step's result), and fe_runner's batch writer picks fields explicitly — it keeps book_id and drops BOTH. So a batch can show a cross-wired id and contain nothing to say what that id IS. That is why this tool got a confident, wrong blocked reason. Recording them is a prerequisite for the measurement, not a convenience.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.measured_outcome:
BOTH OF MY HYPOTHESES WERE REFUTED BY THE MEASUREMENT, and recording that is the point of having written them down first.
  H1 the project_id — REFUTED. H2 the seeded plan run — REFUTED.
The id is the fixture's CHAPTER_ID: the editor context the turn carries. Identified on 2 of 2 runs of batch c-authrun4-diag, by an instrument built for the purpose (fe_runner.seed_ids), against the payload recovered from mcp_gate_tasks.

ONE CROSS-WIRE, TWO VICTIMS, AND THE SECOND IS WHY IT IS SELF-SEALING:
  composition_package_tree      book_id      = the chapter id -> 'not found or not accessible'
  composition_authoring_run_manage plan_run_id = the chapter id -> LookupError -> bare 400
package_tree is the tool that RETURNS the real plan run id (`runs.recent`). The cross-wire breaks the lookup that would have corrected it, so the model can never recover inside the turn.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.two_named_causes:
C2 — THE DROP EXISTS AND COULD NOT SEE THIS ARGUMENT. `_inject_context_ids` iterates over exactly ('book_id','chapter_id','project_id'), so a context id landing in an argument called anything else is never examined. Verified against the DEPLOYED function: given {book_id: BOOK, plan_run_id: CHAPTER} it returned plan_run_id UNTOUCHED, while the same function given package_tree's {book_id: CHAPTER} correctly SUBSTITUTED the real book. The mechanism was not weak here, it was absent — and the absence is invisible because those three names cover most tools. FIXED: _drop_crosswired_foreign_ids, same evidence standard (exact match against an id this turn published under another name), same emitter narrowing, DROP only and never substitute.

C1 — THE RESUME PATH IS BLIND TO TWO OF THE THREE IDS. resume_stream_response rebuilds context_ids as {'book_id': susp.book_id, 'studio': susp.studio} — chapter_id and project_id are absent, and chat_suspended_runs HAS NO COLUMN FOR EITHER, so they cannot be restored. Every tool call after a suspension therefore runs with a cross-wire check that has nothing to match against. This is the SAME CLASS as the bug the comment directly above that line already records (the dropped `studio` flag), with the same measured symptom on the same two tools — the fix added `studio` and stopped there. NOT fixed in this cycle: it needs a migration, and the tool under test does not depend on it (the manage call is the FIRST call of the turn, on the main loop, where all three ids are present). Filed separately so it is not lost.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.also_wrong_in_the_surface: plan_run_id's description named ONE supplier, plan_propose_spec, which PROPOSES A NEW PLAN. On a book that already has a compiled plan that is the wrong instruction, and the only other thing the model held was the chapter id. Corrected to name composition_package_tree's `runs.recent` for an existing plan and to say a chapter id is never one.

D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.status: FIXED and PROVEN 2026-08-24. DQ-T42 is withdrawn — it rested on a premise of mine that was wrong.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.what:
composition_generate validates its SCENE target at propose (the node must exist and be in the gated Work's project) and does not validate its CHAPTER target at all. Measured over MCP: a chapter_id that does not exist mints a confirm_token; so does a chapter belonging to a different book, in both directions. The author is shown a cost-bearing approval card for a generation that cannot succeed.

It is APPROVE-THEN-FAIL, not a cross-book write: the payload carries the GATED project's book_id, the chapter path resolves scenes by scenes_for_chapter(project_id, chapter_id), and the persist targets that same book_id — so a foreign chapter fails at confirm. Read from the code rather than confirmed, because confirming spends.

The behaviour is DELIBERATE and documented in the source: 'The CHAPTER target is validated at confirm by the engine (it needs book-service to resolve the chapter sort/plan).'
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.why_i_did_not_just_fix_it:
Because the fix cannot be made without choosing a failure mode, and the choice is not mine.

composition-service holds no authoritative chapter table: outline_node.chapter_id covers only OUTLINED chapters, and a chapter with no scenes is normal and legitimate, so a local check would refuse valid work. Existence therefore requires book-service. The obvious helper, get_chapter_sort_orders, is explicitly NOT book-scoped ('the caller MUST have verified book ownership first') and returns {} on ANY failure — so a guard built on it would fail OPEN, which is the shape this loop has already filed as a defect twice.

So the real question is what the most expensive tool on the platform does while book-service is unreachable, and both answers cost something.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.dq_t42_recommendation:
DQ-T42 — should composition_generate verify the CHAPTER target at propose, and what happens when book-service cannot answer?

MY RECOMMENDATION, and it is a recommendation: verify at propose against a BOOK-SCOPED book-service route (get_draft is scoped by URL: /v1/books/{book_id}/chapters/{chapter_id}), and FAIL CLOSED with a refusal that says the target could not be VERIFIED rather than that it does not exist. Reasons: an unverifiable target during an outage is exactly when a bogus spend is hardest for an author to understand; the refusal costs nothing while the alternative costs money; and 'degrade must surface unverified' is already this platform's rule elsewhere. The cost is real and should be stated plainly: during a book-service outage no chapter generation could be proposed at all.

THE OWNER DECIDES. I am not making this change to unblock a tool.
dq_t42_dissolved_2026_08_24:
🔴 DQ-T42 DISSOLVES AND I RETRACT IT. I filed it because 'existence therefore requires book-service', which made the fix a choice about what the platform's most expensive tool does during an outage of another service — fail-open or fail-closed — and I said that was the owner's. The premise was wrong.

I had reasoned: composition-service holds no authoritative chapter table; outline_node.chapter_id covers only OUTLINED chapters; a chapter with no scenes is normal and legitimate; so a local check would refuse valid work. The last step is false, and the engine says so itself:

    engine.generate_chapter:
        scenes = await outline.scenes_for_chapter(project_id, chapter_id)
        if not scenes:
            raise HTTPException(400, {'code': 'NO_CHAPTER_PLAN',
                                      'detail': 'chapter has no scene plan; decompose it first'})

A chapter with no scene plan CANNOT BE GENERATED AT ALL. Non-empty scenes_for_chapter is a necessary precondition of the whole operation, it is a LOCAL query against this service's own outline_node, and it is scoped by project_id. So the propose-time check refuses exactly what the confirm would refuse, with no cross-service call and therefore no degrade to decide.

And it covers both failing bars by construction: a chapter that does not exist has no scenes in this project, and another book's chapter has no scenes in THIS project either. The same single predicate the engine already trusts.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.theory_2026_08_24_second:
Add the chapter-target branch beside the scene-target branch that already validates, using scenes_for_chapter(pid, chapter_id). Predicts: absent chapter -> refused, foreign chapter -> refused, a real chapter WITH a scene plan -> still mints.

REFUTED IF a chapter that genuinely has a scene plan stops minting — that would mean the predicate is not the one the engine uses and I have broken the tool to satisfy a bar. The control is therefore not optional: it must be asserted in the same test.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.proof:
Falsifier proven RED on the original defect (DID NOT RAISE) and green with the check active, with the CONTROL asserted in the same file: a chapter that HAS a scene plan must still mint, or the predicate is the wrong one and the tool is broken for every real caller.

Verified against the DEPLOYED image, before and after:
    absent chapter                   card minted -> REFUSED
    book B's chapter vs project A    card minted -> REFUSED
    book A's chapter vs project B    card minted -> REFUSED
    a chapter WITH a scene plan      -> STILL MINTS (control)
    a plan-less chapter on book B    -> still refused (the seed did not disable the check)

Live K=5 on an arm that seeds a scene plan: called 5/5, suspended 4/5, store unchanged, zero errored runs.

TWO PRE-EXISTING TESTS FAILED AND BOTH WERE RIGHT TO. test_uuid_errors_name_the_field caught the new site naming 'chapter_id' while READING the target_id alias — fixed by reading args.chapter_id, which is also what makes the message true for the caller. And test_generate_chapter_mints_confirm_token stubbed no outline repo, because until now a chapter target needed nothing; it now stubs a chapter that HAS a plan, with the absent case left to its own file. D-SYNC-APPLY-MINTS-A-CARD-FOR-ROWS-THAT-.status: NAMED and FIXED 2026-08-24, after the divergence seed made the tool reachable for the first time.
D-SYNC-APPLY-MINTS-A-CARD-FOR-ROWS-THAT-.what:
With a real divergence seeded, glossary_book_sync_apply is reachable — and three SHIP bars fail. Driven over MCP, every one of these MINTED A CARD:
    an item id that does not exist anywhere            -> card minted
    a book with ZERO available updates                 -> card minted
    book A's sync row applied against book B           -> card minted
The empty-items case is refused correctly ('items is required (read glossary_book_sync_available first)'), and a valid propose changes nothing until confirmed (verified: the seeded rows were still stale after the propose).

So the author can be shown a Tier-W card — one whose every row decides whether their own value is overwritten — for rows that are not available updates at all. Same class as composition_generate's chapter target and composition_authoring_run_create's plan run: approve-then-fail on a gated write.
D-SYNC-APPLY-MINTS-A-CARD-FOR-ROWS-THAT-.why_this_one_is_mine_to_fix_and_generate:
composition_generate's chapter check needs BOOK-SERVICE, so fixing it meant choosing what happens during an outage of another service — fail-open or fail-closed on the most expensive tool on the platform. That is DQ-T42 and the owner's.

This check is SAME-SERVICE. The available set is computed by syncGenresAvailable / syncKindsAvailable / syncAttributesAvailable, which glossary_book_sync_available already runs against the same pool for a Tier R call. There is no cross-service degrade to decide: a query failure here is a database failure in this service and surfacing it is ordinary. The file also already states the principle — 'Mint-time validation (§11 #8): reject a malformed proposal up front so the agent never shows a card destined to 4xx' — and already validates entity, choice and UUID SHAPE. This extends that rule from the shape of an id to whether the id is one of the book's available updates.
D-SYNC-APPLY-MINTS-A-CARD-FOR-ROWS-THAT-.fix: Before minting, compute the book's available set from the same three functions the reader uses and refuse any item whose id is not in it. One rule covers all three failing bars: an unknown id, another book's id, and an id that is up to date are all simply absent from that set. The refusal names the reader, exactly as the empty-items refusal already does.
D-SYNC-APPLY-MINTS-A-CARD-FOR-ROWS-THAT-.proof:
FIXED AND VERIFIED BY BEHAVIOUR AGAINST THE DEPLOYED BINARY (the image's `strings` showed nothing, so the symbol check was a false negative and the probe decided it instead):
    an id that exists nowhere          card minted -> REFUSED
    a book with zero available updates card minted -> REFUSED
    book A's row against book B        card minted -> REFUSED
    a genuinely available row          card minted -> STILL MINTS (the control)
Falsifier proven RED on all three assertions with the guard neutralised, GREEN with it active.

🔴 THE FALSIFIER WAS PARTLY VACUOUS AT FIRST AND THE ORDER OF ITS CALLS WAS WHY. The control mint ran FIRST, and because sync_apply is single-use that changed what a later mint on the same book did — so with the guard disabled the unknown-id assertion still passed, crediting this check with a refusal it never made. Fixed twice over: the refusals now run against untouched state with the control LAST, and the unknown-id assertion asserts the MESSAGE ('not an available update') rather than merely that an error occurred.
D-SYNC-APPLY-MINTS-A-CARD-FOR-ROWS-THAT-.suite_state: 🔴 THE GLOSSARY-SERVICE SUITE IS NOT GREEN AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT IS. Run whole against the dev database: 32 failures in internal/api and 1 in internal/migrate, on state this DB does not have — the migrate test wants 93 empty attribute descriptions pre-migration and finds 3. D-JOBS-LIST-ADVERTISES-CANCEL-ON-JOBS-TH.status: OPEN - BLOCKED on DQ-T46 for the product half. The harness half is now DURABLE rather than cleaned-once, and the row's own description of the mechanism was wrong.
D-JOBS-LIST-ADVERTISES-CANCEL-ON-JOBS-TH.what:
Measured: all 60 translation jobs visible to the test account via jobs_list were ORPHANS whose book had been deleted. jobs_list listed every one with control_caps ['cancel']; translation_job_control resolves through the job's book and refused every one with 'not found or not accessible'. So the list offered an affordance that could not be exercised, and the refusal said nothing about why.

This cost a probe before it was understood: ids read straight out of translation_jobs looked perfectly good and every call refused, which reads as a broken tool. It is not — the tool is right and the LIST is optimistic.

SEVERITY IS MODEST AND STATED: books are not routinely deleted in production, so the population here was manufactured by this harness. What is general is the shape — control_caps is computed without asking whether the controlling tool could actually reach the job.
D-JOBS-LIST-ADVERTISES-CANCEL-ON-JOBS-TH.harness_half_fixed: Every translation scenario SQL-seeds a pending job on its throwaway book; teardown removes the book and the job survives, because it lives in another database with no FK to it. provision.py --sweep cleaned books and worlds and not jobs, so 304 rows had accumulated. sweep_orphan_translation_jobs now removes a job ONLY when its book_id is absent from loreweave_book.books. SELECT before DML, run once: 310 rows -> 6, and all six survivors were verified to have live books (including the dogfood book's). A harness that leaves undeletable rows behind eventually measures its own debris.
D-JOBS-LIST-ADVERTISES-CANCEL-ON-JOBS-TH.the_harness_half_was_not_actually_fixed_:
🔴 THE SWEEP EXISTED AND NOTHING CALLED IT. `sweep_orphan_translation_jobs` was written on 2026-08-24 and run ONCE by hand (310 rows -> 6). Re-derived today:

    21 translation jobs, 14 of them CONTROLLABLE (pending/running)
    those 14 reference 14 distinct books - and ZERO of those books exist

The debris came straight back, because the leak is per-run and the cleanup was not. A one-time sweep for a recurring leak is not a fix; it is a measurement taken once.

fe_runner now calls it BEFORE every batch, beside the existing leaked-fixture sweep and for the same stated reason: a crashed run leaves debris and the NEXT batch must not measure it, so an after-only sweep is skipped by exactly the crash that caused the mess. Swept 15 on the run that found this; 0 controllable orphans remain, 6 total, all with live books.
D-JOBS-LIST-ADVERTISES-CANCEL-ON-JOBS-TH.the_rows_mechanism_was_WRONG_and_here_is:
The row says 'translation_job_control resolves through the job's book'. Traced: `_cancel_job_core` does NOT touch the book at all - it queries translation_jobs by job_id and owner, so an orphan would cancel fine through that path.

The refusal comes from ONE line higher, in the MCP tool:
    row = SELECT owner_user_id, book_id, status ... FROM translation_jobs WHERE job_id=$1
    await _require_edit(tc, row['book_id'])        <- HERE
It is an EDIT-grant check on the book, and a deleted book has no grant to check. Worth correcting because it changes what a fix would have to touch: the gate is doing its job, and nothing in the control path is broken.
D-JOBS-LIST-ADVERTISES-CANCEL-ON-JOBS-TH.what_is_NOT_covered:
- THE PRODUCT HALF IS UNTOUCHED and is DQ-T46: control_caps is derived from the job's STATUS and KIND alone, so the list advertises an affordance it has not verified is reachable.
- `control_caps` IS NOT DOCUMENTED ANYWHERE. jobs_list's description never mentions it, so a caller reading control_caps: ['cancel'] reasonably treats it as a promise rather than a status-derived hint. Naming that in the description is the cheap honest half and is part of the DQ rather than done unilaterally, because it decides what the field MEANS.
- OTHER SERVICES WERE NOT AUDITED for the same shape. knowledge, composition, video_gen and lore_enrichment all register control endpoints; whether any gates on a resource that can vanish beneath a job is unmeasured.

D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-24, and the arm is REFUTED by its own falsifier. The tool stays blocked; my recommendation is REVERSED.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.retracts:
🔴 THIS RETRACTS THE BLOCKED REASON I WROTE FOR registry_list_workflows. It says 'THE TWO TOOLS ARE THE SAME CAPABILITY, checked rather than assumed' and recommends marking it visibility=legacy, superseded_by=workflow_list — which would have DELETED a capability from the catalogue on the strength of a comparison that missed the arguments.

What I compared was the two DESCRIPTIONS and the UNFILTERED return (12 rows each). What I did not read was what each tool ACCEPTS:
    registry_list_workflows  properties: {surface: book|editor|studio}
    workflow_list            properties: {}            <- no arguments at all
MEASURED by calling the federated tool, and the filter is not cosmetic:
    (no filter) 12    book 12    editor 11    studio 6
The studio sees HALF the workflows. So there is a question only this tool can answer — 'what workflows are available in the studio?' — and its always-on twin cannot answer it at all.

Same error class as two other reasons I retracted this week: for composition_authoring_run_manage I censused required ARGUMENTS and never read what the readers RETURN; here I read the returns and never read the arguments. Both times the conclusion was 'nothing else can do this' / 'something else already does this', and both times one unread half of the schema decided it.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.theory:
The tool is unreachable for 'What workflows are available to me?' because the always-on twin answers that question completely and first. It should be REACHABLE for a request that names a SURFACE, because the twin structurally cannot narrow and returning all 12 would be wrong.

Verified against the deployed matcher: 'What workflows are available on the studio surface?' makes registry_list_workflows answerable — and it is the ONLY tool in that set, because workflow_list is consumer-local and invisible to R1 (though still advertised).
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.refuted_if:
The model answers a surface-scoped question with workflow_list anyway — returning all 12 where 6 are correct — or asks rather than calling. Then the twin wins even where it is WRONG, which is a stronger version of the duplicate finding and I say so rather than reaching for another prompt.

🔴 AND THE ORIGINAL ARM KEEPS ITS RESULT EITHER WAY. 'What workflows are available to me?' answered by workflow_list on 5 of 5 is CORRECT behaviour — the answer was true and complete — and a surface-scoped arm does not retire that finding.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.outcome:
The theory held on the schemas and the refutation clause fired on the model. Measured, K=5:
    4 of 5 runs answered from workflow_list and reported NINE workflows as 'available on the studio surface' — five of them are not (draw-a-map, kg-build, lore-so-far, populate-from-notes, translation-pass). The studio has six.
    1 of 5 called registry_list_workflows and named studio workflows only.

So the always-on twin does not merely win a duplicate race; it makes the model WRONG on a question it structurally cannot answer, and confidently. The arm is refuted and is recorded as such rather than concluded.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.recommendation_reversed:
🔴 DO NOT MARK registry_list_workflows visibility=legacy / superseded_by=workflow_list. That was my recommendation on file and it is WRONG: it would delete the only tool that can answer a surface-scoped workflow question, and the measured consequence of answering such a question without it is a wrong list presented as fact.

THE QUESTION I NOW RECOMMEND PUTTING instead — still the owner's — is how an always-on consumer-local tool should coexist with a federated tool that is strictly more capable. Two shapes worth weighing, neither of which I am choosing:
  * give workflow_list the same `surface` argument, so the always-on answer can be correct; or
  * have workflow_list's description say what it CANNOT do (it cannot narrow by surface) and name registry_list_workflows for that case, which is the cheaper change and leaves the capability where it is.
The first makes the twin sufficient; the second makes the twin honest. The measurement does not decide between them.

D-THE-GATE-CANNOT-SEE-A-FALSIFIER-I-MEAS.what:
The DATA-falsifier bar is `self._check(bool(t.get('falsifier')), ...)` — it asserts a falsifier EXISTS. It has no way to know the run REFUTED it. So a batch whose stored tool calls contradict its own prediction still passes that bar, and the only thing standing between it and a `proven` conclusion is a human reading the prose.

TWICE NOW THAT HUMAN WAS ME, AND ONCE I NEARLY MISSED IT:
  * b18-gen-control (cycle 12) passed 8 of 9 bars while every composition_generate call in it carried model_ref='default' and came back ok=false — the exact invention its falsifier names. I annotated it `falsifier_violated_2026_08_24` and moved on.
  * c-regwf (cycle 18) passes the bar today while 4 of 5 runs reported NINE workflows as studio-available when the studio has six — a refutation clause I had added to that falsifier myself before the run.

A gate that says 'the batch may NOT be concluded' for a missing ship_audit case, but says nothing when the prediction was measured false, is protecting the cheaper thing.
D-THE-GATE-CANNOT-SEE-A-FALSIFIER-I-MEAS.theory:
Make the refutation MACHINE-VISIBLE and fail the bar on it. A tool entry that records a violation — the key I already used by hand, `falsifier_violated*` — must fail DATA falsifier, so `conclude --state proven` refuses it and the only way past is to fix the cause and re-run.

REFUTED IF: the new bar does not fire on b18-gen-control, the ORIGINAL instance, which is annotated and on disk; or if it fires on any batch already concluded proven, which would mean it is catching something other than a recorded refutation.
D-THE-GATE-CANNOT-SEE-A-FALSIFIER-I-MEAS.not_in_scope: This does NOT recompute falsifiers. The gate still cannot read 'the model invented an id' out of a batch and judge it — that needs the claim expressed as data, per falsifier, which is a much larger design. This only stops the gate from silently accepting a refutation SOMEONE HAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. It is the cheap half, and it closes the specific hole that let an 8-of-9 sit one probe away from `proven`.

So a summary would be reporting, not inventing — unlike the degenerate-pass case, where there was genuinely nothing to say.

RECOMMENDATION: on hitting max_total_passes, emit an honest close naming what DID land and what stopped — 'created 2 entities and 2 graph nodes; could not build the graph because the project has no embedding model configured'. Both halves are already in the turn's own record. The alternative shape, a bare 'I ran out of steps', is worse than it looks: an author who is told nothing at least does not believe the work is finished, whereas a vague apology after a successful write invites exactly the wrong inference. D-THE-OUT2-LINT-ONLY-INSPECTS-TOOLS-THAT.what:
scripts/context-budget-defaults-lint.py is the cross-service enforcement for OUT-2, and docs/standards/mcp-tool-io.md cites it as the partial coverage that 'blocks NEW violations'. Its trigger is the presence of the compliance machinery:

    line 222   if "detail" not in params or "limit" not in params: continue
    line 238   if "detail" in fields and "limit" in fields:

So it checks that a tool which ALREADY has `detail` and `limit` defaults them well. A list tool that never implemented either falls through the `continue` and is never looked at. 🔴 A tool is exempted from the check by being MORE non-compliant, not less. Line 18's stated exemption ('a single-item tool — has `detail`, no `limit` — is EXEMPT') is deliberate and correct; the NEITHER case is not an exemption anyone wrote, it is a fall-through.

D-THE-OUT2-LINT-ONLY-INSPECTS-TOOLS-THAT.what_this_does_NOT_say:

Not shipped here: it belongs to the OUT-2 owner, it would red a pre-commit lint across five services on its first run, and — measured — it clears neither blocked tool. Filed with the numbers so it can be taken as a decision rather than as a side effect of my chasing a silent turn.

D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.status: NAMED and MEASURED 2026-08-25 at 5/5. Found by reading a reply in full instead of trusting my own counter. RECOMMENDED, not shipped — see why.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.what:
services/chat-service/app/services/stream_events.py::scrub_jargon is the Track C §4 'speak plainly' guard: a deterministic table of regex rewrites applied to the assistant's user-facing text at the wire chokepoint, because a mid-tier model does not reliably comply with being asked. The intent is sound and the table is thoughtfully scoped — its own comment excludes kind/tool/spec/job/token precisely because rewriting them 'would mangle normal prose'.

But the rules are word-boundary regexes, and `-` is a word boundary. So they fire INSIDE identifiers, which the guard has no concept of:
    glossary-bootstrap   -> 'story bible-bootstrap'
    entity-triage        -> 'element-triage'
    vision-to-book       -> 'book-building'
None of those three names exists. The guard was designed not to mangle PROSE and was never asked about NAMES.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.measured:
c-regwf4, 5 of 5 runs. Every reply answers the studio-surface question correctly — the right six workflows, no non-studio ones — and then hands the user two identifiers that do not exist. Verbatim from run 2:
    * **Clean up a book's suggested items** (`element-triage`): …
    * **Set up a book's world categories** (`story bible-bootstrap`): …
This is 5/5, not the 1-in-5 effects this loop usually argues about, and it needs no live run to reproduce — scrub_jargon('glossary-bootstrap') shows it in one line.

AND IT SILENTLY CORRUPTED MY OWN MEASUREMENTS. Cycle 36 recorded that a reply 'names workflows by TITLE — Book-building'. That was never the model paraphrasing: it is vision-to-book with this table applied. Any counter of mine that matches raw slugs under-counts by exactly these three names, so the c-regwf4 numbers above were re-taken with a scrub-aware matcher (importing the real _JARGON_SUBS, not a copy of it) before being believed. They were unchanged.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.why_it_blocks_the_tool: registry_list_workflows' DATA bar is answer-is-true. The answer that reaches the user misnames two of the six things it is listing, in a form the user cannot use and a subsequent workflow_load(slug) cannot resolve. Calling that a true answer to get a green would be exactly the gaming the standing rule forbids, so the tool stays blocked — but on this cause rather than the one it was blocked on, which is a different problem and is recorded as such.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.the_fix_and_why_not_here:
The narrow fix is to leave inline code spans alone: the slugs arrive wrapped in backticks, and a code span is by definition a NAME rather than prose, which is the distinction the guard's own comment is reaching for. Doing it inside scrub_jargon alone is a trap, though — it is also called per-DELTA on a hold-back buffer, so a span split across two deltas would still be rewritten. A correct fix has to teach _is_risky_tail to hold an unterminated span the same way it already holds an unfinished multi-word phrase.

That is a change to a flagship streaming guarantee, and the half of it that fits in the end of a cycle is precisely the half that leaves a silent seam. Filed with a 5/5 measurement and a one-line reproduction so it can be done properly.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.state_reason: VERIFIED 2026-08-25: the guard IS shipped - stream_events.py::_rewrites_part_of_a_hyphenated_name, line 142. The row still read 'RECOMMENDED, not shipped'.

D-GLOSSARY-BUILD-WRITES-VIETNAMESE-INTO-.what:
services/composition-service/app/services/glossary_build/prompts.py states the intent in its module docstring: 'language adapts to the book's source language via `lang` (the POC ran vi)'. The MCP boundary carried the POC's value as the DEFAULT — _GlossaryBuildArgs.lang: str = 'vi' (server.py:8762) — and the op=start handler passes `args.lang` straight into create_run with no fallback to the book. The argument also carries NO description, so a model has no reason to set it and never does.

Net effect: every model-initiated build writes the glossary in Vietnamese, whatever the book's language.
D-GLOSSARY-BUILD-WRITES-VIETNAMESE-INTO-.measured:
Seen while running the A/B depth probe. The harness fixture is created with original_language='en' (scripts/toolloop/provision.py:139) and the build returned original_language 'vi' with names like 'Ấn Chương Tro (Ashen Sigil)' and 'Hộ Vệ của Pale (Wardens of the Pale)'.

🔴 AND IT CONFOUNDED MY OWN HEADLINE. The A/B compared arm A (English) against arm B (Vietnamese) and I reported chars-per-filled-field across them as if the two were like for like. The fill-RATE comparison survives — a filled slot is filled in any language — but the depth figure spans two languages and I should not have quoted it without saying so.
D-GLOSSARY-BUILD-WRITES-VIETNAMESE-INTO-.the_fix:
Resolve the book's original_language when `lang` is not supplied, using the get_book client already used elsewhere in this file, with a service bearer minted the same way. An explicitly supplied lang still wins. 'vi' stays as the LAST-RESORT fallback when the book cannot be read, so the error path keeps today's behaviour instead of smuggling in a different guess — and it logs when that happens.

The default must become None, not a different string: with `lang: str = 'vi'` there is no way to tell 'the caller asked for Vietnamese' from 'the caller said nothing'. Presence, not truthiness.

An explicit lang still wins; "vi" remains only as the last-resort fallback when the book cannot be read, so the error path keeps today behaviour instead of swapping in a different guess, and it logs.

D-GLOSSARY-BUILD-WRITES-VIETNAMESE-INTO-.and_it_corrected_my_own_headline:
The A/B I published had compared arm A in ENGLISH against arm B in VIETNAMESE and I quoted a chars-per-field figure across the two as if like for like. Re-run with the confound removed, the result stands and the numbers barely move:

    ARM A  0.246 fill / 39.0 ch  ->  0.246 / 39.3   (two runs, essentially identical)
    ARM B  0.516 / 108.7 (vi)    ->  0.469 / 114.5  (en)

Corrected claim: 1.9x the fill at 2.9x the depth, about 5.8x the attribute content (15 x 39.3 = ~590 chars against 30 x 114.5 = ~3,435). Arm A reproducing to three decimal places across two independent runs is also the only stability evidence this probe has - n=2, still not a distribution.

D-TWO-TOOLS-DECLARE-THE-IDENTICAL-SYNONY.status: NAMED and MEASURED 2026-08-25. A concrete, fixable instance of what DQ-T41 argues about.
D-TWO-TOOLS-DECLARE-THE-IDENTICAL-SYNONY.what: composition_build_cast_and_graph and kg_build both declare the synonym "build the knowledge graph" - the same five words, verbatim, in two different tools. answerable_tools is additive and scores by match LENGTH, so an identical string is an exact tie by construction: nothing downstream can break it, because there is nothing to break it WITH. Both land on the wire indistinguishable.
D-TWO-TOOLS-DECLARE-THE-IDENTICAL-SYNONY.why_it_matters_here: The composition-glossary-build scenario built its prompt from that exact phrase, on the reasoning that a tool declaring words verbatim should be reachable by them. It is - R1 returns it on every run - but so is its twin, so the scenario cannot discriminate between the two tools it is supposedly choosing between. 0/10 measured a tie, not a tool.
D-TWO-TOOLS-DECLARE-THE-IDENTICAL-SYNONY.the_fix_is_an_owner_call: De-duplicate the phrase: one of the two tools owns "build the knowledge graph" and the other drops it for something that distinguishes it. kg_build is the KG-only builder; composition_build_cast_and_graph builds the cast AND the graph in one call from prose. Those are different jobs and should not share a headline phrase. Which tool keeps it is a product decision, so it is recorded rather than taken.
D-TWO-TOOLS-DECLARE-THE-IDENTICAL-SYNONY.a_lint_would_have_caught_it: Nothing checks for duplicate synonyms across the catalogue. A cross-tool duplicate is always a defect - it guarantees an unbreakable tie - and it is cheap to detect at build time from the same catalog cache this was found in.
D-TWO-TOOLS-DECLARE-THE-IDENTICAL-SYNONY.state_reason: VERIFIED 2026-08-25: scripts/lint_duplicate_synonyms.py reports 0 still-live ties. The phrase was de-duplicated in 4976cc055; the row still read NAMED.

D-THE-GBUILD-SCENARIO-CANNOT-TEST-ITS-OW.status: NAMED 2026-08-25. The scenario is not well-formed; NOT changed, because changing a bar to fit is the one thing the loop forbids.
D-THE-GBUILD-SCENARIO-CANNOT-TEST-ITS-OW.what:
The scenario composition-glossary-build-with-an-ontology carries a falsifier about POST-CALL behaviour: refuted if entities are created with no confirm card, if the op is not start on a first request, or if the model invents a run_id. Every one of those needs the tool to have RUN. The gate blocks earlier, on LIVE called >= 1, so across 39 live runs the falsifier has never been evaluated once.

The scenario therefore measures SELECTION while its falsifier describes SAFETY, and it reports the tool blocked on the first without ever reaching the second.
D-THE-GBUILD-SCENARIO-CANNOT-TEST-ITS-OW.proven_by_the_owners_control: The owner asked the question the loop never asked: name the tool and see. Two control arms, K=5 each. Naming it outright: 5/5 called, 5/5 surfaced, and the store proves execution - glossary_build_runs went from empty to 2 rows every run. Describing its unique capability without naming it: 0/5. So the tool works, and the falsifier becomes evaluable the moment selection is taken out of the question.
D-THE-GBUILD-SCENARIO-CANNOT-TEST-ITS-OW.recommendation:
Split the scenario in two, which is what it is already trying to be: one arm that NAMES the tool and tests the falsifier it actually wrote (confirm card, op=start, no invented run_id), and a separate arm that tests SELECTION against kg_build - which is DQ-T41 and should be reported as a precedence measurement, not as this tool being broken.

NOT DONE HERE. Rewriting a scenario so a blocked tool passes is exactly the move the loop forbids, and it stays forbidden when the scenario really is wrong. The owner decides.

D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.found_by: being asked what remains in runstate, and counting the rows instead of reading the headline
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.invariant: A counter reads a CLOSED machine field. A row it cannot classify STOPS the count; it is never absorbed into a remainder. Prose may sit beside the field and must never be parsed for meaning.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.what:
`recompute_progress` classified defects with `defect_state(d).startswith('open')` over `state or status`. `status` is free prose - 104 of 156 rows carried ONLY that field, median 89 chars, max 311 - and this ledger writes it in capitals ('OPEN - measured 2026-08-23'). So 57 open rows matched neither bucket and fell into `defects_other`, which was DEFINED as `total - proven - open` and therefore always absorbed them silently.

Reported 14 open / 117 other. Actual, after every row was classified: 80 open / 39 fixed / 25 proven / 11 withdrawn / 1 superseded.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.why_it_survived: The guard over it asserted `proven + open + other == total`. Since `other` is the remainder, that identity holds for EVERY possible partition, including a classifier that scores nothing at all. A vacuous assertion over a remainder bucket cannot go red.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.the_fix: `state` is now closed (open|fixed|proven|withdrawn|superseded), is the only field consulted, and an unrecognised or missing value raises. `defects_other` is deleted, and `apply_progress` drops retired keys so it cannot linger at its last value. All 156 rows were classified by rule where the first clause is unambiguous and by an explicit OVERRIDE table where it is not; each override carries its reason in the row as `state_reason`.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.what_the_triage_found: 13 overrides, and 4 of them were rows the loop had already closed and never re-statused - the synonym tie (lint now reports 0 live ties), the jargon scrubber (guard shipped at stream_events.py:142), the registry tenancy bar (probe exists). The fourth is worse: D-GLOSSARY-BUILD-LOSES-TO-A-RAIL read 'NAMED and PROVEN' while this same ledger records pinned_step_tools=[] on all 17 gbuild rows, which refutes it. It is now `withdrawn`.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.red_on_original: PROVEN RED, in memory on a deepcopy - never by editing and restoring the ledger. Parametrised over the shapes that actually shipped: a missing `state`, the verbatim 'OPEN - measured 2026-08-23', 'opened', and 'Open'. Each must raise; under the old counter each was scored as not-open and counted as `other`.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.blast_radius: Every status report this loop produced. The headline 'Open: 14 defects' was wrong in every summary that carried it, including the runstate audit written yesterday.

D-A-REDIRECT-ROW-AND-A-DEPRECATED-ROW-WE.found_by: running the WHOLE scripts suite instead of the one file this cycle touched
D-A-REDIRECT-ROW-AND-A-DEPRECATED-ROW-WE.invariant: An excluded row is excluded for a REASON, and two reasons that need different arithmetic may not share a predicate.
D-A-REDIRECT-ROW-AND-A-DEPRECATED-ROW-WE.what: `test_a_deprecated_row_stays_out_of_the_numerator` asserted `including_deprecated == concluded + len(excluded)`. `excluded` was every row with `counts_toward_release: false` - five deprecated-but-PROVEN tools when it was written. D-A-REDIRECT-ROW-AND-A-DEPRECATED-ROW-WE.the_uncomfortable_half: 🔴 THIS WAS RED AT HEAD AND I SHIPPED IT. The commit that added the redirect row (d1aab0959) ran the composition-service suite - 3816 passed - and not scripts/, where the assertion lives. D-A-SYNONYM-DEDUP-DISARMED-THE-TOOL-THAT.found_by: running the reachability gate that 4976cc055 never ran
D-A-SYNONYM-DEDUP-DISARMED-THE-TOOL-THAT.invariant: A synonym tie is broken by taking the phrase off the tool that LOSES it. Taking it off the winner does not redirect the request - it leaves nobody holding it. And when the loop already holds a MEASUREMENT of which tool a phrase should reach, that measurement outranks a reading of the two descriptions.
D-A-SYNONYM-DEDUP-DISARMED-THE-TOOL-THAT.what:

scenarios-c-silentlen.json (3 sites), scenarios-idem-outline.json (1), scenarios-rebaseline.json (1).

D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.status: Filed and FIXED 2026-08-25. The cause behind two rows that named it from opposite ends: D-A-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-ONLY-THE-AUTHOR-CAN-SUPPLY-HAS-NO-ASK-PATH and D-A-FLAT-SUPERSET-TOOL-DOCUMENTS-NEITHER-ITS-REQUIREMENTS-NOR-ITS-SHAPES.
D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.what:
18 catalogue tools are flat-superset op-dispatch: they declare only `op` as required because one schema serves several ops. So `_missing_required_names` finds nothing missing, the call DISPATCHES, and the SERVER refuses with the per-op requirement it knew all along - "op=create requires from_motif_id, to_motif_id, and kind".

EVERY REPAIR PATH ABOVE THE DISPATCH IS BLIND TO IT. No supplier is named, `_missing_args_message` never runs, and `_tools_named_in_refusal` arms NOTHING because the sentence contains no tool name. The model is told exactly what it lacks and given no way to obtain any of it.

🔴 THE PLATFORM COMPUTED THE ANSWER AND THREW IT AWAY - the third time this loop has met that shape (D-FJ-3 blocking rules computed and discarded, D-FJ-5 a failure emitted with its message removed, D-FJ-12 the emitter written down in prose and not said).
D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.how_it_was_found: Investigating the ASK-PATH row, whose fix I expected to be in `_missing_args_message`. Reading the RECORDED refusal showed it never came from chat-service at all: "Error executing tool composition_authoring_run_manage: op=create requires plan_run_id, budget_usd, and pause_after_each_unit" is the SERVER's string. Verified current by calling four op-dispatch tools directly with only `op` - all four refused server-side with their per-op requirement.
D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.measured: 45 literal per-op refusal strings across every service's MCP layer, all of one shape. In the recorded corpus 52 refusals name arguments this way: 27 also happen to name a tool (arming already fires - composition_arc_template_edit's own prose says "Call composition_arc_template_list to get the id"), and 25 name none at all and are dead.
D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.invariant: A refusal that names required ARGUMENTS must also name a legal MOVE for each - the emitter tool when one is declared, and otherwise to ASK THE AUTHOR.
D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.chokepoint: services/chat-service/app/services/stream_service.py, at the dispatch-refusal site, ABOVE the existing arming call. The guidance is appended to `_refusal_text` so `_tools_named_in_refusal` picks the emitter's name out of it - the fix composes with the arming that already works instead of adding a second arming path.
D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.precision_and_recall:
Measured BEFORE the code was written.
  RECALL   45/45 source strings parse, three-item lists intact.
  PRECISION the schema is the guard: a token survives only if the refusing tool DECLARES it. Over the 70 service 'requires' strings that are NOT the per-op shape - where a greedy matcher does its damage - the guard rejects 66, and the 4 survivors are genuine ("scope=dirty requires chapter_id", "delete_attribute requires genre_code").

🔴 AND THE CONTROL CAUGHT MY FIRST REGEX. `([a-z0-9_]+(?:\s*,\s*[a-z0-9_]+)*(?:\s*,?\s*and\s+[a-z0-9_]+)?)` let the repeating comma group consume ", and" as if `and` were an item, so `kind` was silently dropped from a three-item list. It parsed, it looked right, and it under-counted exactly the arguments a model most needs named. Three candidates were compared against the real strings before one was kept.
D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.proven_live_2026_08_25:

The scenario uses VERBATIM the prompt scenarios-c-authrun.json retired on 2026-08-23 as unsatisfiable - 'Start an authoring run for this book - begin autopilot.' - and that file is NOT modified. What changed is the platform, not the bar.

No tool supplies budget_usd and pause_after_each_unit - take those values from the author's request, or ASK THE AUTHOR...

D-A-PER-OP-REFUSAL-NAMES-ARGUMENTS-AND-N.the_scenarios_falsifier_was_TRIPPED_and_:

    run 1  {op: create, plan_run_id: ..., budget_usd: 50}      INVENTED
    run 2  {op: create, plan_run_id: ..., budget_usd: 50}      INVENTED

THE INVENTION IS IN THE FIRST CALL, BEFORE ANY REFUSAL EXISTS, so this fix neither causes nor prevents it: the guidance is what the model receives AFTER that call, and what it does after receiving it is ask. Softening the bar to 'invents it AND the run is created' would be weakening a bar to fit, and I wrote this bar an hour earlier. It is left RED and filed as its own defect - D-THE-MODEL-FABRICATES-A-MONEY-VALUE-ON-A-SPECULATIVE-FIRST-CALL.

D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.status: OPEN - found 2026-08-25 while verifying kg_build's provenance.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.what:
Tool-result content stored in docs/eval/toolloop/*-raw.json is cut at EXACTLY 4000 characters, mid-token. Distinct recorded content lengths in c-gbuild9 top out at 4000, and 17 kg_project_list results raise 'Unterminated string starting at ... column 3970' on json.loads.

So any analysis that PARSES a recorded result silently fails on every large one, and fails in the direction that looks like a finding: an empty parse reads as 'the tool returned nothing', not as 'the recording is clipped'.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.how_it_bit: My kg_build provenance check reported the project_id came from kg_project_list on 0 of 10 runs. That is the shape of a real and serious finding - it would mean the runtime's context-fill supplied the id and the declaration did nothing. Reading one run by hand refuted it; a substring check gave 10/10.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.why_it_matters: This loop's conclusions are largely derived by sweeping these files. Every such sweep that json.loads a result is under-counting by an unknown amount, and none of them says so.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.not_yet_known: WHETHER THE MODEL SAW THE TRUNCATED TEXT TOO, or only the recording is clipped. Those are very different defects - the first is a live capability bug, the second is an instrument bug - and this row does not claim either. The cap is a suspiciously round 4000, which points at a deliberate recording limit rather than a transport failure, but that is a lead, not a finding.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.third_instance_2026_08_26:
THIRD TIME IN ONE SESSION. Checking whether composition_arc_apply's arc_template_id came from composition_arc_template_list, the substring test said NO on 5 of 5 - which reads as 'the model got the id from somewhere unaccounted for', a serious finding. The list result's recorded content is exactly 4000 chars and ends mid-token ('..."o'), so the id was simply past the cut. Settled instead from the run's own `seed_ids` map: 4 of 5 used THIS RUN'S SEEDED template.

Every instance so far has pointed the same way - the clipped read looks like a defect, not like a clipped read.

D-A-TWO-ENDPOINT-EDGE-NEEDS-N-SEQUENTIAL.status: FIXED - proven live 2026-08-26, batch c-kgedge4, K=5: the edge is PARKED on 5 of 5 runs. Both halves are now closed - the per-node card cost (mode description) and the id-family confusion that survived it (its own row).
D-A-TWO-ENDPOINT-EDGE-NEEDS-N-SEQUENTIAL.what:
kg_propose_edge needs TWO node ids. The path the model takes to get them, kg_add_nodes mode=manual, creates ONE node per call and is Tier A, so every node costs a confirm card. Asked to record that two characters know each other, the turn spends its passes and approvals one node at a time and SUSPENDS on the card for the second node - before kg_propose_edge is ever reached.

Measured: kg_propose_edge called in 1 of 5 runs, and on that run its endpoints were MISSING on all three attempts. 4 of 5 runs ended suspended on a kg_add_nodes card holding exactly ONE node id.
D-A-TWO-ENDPOINT-EDGE-NEEDS-N-SEQUENTIAL.the_one_call_path_exists_and_is_never_ch: mode=from_glossary projects the book's glossary entities in ONE call and returns them all in `nodes` - it would produce both endpoints at once, behind a single card. D-THE-NARRATED-WRITE-GUARD-COUNTS-ACKNOW.status: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-26, within hours of shipping the guard it corrects.
D-THE-NARRATED-WRITE-GUARD-COUNTS-ACKNOW.what: _claimed_an_effect_without_acting matched "I have NOTED your instruction to stop the translation" and reported it as a narrated write. The pattern was a word-boundary match on "i've" or "i have", an optional "already", then any word ending in -ed (plus a short list of irregulars). A bare -ed suffix cannot tell RECEIVING information from CHANGING something. The turn it fired on had honestly reported an error one sentence earlier, so the guard would have nudged a model that was already being candid.
D-THE-NARRATED-WRITE-GUARD-COUNTS-ACKNOW.how_it_was_caught: 🔴 BY THE CALIBRATION TEST THAT WAS WRITTEN FOR THIS, and the design detail that made it work is worth keeping: it asserts WHICH TOOLS fire, not how many. Adding batch c-cancel1 to the corpus put a third tool in the set and the test went red. A count-based assertion would have absorbed a new false positive silently every time the corpus grew.
D-THE-NARRATED-WRITE-GUARD-COUNTS-ACKNOW.the_fix_and_its_measurement:
Excluded verbs that describe receiving rather than acting - noted, understood, reviewed, read, seen, heard, considered, checked, observed, noticed - as a negative lookahead, so it is a PREFIX guard and not a substring ban: 'I have updated the note you asked about' still fires, and a test pins that.

MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE 2656-TURN CORPUS BEFORE SHIPPING:
    before  9 fires across 3 tools (memory_forget, plan_keep_material, translation_job_control)
    after   8 fires across 2 tools (memory_forget, plan_keep_material)
Exactly the one false positive removed and every true positive kept. Verified on the deployed image: the acknowledgement returns False, 'I have cancelled the pending translation jobs' returns True.
D-THE-NARRATED-WRITE-GUARD-COUNTS-ACKNOW.what_it_does_not_cover: The verb list is a closed set chosen from ONE observed false positive plus its obvious neighbours. Another acknowledgement verb outside it would still fire. The calibration test is the thing that would catch it - which is the argument for keeping that test asserting tool NAMES rather than a count.

D-A-RECOGNISABLE-PLACEHOLDER-UUID-PASSES.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-26, batch c-owedheld1, K=5, 3 of 5 runs.
D-A-RECOGNISABLE-PLACEHOLDER-UUID-PASSES.what:
Asked to apply a plan on the confirmation turn, the model passed plan_bootstrap_apply a proposal_id it invented:

    77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777   (runs 0 and 1)
    78965432-1234-5678-90ab-cdef12345678   (run 3)

Both are syntactically valid UUIDs, so `_invented_supplier_ids` - whose test is SYNTACTIC - passed them through, `_missing_required_names` saw the argument as PRESENT, and the call was DISPATCHED to a Tier-A write tool.
D-A-RECOGNISABLE-PLACEHOLDER-UUID-PASSES.what_stopped_it: The SERVER's own scoping check, and its message is the good kind: 'no bootstrap proposal 77777777-... on this book - run plan_bootstrap_propose first and pass the proposal_id it returns (a proposal is book-scoped ...)'. D-A-RECOGNISABLE-PLACEHOLDER-UUID-PASSES.why_it_is_worth_filing_separately:
The syntactic blind spot is already recorded on D-SUPPLIER-RETURNS-COUNTS-NOT-THE-IDS-ITS-SUCCESSOR-NEEDS ('a syntactically valid placeholder is invisible to a guard whose test is syntactic'), where the invented value was 66966666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666. This measures the SAME blind spot on a different tool, a different argument, and with a SECOND pattern - so it is a class, not one tool's quirk:
    repeated-digit      77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777, 6696...6666
    sequential-hex      78965432-1234-5678-90ab-cdef12345678
Both are recognisable WITHOUT knowing any real id, which is what makes a detector plausible here where a general 'is this id real' test is impossible.
D-A-RECOGNISABLE-PLACEHOLDER-UUID-PASSES.candidate_direction_NOT_MEASURED: A shape test for degenerate UUIDs - one distinct hex digit across the whole value, or a run of sequential nibbles - beside the existing syntactic check. NOT measured and NOT recommended yet: its PRECISION against real platform ids is unknown, and this platform mints UUIDv7, whose leading timestamp bytes are highly ordered by construction. A sequential-nibble rule could plausibly fire on a genuine id minted in the same millisecond. That measurement is the next step, not the fix.

D-A-TIER-R-TOOL-WRITES-TO-THE-STORE.status: OPEN - BLOCKED on DQ-T45. Investigated 2026-08-26: the write is not an audit row, it is a LIFECYCLE TRANSITION into a status that gates a cost-bearing operation.
D-A-TIER-R-TOOL-WRITES-TO-THE-STORE.what:
plan_validate is declared Tier R - a READ - and the harness flagged 'READ-INTENT TURN WROTE TO THE STORE in 5/5 runs' on both builds. The store diff is loreweave_composition.plan_run: row count 1 -> 1, but `latest` advances during the turn. Only plan_validate and composition_package_tree ran, and package_tree is a pure read.

The tool's own description says what it does: 'run the S1-S8 golden linter (+ fidelity report)', and it returns a `fidelity_report_id` - so it PERSISTS a report. That may be entirely intended; what is not obviously intended is that a tool doing it is classified R, which is the tier that decides whether a turn needs a confirm card and whether a read-only turn is allowed to reach it.
D-A-TIER-R-TOOL-WRITES-TO-THE-STORE.not_yet_investigated: I have NOT read the write path or established whether any other Tier-R tool does this - so this is one measured instance, not a class. The next step is a sweep of Tier-R tools against store diffs, which the harness already computes.
D-A-TIER-R-TOOL-WRITES-TO-THE-STORE.measured_by: PlanForgeService.validate + authoring_run_service._APPROVED_PLAN_STATUSES; a sweep of 318 all-Tier-R turns across every batch; plan_run status census on the live store, 2026-08-26
D-A-TIER-R-TOOL-WRITES-TO-THE-STORE.investigated_2026_08_26:
The row admitted it had not read the write path. Read now, and it is worse than the row guessed. `plan_validate` (Tier R) calls TWO writes in PlanForgeService.validate:
    save_artifact(created_by, run_id, 'validation_report', report)   - the report
    if all_pass: update_run(book_id, run_id, status='validated')     - a STATE TRANSITION

🔴 AND THAT STATUS IS AN AUTHORISATION GATE. authoring_run_service.py:113 reads
    _APPROVED_PLAN_STATUSES = ('validated', 'compiled')
so a plan in 'validated' is authorised to start an autonomous authoring run - the multi-chapter drafting run that SPENDS LLM tokens. A tool the platform classifies as a READ moves a plan into the approved set.

WHAT TIER R MEANS HERE, from the SDK's own definition (sdks/go/loreweave_mcp/meta.go):
    R = read - no confirm, doesn't count against the write budget
    A = auto-commit + activity/Undo strip
So this transition needs no confirmation, is invisible to the write budget, AND never appears in the activity/Undo strip. The plan's status changes and the author has no record that it did.
D-A-TIER-R-TOOL-WRITES-TO-THE-STORE.the_sweep_the_row_asked_for:
'A sweep of Tier-R tools against store diffs' - run across all 1,360 recorded turns, restricted to the 318 turns where EVERY tool called was Tier R (any non-R tool would explain a write). Three distinct shapes came out, and only one is this defect:

  1. plan_run, 10x, tools {plan_validate, composition_package_tree} - THIS defect.
  2. entity_access_log, with glossary reads - an access AUDIT row. A read recording that it read is correct, and is NOT the same thing as advancing a lifecycle.
  3. extraction_pending, 32x, under tools that CANNOT enqueue extraction - jobs_list, tool_load, settings_list_models, registry_list_workflows, catalog_get_book. The common factor is the TURN, not the tool, so something outside the tool call writes it.

🔴 A CONFOUND WAS CHASED AND REFUTED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BELIEVED. The harness snapshots AFTER seeding (deliberately - its docstring says a seed inside the window would make every scenario report a change), but a seed's ASYNC tail could still land after the snapshot and read as a turn write. Tested by dating every write against fixture creation, which the UUIDv7 book_id encodes: the median gap is 15-40s and the MINIMUM across all tables is 10.5s, so no write sits in the seed's immediate wake. The writes happen during the turn.

D-THREE-KNOWLEDGE-SERVICE-GUARDS-ARE-RED.the_cause_of_each_and_they_pointed_the_S:
The row asks the right first question — 'whether the snapshot needs regenerating or a payload genuinely re-bloated, and the two answers point opposite ways'. Investigated one at a time; all three turned out to be the test, not the code:

  test_build_timeline_orders_and_maps — the fixture fed `valid_from`/`valid_to` and asserted they came back as the NARRATIVE interval. F3's ordinal model keeps that interval in `valid_from_ordinal`/`valid_to_ordinal`; the bare `valid_from` is a WALL-CLOCK datetime and `valid_to` is not a Neo4j property at all (temporal.py: an open fact stores valid_to_ordinal = NULL, and a grep finds no bare `valid_to` ever written). Commit 3dca8c87a moved the reader onto the ordinals — so this test had been asserting that the wall clock IS the ordinal, which is precisely the bug that commit fixed. Property names corrected; every assertion left as it was.

  test_kg_triage_list_default_is_bounded_and_summary — the SimpleNamespace fake was never given `sample_triage_id`, added to the grouped listing by 68464ea9b ('the triage listing told the agent to place an edge and gave it no id'). The handler raised AttributeError before reaching a single assertion. One field added to the fake.

  test_response_shapes_match_committed_snapshot — the same field reached TRIAGE_GROUP_REF_FIELDS and the committed snapshot was never regenerated.
D-THREE-KNOWLEDGE-SERVICE-GUARDS-ARE-RED.regenerating_the_snapshot_was_justified_:
This is the guard that exists to catch a re-bloated payload, so 'just regenerate it' is the exact move that would hide the thing it protects. Two checks before running it:

  IS THE FIELD A BODY OR A REFERENCE? The code's own comment answers: 'An id is a reference, not a body: §6b exists to hand back cheap ids the agent can act on. kg_triage_place_edge needs this one.' A single UUID per GROUP is the supplier-returns-its-successor's-id pattern this loop has spent cycles adding elsewhere — the opposite of a bloat.

  DID TWO WEEKS OF RED ACCUMULATE OTHER DRIFT? That was the real risk: a regeneration silently absorbing everything that changed while nobody was watching. The written diff is ONE LINE — `sample_triage_id` added to TRIAGE_GROUP_REF_FIELDS and nothing else. Nothing was absorbed.
D-THREE-KNOWLEDGE-SERVICE-GUARDS-ARE-RED.red_able: The two fixture repairs are self-falsifying — reverting either restores the exact failure quoted above. The one that needed proving is the SNAPSHOT, because a guard that is red is indistinguishable from a guard that is broken: with the fix in place, appending a synthetic field to MEMORY_SEARCH_REF_FIELDS makes it fail with 'ref-field set changed ... you likely re-bloated a summary payload'. It is protecting again, not merely green. Snapshot restored byte-identical (sha256 equal).
