D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.status: FIXED 2026-08-26 — `db: "neo4j"` now routes to cypher-shell, proven in both directions: a graph assertion PASSES when the fixture matches and REFUSES when it does not, which is the seed_assert's real job the row said was missing.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.what:
A scenario's `seed_assert` runs `psql` against a named Postgres database. Facts, entities and events live in NEO4J, so an assertion over them cannot be written: the harness refused the batch with 'db_query failed (neo4j): psql: error: ... database "neo4j" does not exist'.

THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND IS NOT THE DEFECT - a scenario whose assertion cannot execute measures nothing, and declining to start is the right call. The defect is that a whole class of seeded state cannot be preflighted at all, so a graph-seeded scenario runs with no guard that its seed landed.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.the_workaround_used: store_snapshot._neo4j already emits `neo4j.Fact.project` {rows, latest}, so the before/after Fact count IS in every run's store_diff and the falsifier can read it. That covers the count; it does not cover a seed_assert's real job, which is to refuse to START when the fixture is wrong.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.candidate_direction_NOT_MEASURED: seed_assert already dispatches on a `db` field; a 'neo4j' value could route to cypher-shell the way store_snapshot._neo4j already does, reusing that helper rather than adding a second way to reach the graph. Not built and not measured - the expect-value comparison for a Cypher scalar is the open question.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.measured_by: assert_seeded + preflight_seed_asserts exercised against the live graph, 2026-08-26; store_snapshot re-run through the unified reader
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.the_chokepoint_is_db_query_not_the_call_: The candidate direction was right and the placement mattered. Both seed-assert paths go through `oracle.db_query(c['db'], sql)` — `preflight_seed_asserts` (every query once, before the batch spends a turn) and `assert_seeded` (per-run, against the real fixture) — so the dispatch lives THERE. Routing at each call site would have been two chances to diverge, and the preflight is exactly the half that would have been forgotten.

D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.a_diagnosis_defect_found_by_exercising_t:
The first preflight run rejected a VALID query and blamed the JVM. cypher-shell prints four lines of 'WARNING: A restricted method in java.lang.System has been called' to stderr on every invocation, so a bare [:400] truncation showed only those — a syntax error in the caller's Cypher arrived as a Java module warning. Warnings are now stripped before the message is built:
    BEFORE: cypher_query failed: WARNING: A restricted method in java.lang.System ...
    AFTER : cypher_query failed: 42I06: syntax error ... Invalid input 'RETURN', expected: a parameter, '&', ')', ':', 'WHERE', '{' or '|'
This is the same class as the harness's own recorded lesson about an ExceptionGroup burying a clear server error — an instrument that reports the wrong cause costs more than one with no message.

    expect '999999' -> REFUSED: 'SEED ASSERTION FAILED: the seeded facts are present / expected 999999, store says 455'
preflight_seed_asserts, which is the half that runs before any turn is spent:
    valid Cypher  -> accepted

- READ-ONLY IS BY CONVENTION, NOT ENFORCED. `cypher_query` will happily run a write — nothing rejects a CREATE/MERGE the way a scenario author might assume. The Postgres side has the same property, so this is not a regression, but a seed_assert that mutates the graph would corrupt the very fixture it is checking.
- ONE CELL PER ROW. The parser returns each line as a single cell; a multi-column Cypher RETURN is not split the way psql's `-F|` splits columns. Every assertion this loop writes is a scalar, so it was not built — but a two-column query would silently come back joined.

D-THE-EMITTER-ARM-IS-UNREACHABLE-WITHOUT.what:
`argument_emitters` is read in TWO places and only ONE of them is reachable for most tools.

  R1 answerability transitivity - reads the map directly. Works for any tool.
  _missing_args_message's emitter sentence - lives inside the `owed` branch, which is entered only when declared_supplier(contract, arg) is 'context' or 'plan'. That reads a tool's `argument_supplier` member, and only 14 of the 316 federated tools carry a contract row at all.

So for ~300 tools a DECLARED emitter can never be named in a refusal. memory_forget is a measured instance: the emitter is declared and verified, and the refusal still reads 'The tool DOES declare what this is - fact_id: The id of the fact to invalidate. - so use that to obtain the real value and call again', which states WHAT the argument is and not WHERE to get it.
D-THE-EMITTER-ARM-IS-UNREACHABLE-WITHOUT.why_it_is_not_cosmetic: The two readers fail in different situations. R1 transitivity only expands from tools the request already made ANSWERABLE, so a tool reached by any other route - a rail, the hot seed, an explicit tool_load - gets no supplier forced onto the wire and a refusal that names none either. On c-forgetchain2 the chain closed via transitivity; the refusal contributed nothing.
D-THE-EMITTER-ARM-IS-UNREACHABLE-WITHOUT.candidate_direction_NOT_MEASURED: Name a declared emitter regardless of the `owed` branch - the map is the same structured source either way, and a declaration is a fact about the catalogue, not about who owes the value. NOT measured: whether that would change the model's behaviour where transitivity already surfaces the supplier is exactly the question a stripped-declaration control answered NO to once already this run, so the recall must be measured before it is recommended.

    93 declared (tool, arg) emitter pairs
    90 unreachable from a refusal (97%) - only 3 sit behind a contracts row whose

D-THE-MOTIF-LINK-SCENARIO-TIMES-OUT-6-OF.the_investigation_the_row_asked_for:
The row's own next step was 'the chat-service log for one timed-out session_id, not another batch'. Done, in three moves:

  1. THE OLD SESSIONS WERE UNREADABLE. Their logs had rotated (chat-service was restarted several times that day), so the store was asked instead: each timed-out session holds TWO user messages ~180s apart — the runner's retry, at exactly TURN_TIMEOUT — and ZERO assistant rows. The turn produced nothing, twice.

  2. REPRODUCED WITH THE LOG OPEN. K=2 passed 2/2, which proves only that it is stochastic; K=5 at the original concurrency errored 2 of 5.

  3. THE ERROR CHANGED SHAPE AND THAT WAS THE CLUE. This time it was HTTPStatusError 500, not ReadTimeout — and the log showed a duplicate-key violation on the message sequence after an interrupt-persist. Same cause, two presentations.
D-THE-MOTIF-LINK-SCENARIO-TIMES-OUT-6-OF.what_was_wrong_with_the_rows_own_theory:
The row suspected the approval loop ('it seeds two motifs and its recorded runs show up to 3 approval round-trips, so the approval loop is the obvious suspect - but that is a guess'). It was a guess and it was wrong: the failure needs only an ABORT followed by a RETRY on the same session. What made this scenario the one that surfaced it is that its turns are long enough to hit the timeout, and the runner retries — nothing about motifs or approvals.

So the 60% loss is real and the scenario is not at fault. Concurrency and turn-timeout changed nothing precisely because neither touches the race.
D-THE-MOTIF-LINK-SCENARIO-TIMES-OUT-6-OF.reopened_and_what_is_now_known:
Superseding this row was WRONG and the correction is the point. The investigation did find a real platform defect — the duplicate-key 500 on an aborted-then-retried turn — and that is fixed and separately confirmed (6 preconditions since deploy, 0 violations). But the ORIGINAL symptom is not that defect:

    c-motiflink10   3/5 errored (ReadTimeout)      before any fix
    c-motiflink11   3/5 errored (ReadTimeout)      concurrency 2, timeout 300
    c-motiflink13   2/5 errored (500 duplicate key) the race, reproduced with the log
    c-motiflink15   0/5 errored                     after the fix, concurrency 2
    c-motiflink16   2/5 errored (ReadTimeout)       after the fix, concurrency 3

So the scenario is still losing runs, to a hang that produces no assistant row and no duplicate key. What the race fix DID remove is the 500 presentation; what remains is the one this row was filed for.

NARROWED, which is progress: the timeouts are NOT the duplicate-key race, and they are not explained by concurrency either — c-motiflink11 failed 3/5 at concurrency 2 and c-motiflink15 was clean 5/5 at concurrency 2. The next probe should capture the chat-service log for a session that times out AFTER this fix, which no batch has yet done.
D-THE-MOTIF-LINK-SCENARIO-TIMES-OUT-6-OF.the_rate_measured_before_and_after:
Same scenario, same prompt, same approvals; four post-fix batches:

    BEFORE   c-motiflink10  3/5   ReadTimeout, concurrency 3
             c-motiflink11  3/5   ReadTimeout, concurrency 2, turn-timeout 300
                            ----  6/10 = 60%
    AFTER    c-motiflink15  0/5   concurrency 2
             c-motiflink16  2/5   concurrency 3
             c-motiflink17  0/5   concurrency 3
             c-motiflink18  0/5   concurrency 3
                            ----  2/20 = 10%

Fisher exact, two-tailed: p = 0.007. So fixing the aborted-turn sequence race removed most of this, which is NOT what the previous entry concluded — that entry saw one post-fix batch come back 2/5 and said the timeouts were untouched. Four batches say they were mostly touched. One batch is not a rate.
D-THE-MOTIF-LINK-SCENARIO-TIMES-OUT-6-OF.what_i_set_out_to_do_and_did_not:
The row's next step was 'the chat-service log for a session that times out AFTER the fix'. I ran two batches with `docker logs -f` capturing throughout and BOTH came back 0/5 — the residual is now rare enough that catching one is a lottery. So the log for a post-fix timeout still does not exist, and the cause of the remaining 10% is still unknown.

Recorded rather than retried indefinitely: at a 10% rate, an expected ~10 more runs per capture, and a scenario batch is not a cheap way to buy one. A cheaper instrument would be a standing log filter that keeps only sessions with no assistant row.
D-THE-MOTIF-LINK-SCENARIO-TIMES-OUT-6-OF.what_is_NOT_covered:
- THE RESIDUAL CAUSE IS UNKNOWN. Not the duplicate-key race (fixed and separately confirmed), and not concurrency: c-motiflink11 failed 3/5 at concurrency 2 while c-motiflink15 was clean 5/5 at the same setting.
- 20 POST-FIX RUNS IS NOT MANY for a 10% rate. The confidence interval on 2/20 is wide; what is solid is the DIFFERENCE from 60%, not the precise residual.

D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACH.status: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-26 - a DUPLICATE of D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-BY-CONSTRUCTION, which established the same mechanism on the SAME tool on 2026-08-23.
D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACH.what:
R1 answerability's whole promise is that a tool whose OWN declared vocabulary answers the request reaches the wire. For glossary_book_sync_apply it matched, logged the match, logged NO skip reason, and the tool is still absent from the final advertised surface.

The prompt contains its declared synonym verbatim ('Apply the standard updates'). Confirmed three ways:
  * answerable_tools(), called inside the DEPLOYED chat-service container against the live catalogue, returns glossary_book_sync_apply as answerable.
  * the service log: 'R1 answerability: request matches [book_steering_list, glossary_book_sync_apply, glossary_book_sync_available]', on every session.
  * the service's OWN advertised log, emitted AFTER the surface builder returns, lists 34 activated tools including glossary_book_sync_AVAILABLE and NOT glossary_book_sync_APPLY.

The forcing loop has exactly three skip branches - suppressed by a loop breaker, absent from the turn's catalog, and wrong tier under ask/plan mode - and EVERY one of them logs. None fired. So the tool was dropped by a path that says nothing.
D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACH.why_it_matters: R1 is the mechanism this loop has leaned on repeatedly - it is what makes a declared emitter reach the wire, and several fixes are built on that guarantee. A silent hole in it means those fixes hold only where nothing else drops the tool, and nobody would see the difference: the log says 'matched' and the tool simply is not there.
D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACH.not_investigated: WHERE the drop happens. `_add()` has two silent early returns (a falsy td, and a name already seen) and neither should fire here, so the drop is likely further downstream - a budget or a filter applied between the builder and the wire. Settling it means instrumenting the path, not another batch.
D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACH.measured_by: docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/c-booksync1.json; answerable_tools() in the deployed container; chat-service advertised log, 2026-08-26
D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACH.narrowed_by_reading_the_path_2026_08_26:
Traced as far as reading can take it, and the drop is genuinely silent:
  * The 'request matches' log lives INSIDE _advertise_discovery_tools (line 1838, def at 1696), so the DISCOVERY path demonstrably ran - the tool did not fall down the plain-path branch that has no R1 forcing at all.
  * The forcing loop is at 1894, after that log, and its three skip branches all log. Counted across the whole 40-minute window: ZERO 'NOT forced' lines, zero catalog_miss, zero permission_tier. So _add(_ans_td) was reached.
  * `advertised` at the log site (4534) is the list ITERATED to build the SSE payload - it is the wire, not an activation registry - and it is emitted long after the builder returns at 1953. The tool is absent from it on all five sessions.
  * The breaker de-advertise filter that could remove it (4312) is in the ELSE branch, the plain path, which this turn did not take.

So: added, and gone by the time the surface is sent, with nothing in between that says so. The next step is a counter or a log at the point `out` becomes `advertised`, not another batch and not more reading - which is why this is recorded rather than guessed at.
D-R1-MATCHED-THE-TOOL-AND-IT-NEVER-REACH.withdrawn_because:
🔴 I FILED THIS AS A NEW DEFECT AND IT WAS ALREADY ON THE LEDGER. Same tool (glossary_book_sync_apply), same symptom (R1 matches, the tool is absent from the wire), same cause - two advertise sites handed two DIFFERENT catalogues, the per-pass one built from a catalog the tool was already filtered out of.

The standing rule is explicit that a defect must not be split to inflate the count, so this row is withdrawn rather than kept as a sibling. What the investigation ADDED is folded into the original row: a live re-confirmation, and permanent observability that turned a multi-hour trace into two log lines.

WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE FIRST: searched the ledger for the tool NAME before opening a row. The existing row names glossary_book_sync_apply in its own `measured` field.

    both               : 2 rows

Every one of the five was written by me, in this run, under a name I invented without checking what the reader looked for. D-THE-RESUME-POINTER-AIMS-AT-A-BLOCKED-R.what_it_actually_broke:
Two things, both silent, and both are things this run steers by:

  THE POINTER. NEXT aimed at D-RESTORE-WITH-NO-WAY-TO-SEE-WHAT-IS-RESTORABLE, blocked on DQ-T44, and all three QUEUE rows it displayed were blocked (T44/T45/T31) while SEVEN unblocked contract rows existed. I derived them by hand and only then noticed the pointer was wrong.

  THE STOP CONDITION. `--check` ends the entire run when every open contract row is DQ-blocked. Under-counting blocked rows means that condition can never be reached honestly - the run would be told to keep going by an instrument that cannot see the blocks. A goal whose terminating check is blind to five of its own blocks is a goal that cannot end.

It also inflated my own working count all session: I reported 17, 15 and 14 actionable contract defects in successive cycles. The true figure was 7. Every one of those numbers was derived with a filter that read only `dq`, so it missed the rows blocked under the OTHER name - the same mistake in the mirror.

  * dq_alias_drift() reports any row blocked under an alias
  * cmd_audit REFUSES on one, printing the row and the field to rename TO

It does NOT auto-migrate, deliberately: a row rewritten by a tool is a row nobody re-read, and that judgement earned its keep immediately - one of the seven held a SENTENCE under the marker's name ('DQ-T32 asks whether to relax the matcher, and how'), not an id. The row guessed 'a chat-session side effect ... that is a guess; it was not traced'. The guess was right and is now traced.

It is ASYNCHRONOUS, which explains the 1-of-5 shape the row flagged as 'exactly the shape of a race': the enqueue sometimes lands before the run's `after` snapshot and sometimes after it.

D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.status: FIXED - proven on the deployed build in BOTH directions: the measured call is refused with an actionable message, and the path that works is untouched.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.what:
kg_add_nodes mode=from_glossary was called with entity_ids=['Mira Solene', 'Aldric Vane'] - NAMES, where the argument takes glossary entity UUIDs. The tool returned:
    ok: true, nodes: [], entities_seen: 0, nodes_created: 0, nodes_existing: 0
and the activity strip recorded 'Did kg_add_nodes'. A call that matched nothing, created nothing and touched nothing is reported to the model, and to the human's activity feed, as a completed write.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.why_it_matters: The model has no way to tell this apart from a real projection. Its next move assumes two nodes exist. `entities_seen: 0` is the tool's own evidence that the argument matched nothing - it is IN the payload and nothing acts on it. This is the same shape as an unconditional success that discards its own signal.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.the_two_halves: (1) A zero-match from_glossary should say so - 'none of the 2 entity_ids matched a glossary entity in this book' - rather than ok:true with empty counts. (2) The arg description reads 'mode=from_glossary: optional specific glossary entity ids; omit for the whole active glossary' and never says they are UUIDs, nor where to get them (glossary_search / glossary_propose_entities return them). A name is the obvious thing to pass.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.not_investigated: Whether the omit-entirely path (no entity_ids, 'the whole active glossary') works - it was never exercised, and it is the path that would have projected both characters in one call.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.measured_by: direct MCPDirect probe of both directions against the deployed build, 2026-08-26; the original observation in docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/c-kgedge3.json
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.the_fix_is_narrow_and_the_narrowness_is_:
The predicate is 'the caller NAMED entity_ids AND none of them matched', not 'nothing was projected'. Omitting entity_ids means 'the whole active glossary', and a book whose glossary is genuinely empty is a legitimate no-op - that is ALSO the route measured working end to end in c-kgedge4 (entities_seen 2, both nodes created, edge parked, 5/5). Refusing on a bare zero would have closed this row by breaking the only path that succeeds, which is the kind of fix this loop exists to catch.

The PARTIAL match gets a note rather than a refusal: naming five ids and matching three is the same defect in miniature - a cheerful success that never mentions the two which do not exist - but three real nodes WERE created and refusing would throw them away.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.also_fixed_the_argument_that_invited_the: The description read 'mode=from_glossary: optional specific glossary entity ids; omit for the whole active glossary'. It never said they are UUIDs, and never said where one comes from - so a NAME is the obvious thing to pass, and the model passed two. It now leads with the easier and usually-correct route (omit it) and says the ids are glossary entity UUIDs from glossary_search, not names.

  A) THE MEASURED DEFECT - entity_ids=['Mira Solene','Aldric Vane']:
     REFUSED: 'none of the 2 entity_ids matched a glossary entity in this book, so nothing was projected and the graph is unchanged. `entity_ids` takes glossary entity UUIDs, not names - get them from glossary_search, or omit the argument entirely to project the book's whole active glossary.'
     Before: ok:true, nodes:[], entities_seen:0, nodes_created:0, and 'Did kg_add_nodes' in the activity strip.

  B) THE RECALL CONTROL - entity_ids omitted, on a project whose glossary is empty:
     OK, entities_seen=0, nodes_created=0 - NOT refused, because no ids were named. This is the case that would have caught a too-wide predicate, and it is the reason it was run.

services/knowledge-service/tests/unit/test_a_projection_that_matched_nothing_is_not_a_success.py, 10 guards including a four-case truth table that drives the REAL handler. Inverse edit - the guard disabled with `if False and ...` - reds the measured case; source restored byte-identical.

D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.status: FIXED - proven live 2026-08-26, batch c-kgedge4, K=5: the turn completes end to end on 5 of 5 runs (0 of 5 the batch before). Two id families, a description that named neither, and a recovery path that named a DEAD tool.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.what:
A GLOSSARY entity id and a graph `:Entity` NODE id are different objects with the same shape and the same name. kg_propose_edge's arguments are `source_entity_id` / `target_entity_id`, described as 'The id of the relationship's source entity.' - and it requires NODE ids: existing_entity_node_ids matches on Entity.id and KG_ENDPOINT_NOT_NODE rejects anything else.

Measured: on 3 of 3 edge calls the model passed the GLOSSARY entity ids, matched exactly against the run's own seed_ids (glossary_propose_entities.results[N].entity_id). Well-formed UUIDs, real objects, wrong family.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.why_it_matters: This is the root of D-A-TWO-ENDPOINT-EDGE-NEEDS-N-SEQUENTIAL-CONFIRM-CARDS and it survives every fix aimed at the card cost. Cheapening the node-creation path does not help a caller who does not know it needs to create a node at all - it HAS an 'entity id' and the argument asks for one.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.candidate_directions_NOT_MEASURED: (a) name the argument for what it is (source_node_id), which is a breaking rename of a published tool; (b) say it in the description - 'a graph NODE id from kg_add_nodes or kg_graph_query, NOT a glossary entity id' - and declare the emitter, which the emitter-arm fix now makes sayable in a refusal; (c) ACCEPT a glossary entity id and project it, which turns a rejection into the one-call path the model keeps reaching for. Each is a different owner-level trade and none is measured.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.measured_by: docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/c-kgedge4.json vs c-kgedge3.json (K=5 each); chat_messages.tool_calls + withheld_tools; drop_superseded_tools source, 2026-08-26
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.the_second_half_was_worse_than_the_first:
🔴 THE PLATFORM'S OWN REMEDY NAMED A TOOL THE TURN CANNOT SEE. KG_ENDPOINT_NOT_NODE said 'project the glossary entities into the graph first (kg_project_entities_to_nodes)'. That tool is `visibility: legacy` — and on 2026-08-25 drop_superseded_tools was WIDENED to drop every legacy tool from every turn catalogue unconditionally ('a legacy tool is a DEAD tool'), not just those whose replacement is on the same wire. Measured over batch c-kgedge3, from chat_messages.withheld_tools: withheld on 5 of 5 runs, at stages `superseded` AND `domain_not_selected`.

So the sentence the runtime emits when a caller gets this exact thing wrong instructed the model to call something provably absent from its wire. Naming a tool is also what ARMS it onto the turn, so an unreachable name arms nothing: the refusal was not merely unhelpful, it consumed the one mechanism that could have helped.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.the_fix_three_surfaces_one_cause:

D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.status: FIXED - deployed and verified by content 2026-08-26. The scenario that lost 60% of its runs is clean 5/5, and 6 aborted turns since deploy produced ZERO duplicate-key 500s.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.what:
Posting a message allocates its position with a READ-THEN-WRITE and no lock:
    seq = SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sequence_num),0)+1 FROM chat_messages WHERE session_id=$1 AND branch_id=0
    INSERT INTO chat_messages (... sequence_num ...) VALUES (... seq ... 0 ...)
and `idx_chat_messages_branch_unique` is UNIQUE on (session_id, sequence_num, branch_id). Two concurrent writers therefore compute the same number and one gets a 500.

The second writer is the platform's own: when a client aborts a turn, stream_service DETACHES the persist — 'interrupt-persist detached for session ... (write continues after cancel)' — and then writes the interrupted assistant reply. A client that retries the aborted turn races that detached write.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.measured:
Reproduced 2026-08-26, batch c-motiflink13, 2 of 5 runs, with the chat-service log open. The sequence in one session:
    POST /messages -> 200 OK, turn starts
    interrupt-persist detached for session 01a03eaa-823b-... (write continues after cancel)
    terminal-persist: saved interrupted assistant reply ... 0 chars, outcome=abandoned_by_user
    POST /messages (the retry) -> 500
    duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_chat_messages_branch_unique"
    DETAIL: Key (session_id, sequence_num, branch_id)=(01a03eaa-..., 2, 0) already exists.
The interrupted assistant row took position 2; the retry's user message computed 2 as well.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.why_it_matters:
This is what a user does when a reply is slow: stop it and ask again. The second ask 500s. It needs no harness and no unusual client — only an abort followed by a retry on the same session, which is the ordinary shape of impatience.

It also corrupts MEASUREMENT wherever it happens, because the two presentations look like different problems: the retry either 500s (HTTPStatusError) or hangs behind the same contention (ReadTimeout). The instrument row this was traced from recorded the second shape for weeks as 'the scenario times out'.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.the_mechanism_does_NOT_exist: Checked before proposing one: there is NO advisory lock anywhere in chat-service (`pg_advisory` appears zero times), and the enclosing `conn.transaction()` does not help — under READ COMMITTED two transactions read the same MAX quite happily. Five other sites derive a sequence the same way (stream_service x3, voice_stream_service x2), so a fix at one call site would leave the class open.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.candidate_direction_NOT_YET_MEASURED: A per-session advisory lock taken inside the existing transaction (pg_advisory_xact_lock on the session id) serialises allocation and releases at commit, with no migration and no schema change. The alternatives — retry-on-unique-violation, or a real per-session sequence — are heavier and one of them still needs the lock to be correct.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.measured_by: docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/c-motiflink13.json (reproduction with the log), c-motiflink14.json (my broken SQL), c-motiflink15.json (0/5 errors); chat-service log counts since deploy, 2026-08-26
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.the_fix:
`app/db/message_sequence.py::next_sequence_num` takes a per-session advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock on hashtextextended(session_id, namespace)) and then reads MAX+1. The lock is held to COMMIT, so allocation and the INSERT that uses it are one indivisible step for a session; different sessions never contend.

Applied to the THREE allocation sites that already run inside a transaction — the message endpoint (the retry's user insert) and stream_service's two persist paths (the detached writer). A retry-on-unique-violation was rejected: it papers over the race while leaving two writers free to interleave, where the lock asserts the property the unique index is already claiming.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.what_is_deliberately_NOT_converted:
The two VOICE sites (voice_stream_service:313 and :625) acquire a connection WITHOUT a transaction. pg_advisory_xact_lock there would be taken and released by its own statement — protecting nothing while looking protected, which is worse than no lock at all. So next_sequence_num REFUSES outside a transaction rather than degrading, and those two sites keep the old unlocked read: they carry the SAME race and are named here rather than silently half-fixed. Converting them means wrapping voice persistence in a transaction, a behaviour change on a surface this defect was never measured on.

A sixth MAX(sequence_num) read in stream_service is a cadence CLOCK, not an allocation, and is correctly untouched.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.the_first_fix_was_worse_than_the_defect:
🔴 IT SHIPPED BROKEN SQL AND 3,608 GREEN TESTS COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT. The first version called `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0), $2)` — a bigint AND an int — where Postgres has only `(key bigint)` or `(key1 int4, key2 int4)`. Every message POST then failed with `function pg_advisory_xact_lock(bigint, unknown) does not exist`: batch c-motiflink14, 5 of 5 runs, 0 tools called. Strictly worse than the defect it replaced.

The whole chat suite was green through it and always would have been: every test of this path uses a FAKE connection, so not one of 3,608 assertions executes a character of the SQL. Verifying the statement against the real database costs two seconds and is the only thing that could have caught it — which is now a test.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.proof:
Deployed, container/host sha256 equal on all three files.

  BATCH, same scenario/concurrency/timeout as the failing ones:
    c-motiflink10   3/5 errored (ReadTimeout)
    c-motiflink11   3/5 errored (ReadTimeout, concurrency 2, timeout 300)
    c-motiflink13   2/5 errored (500 duplicate key) - reproduced with the log open
    c-motiflink14   5/5 errored - MY broken SQL
    c-motiflink15   0/5 errored, 5/5 called

  INDEPENDENT OF THE BATCH, from the service's own log in the 25 minutes after deploy:
    6  'interrupt-persist detached' events — the race's precondition, six times
    0  duplicate-key violations on idx_chat_messages_branch_unique
That second measurement is the stronger one: it counts the precondition occurring rather than hoping a batch reproduces it.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.red_able:
services/chat-service/tests/test_the_sequence_lock_is_real_sql.py, 4 guards run against the REAL database: the statement is valid SQL, the WRONG overload genuinely fails (anti-vacuity — if both spellings worked the first test would prove nothing), two concurrent allocators for the same session SERIALISE (the second blocks until the first commits), and calling it outside a transaction RAISES.

The gate judged `prompt`. fe_runner measures `turns[-1]` and says so in a comment: 'THE LAST TURN IS THE MEASURED ONE'. For a scenario with follow_ups the first turn is SETUP — very often a read that supplies the id the write needs — and no bar ever reads it.

Re-derived over the 78 Tier-A/W scenarios that declare follow_ups:

    judging the FIRST turn (what shipped)   61 offenders
    judging the MEASURED turn (correct)      1 offender

59 of the 60 seeded as debt were never offenders. Their measured turn asks for the tool's action, exactly as intended — 'Cancel that job.' after 'What is the status of the translation job?'. The single survivor is single-turn and genuine: scenarios-batch10.json::composition-error-block-edit asks 'What passages have I flagged as problems in this book?' of a Tier-A EDIT tool.

HOW IT WAS CAUGHT, which is the part worth keeping: the gate fired on a scenario THIS LOOP ADDED HOURS LATER for an unrelated defect (scenarios-c-surfrec2.json, a verbatim copy of an existing two-turn scenario). A wrong bar that only ever sees old data stays green forever; this one met a new input and failed on it. The suite run is what surfaced it, not a review.

DQ-T1.question: What is `entity_lifecycle_ledger` for, and what should write it? Options seen, none chosen: (a) every status transition (approve/retire/reject via glossary_propose_curation) appends a row, making the ledger the audit trail its columns describe; (b) it is delete/restore-only by design and the column set is aspirational; (c) it is superseded by entity_revisions and should be dropped.
DQ-T1.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13. The table exists with an append-only trigger guard (`entity_lifecycle_ledger_append_only`) and columns op, prior_status, new_status, actor_type, actor_id, reason — the exact vocabulary of a curation status change. It holds THREE rows, all from 2026-08-11, all op='deleted'/'restored', and all with prior_status and new_status NULL. A repo-wide search for 'lifecycle_ledger' finds NOTHING in source, and the only database function referencing it is the append-only guard. Four entities were moved draft -> active live in this cycle and the ledger gained no rows. So it is a table with a guard, no writer, and a column set that describes a transition nobody records. Whether curation SHOULD write it is a product decision about what the audit trail is for, not something measurement can settle.
DQ-T1.recommendation: RECOMMEND (a) - every status transition appends. Not because the ledger is used, but because somebody paid for an append-only TRIGGER on it: that is a deliberate integrity guarantee, and a guarded table holding three rows from a single day is the shape that later gets read as an audit trail it never was. (c) drop-it is the honest alternative and is cheaper; what makes it the wrong DEFAULT is that the columns (op, prior_status, new_status, actor_type, actor_id, reason) already describe the curation transition exactly, so the intent is not in doubt. Decide (c) only after checking for readers - if anything reads it today, (c) is a silent capability loss.
DQ-T1.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.

DQ-T2.question: Should a deprecated tool be required to name a replacement, and what replaces the ones that have none? Options seen, none chosen: (a) superseded_by becomes mandatory for visibility=legacy and the 55 gaps are filled; (b) a retired-with-no-successor tool is legitimate and tool_list's description should stop promising a label; (c) those 55 are not actually deprecated and the visibility tag is wrong.
DQ-T2.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13 against the live federated catalogue. 117 tools carry _meta.visibility='legacy'; 62 carry superseded_by and 55 DO NOT, spread across five services (glossary 28, book 11, kg 11, lore 4, composition 1). tool_list's own description says 'deprecated tools are labeled with their replacement', so for 47% of them there is no label. Observed live in session 019ff9f0: asked what replaced book_get, the model built an accurate migration table for the tools that name a successor and could say nothing actionable about book_create, book_chapter_delete, book_purge or book_set_cover. This is not tool_list's defect - it reports the _meta each provider federates faithfully - and whether a retired tool HAS a successor is a product decision per tool, not something measurement can settle.
DQ-T2.recommendation: RECOMMEND (a) - superseded_by mandatory for visibility=legacy, the 55 gaps filled, enforced by a lint. tool_list's own description PROMISES the label, and 55 of 117 legacy tools do not carry it, so the promise is false for nearly half of them. (b) 'stop promising it' is internally consistent but trades a fixable data gap for a permanent capability loss - the successor is exactly what a model needs when it lands on a legacy tool. The enforcement shape already exists: scripts/lint_superseded_synonyms.py fails the pair at build.
DQ-T2.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.

DQ-T3.question: Should tool_list tell the model that world-setup tools exist but are withheld? Options seen, none chosen: (a) stamp them the way T7-D2 stamps always-on tools, naming the gate and how to open it; (b) keep them wholly invisible, since naming a tool the model cannot call is the retry loop N5a-FULL exists to stop; (c) widen the exemption so a direct request counts as setup intent.
DQ-T3.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13. filter_intent_gated_setup_tools drops five glossary tools (adopt_standards, propose_kinds, plan, propose_batch, book_sync_apply) at catalog assembly unless the glossary_shaping skill is injected or a pinned rail names them - so they are un-seeded, un-findable AND un-loadable. That is deliberate (N5a-FULL, the confirmed over-reach) and it IS instrumented via record_surface_withheld(stage='intent_gate'), but only into telemetry the model never sees: from the model's side they are indistinguishable from tools that do not exist. The gate's own docstring records the cost of the opposite error - guidance naming a tool the capability floor had made unreachable produced 40,597 characters of one repeated paragraph before the author hit Stop. So both directions have a measured failure and the choice is a product decision.
DQ-T3.decision: ANSWERED 2026-08-14 by the owner: option (a) — stamp withheld tools the way T7-D2 stamps always-on ones, naming the gate and how to open it. NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS IT: three prose interventions were measured this session and none moved tool_list off 0/3, so the prior is against prose working here. Build it and MEASURE it; if the measurement refuses it, say so rather than shipping it.
DQ-T3.recommendation: RECOMMEND (b) - keep them wholly invisible, and fix the GATE instead (DQ-T31). Naming a tool the model cannot call is the retry loop N5a-FULL exists to stop. The reason a user's request cannot reach an intent-gated tool is not that the tool is hidden; it is that the gate keys on vocabulary rather than on what was asked. Fix that and (a) stops being needed. DECIDE THESE TWO TOGETHER: (b) here is only defensible if T31 gets its declaration arm - otherwise the tools are both unreachable and unmentioned.
DQ-T3.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.

DQ-T4.question: Should glossary-service's non-ambient tools DECLARE book_id required, or should they BECOME ambient? Options seen, none chosen: (a) declare required, as T10-D1 did for the three legacy entity-detail reads - honest, zero behaviour change; (b) tag them WithAmbientBook and switch to bookToolAuthAmbient, so a model inside a book studio may omit book_id exactly as it can for glossary_get_entity and glossary_search; (c) per-tool, on whether the tool is reachable from a studio surface at all.
DQ-T4.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13 against the live federated catalogue and confirmed over the wire. 46 glossary tools declare book_id; 6 pair an optional book_id with WithAmbientBook (correct), and 40 declared it optional WITHOUT the tag - the pairing bookToolAuthAmbient's own comment forbids. T10-D1 fixed 3 of them (the shared bookEntityToolIn struct), leaving 37, which TestTheAmbientResidueIsStatedNotSilent logs BY NAME so the number cannot quietly grow. Sampled 4 of the 37 from different files (list_unknown_entities, list_merge_candidates, book_sync_available, entity_get_genres): every one answers 'book_id must be a UUID' when it is omitted, so the declaration is wrong for all of them, not just the three. Which way to correct it is a product decision about whether the studio's ambient binding SHOULD reach these tools - measurement can show the contradiction but not which side is intended.
DQ-T4.recommendation: RECOMMEND (a) - declare book_id REQUIRED on the 37 remaining. Zero behaviour change, it makes the wire honest, and it is the same fix T10-D1 already applied to three of them, so both the precedent and the shape are settled. (b) ambient-ify is the better END state for tools genuinely reachable from a studio surface, but it is a per-tool behaviour change across 37 tools and must not ride along on a declaration cleanup. Do (a) now, then (c) deliberately and per-tool.
DQ-T4.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.

DQ-T5.question: How does a NEW book get its first glossary entity? Options seen, none chosen: (a) let a refusal UNLOCK the tool it names for the rest of the turn, the way a pinned rail's step tools are already exempted from the intent gate; (b) make the router inject glossary_shaping on prose like 'set up my book, adopt the standard lore categories', which it does not today; (c) let glossary_ontology_upsert create a kind that is actually usable (with a display attribute), so the non-gated path works end to end; (d) bootstrap a default ontology with the book, the way a knowledge project is already bootstrapped 197ms after creation (OBS-T17).
DQ-T5.evidence: Measured live 2026-08-13 across sessions 019ffa85, 019ffa92 and 019ffa96 on a throwaway book, with every branch tried. A fresh book has no kinds, so glossary_propose_entities refuses. Its remedy, glossary_adopt_standards, is intent-gated and was recorded WITHHELD at stage=intent_gate in the same turn as the refusal that named it - and stayed withheld even on the explicit prose 'Set up my book - adopt the standard lore categories for it'. The non-gated alternative, glossary_ontology_upsert, DOES create the kind (confirmed in the store) but the kind has no display attribute, so the propose is correctly refused with 'refusing to create a nameless entity'; adding a name attribute through the same tool returned ok and changed nothing - the retry produced a byte-identical refusal. Both directions have a measured cost: opening the gate re-admits the over-reach N5a-FULL exists to stop (its docstring records 40,597 characters of one repeated paragraph before the author hit Stop), and leaving it shut means the glossary has no entry point for a new book. Measurement can show the contradiction; it cannot choose which side is intended.
DQ-T5.recommendation: RECOMMEND (a) - a refusal UNLOCKS the tool it names, for the rest of that turn. The platform already does exactly this for a pinned rail's step tools, so the mechanism exists and only its trigger is new; and a refusal naming its own remedy is the strongest evidence of intent available - the system itself just said which tool is needed. It is reactive rather than pre-emptive, which is the pattern that has held up elsewhere here. (b) widens a phrase list and leaves the class; (c) and (d) fix the bootstrap for one path and leave the gate wrong.
DQ-T5.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.

DQ-T6.question: Should the hot-seed budget be allowed to advertise a domain's WRITE tools while dropping its primary READ tool? NOTE: this is about what a plain request LANDS ON, not about reachability — a budget-dropped tool is still reachable via tool_list -> tool_load, proven 2026-08-13. Options seen, none chosen: (a) reserve a slot for each domain's read tools before any write is seeded; (b) spend the budget by RELEVANCE to the turn's request rather than by domain order; (c) raise or scale the 2000-token hot-seed budget; (d) treat a read/write imbalance in a seeded domain as a loud failure rather than silently seeding whatever fits.
DQ-T6.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13 across four attempts on two surfaces. Asked in plain prose to read a chapter, the model never called book_read; it called book_chapter_save_draft. On the BOOK STUDIO surface the runtime recorded book_read withheld with reason 'did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)', and the book tools it DID advertise were book_chapter_save_draft and book_update_details — both writes. On the universal surface book_read was withheld as domain_not_selected and then token_budget, and never advertised at all. This is the causal explanation for three separate write-for-read substitutions recorded the same day (OBS-T16, OBS-T22, OBS-T28), one of which overwrote a real chapter's prose with 'This is a test.' and was only recoverable because the write had snapshotted first. The tool itself is fine — called directly it returns faithful data. Which way to fix the budget is a product decision about how the hot set is spent; measurement can show the imbalance but not the intended policy. SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-08-13 (cycle 22, session 019ffaf4): asked to suggest arc structures for a named BOOK, the turn's hot domain was selected as `knowledge`, and composition_arc_suggest was withheld at stage=domain_not_selected with reason 'domain not in this turn's hot set (knowledge)'. The model then called load_skill('composition') TEN times without reaching any composition tool. So the pattern is not book-service-specific: on both services the surfacing layer, not the tool, is what stops a plain request from being served — once by spending the hot-seed budget on writes (book_read), once by selecting a domain the request never mentioned. THIRD AND SHARPEST MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-13 (cycle 25): retested on the EDITOR surface — the one stream_service documents as seeding 'glossary + composition + book tools hot' — a single turn advertised only 4 of composition's 107 tools, withheld 49 more with 'did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)', and withheld the rest as domain_not_selected. All four tools this loop needed (arc_suggest, arc_template_get, get_outline_node, get_derivative_context) were in the budget-dropped set, and each is verified correct under direct exercise. So the constraint is the 2000-token hot-seed budget itself: on the surface built for authoring, a 107-tool domain gets 4 slots, and which 4 is decided by fit rather than by what the author asked for. CORRECTION 2026-08-13: a budget-dropped tool is NOT unreachable — asked to load it by name, the model runs tool_load and calls it successfully, which is the designed lazy-tail path. Four composition tools and book_read were all recorded BLOCKED on this misreading and are now PROVEN. What remains real, and is what this DQ is about, is the CONSEQUENCE of the seeding choice: on the editor surface the budget advertised book_chapter_save_draft and book_update_details while dropping book_read, and a model asked four separate times to READ reached for a WRITE instead — once overwriting a real chapter's prose. The tools were reachable; nothing in the turn told the model so.
DQ-T6.recommendation: RECOMMEND (b) - spend the hot-seed budget by RELEVANCE to the request, not by domain order. The platform has already committed to this principle one stage later: R1 answerability exists to force a tool whose declared vocabulary answers the request onto the wire 'whatever the budget, the domain selection or the rail decided'. (b) applies that same rule at seeding time, so it removes the need for the rescue instead of adding a second mechanism beside it. (a) fixes the measured case and not the class; (c) raising the budget buys time and changes nothing structural.
DQ-T6.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.
DQ-T6.evidence_2026_08_23:
FOUR NEW INSTANCES, AND THEY DO NOT SUPPORT THIS DQ'S FRAMING - recorded because a DQ strengthened with the wrong evidence is worse than one left alone.

This DQ asks whether the hot-seed budget should advertise a domain's WRITE tools while dropping its primary READ. Four tools blocked on 2026-08-23 all failed because a required id's supplier was on no pass of the wire, which looks like the same thing. It is not. Two of the four pairs are Tier A consumer <- Tier R supplier and fit the framing; the other two are Tier A <- Tier A (plan_bootstrap_apply <- plan_bootstrap_propose) and Tier R <- Tier R (composition_arc_template_get <- composition_arc_template_list), and neither is a read losing to a write.

What the four share is DEPTH, not tier: the request's words select one tool and nothing carries its prerequisites. See D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-THE-MODEL-CANNOT-GET. The recommendation on this DQ - spend the budget by relevance rather than domain order - is unchanged and still stands on its own 2026-08-13 measurement (book_read withheld for budget while two book WRITES were advertised).

DQ-T30.question: When a rail is DONE, what re-reads the data? A completed rail correctly stops driving, and the model then answers data questions from conversation memory — which goes stale the moment anything changes outside the chat. MEASURED 2026-08-13: with two rules in the store, a re-ask returned 'one rule' (the count from the earlier turn); told a rule had been added, the model claimed 'I have checked your consistency rules again' with ZERO tool calls and INVENTED a plausible rule paraphrased from the chapter prose in place of the real one. Options seen, none chosen: (a) a rail step whose tool is a READ never latches done, so a re-ask always re-drives; (b) a freshness window — a read step older than N minutes is re-actionable; (c) a turn-level rule that a question naming stored data must be answered from a tool call in THIS turn, independent of any rail. (c) is the general fix and the most expensive.
DQ-T30.evidence: Session 019ff929, book 019ff8f5, 2026-08-13 14:0x-14:2x. Store: 2 active canon_rule rows ('Sat khi luon tieu hao tuoi tho — magic always costs lifespan', 'The Obsidian Trench never appears on two maps at once'). Turn A (rail drove): tool called, answer correct. Turn B (canon-check now 3/3, 'guards held but no actionable step'): no tool call, answered 'one rule'. Turn C: no tool call, answered with the real first rule plus a FABRICATED second one, 'The world is constantly rewriting itself through shifting geography'. Note this is NOT the same gap as D-FJ-18, which is now fixed and covers the first ask; it is what happens after that ask has already succeeded.
DQ-T30.decision: ANSWERED 2026-08-14 by the owner: option (c) — a question naming stored data must be answered from a tool call in THIS turn, independent of any rail. The general fix and the most expensive, chosen over the two rail-scoped options.
DQ-T30.shipped: (c) built as the turn-level guard (5093177a1). MEASURING it exposed the real mechanism — a completed rail REMOVES the answering read (e133167d2). Both are load-bearing: guard alone 0/3, guard+reclaim 3/3.
DQ-T30.recommendation: RECOMMEND: rail completion suppresses WRITES only, never READS. A finished rail correctly stops driving, but the measured consequence is the model answering data questions from conversation memory - a stale count, then 'I have checked your consistency rules again' with ZERO tool calls and an INVENTED rule. Re-reading is not duplicated work: it IS the freshness the author asked for, and there is nothing to double-apply. The codebase already carries this reasoning for the rail gate's reclaimed reads; this is the same rule at turn scope.
DQ-T30.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.

DQ-T31.question: Should the world-setup intent gate open on WHAT THE REQUEST ASKS FOR rather than on its vocabulary? Options seen, none chosen: (a) add a declaration arm, as the consent check now has — if the request's own words match a gated setup tool's declared synonyms, treat the turn as setup intent; (b) widen the glossary_shaping skill router's phrase list (fixes these sentences, leaves the class); (c) leave it — N5a-FULL is a deliberate over-reach guard and being hard to open is the point, in which case the withheld tools must at least be VISIBLE as withheld, which is DQ-T3 and needs the model to call tool_list.
DQ-T31.evidence:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, two prompts for the same tool, K=3 each.
  v1 'Set up several kinds and attributes at once for this book's ONTOLOGY — I want to do it in one batch': intent_gate withheld 0 tools. Gate OPEN.
  v2 'Set these up together in one batch for this book: a kind called Faction with an attribute Allegiance, and a kind called Artifact with an attribute Origin': intent_gate withheld 4 — glossary_propose_batch, glossary_plan, glossary_propose_kinds, glossary_book_sync_apply. Gate SHUT.
The CONCRETE request — the one that names the exact kinds to create, and is world-setup by definition — is the one denied the tools. The vague one, which the model could not act on (it correctly asked WHICH kinds), got them.
CONSEQUENCE, not inferred: with the batch tool invisible, the model reached for glossary_adopt_standards on 3/3 and suspended on ITS card — adopting SYSTEM standards, which would not create Faction or Artifact at all. It substituted a different tool with different semantics rather than saying it could not do what was asked.
DQ-T31.why_the_DQ_T3_stamp_did_not_help: The stamp is emitted by tool_list/tool_load and the model called NEITHER on any run. This is the D-LAZY-TAIL-UNUSED interaction in full: a tool is withheld, the notice that would explain it lives behind a discovery call the model does not make, and the model substitutes. It is also the first NON-VOID instance of the DQ-T3 condition — three earlier attempts all found the gate open.
DQ-T31.status: OPEN — product decision, recorded per the RUNBOOK rather than answered.
DQ-T31.recommendation: RECOMMEND (a) - add a DECLARATION arm to the intent gate: if the request's own words match a gated setup tool's declared synonyms, the turn is setup intent. It is the rule R1 answerability already applies at the advertise chokepoint, so it introduces no new concept, and it fixes the class rather than the two measured sentences. The evidence is decisive against (b): two prompts asking for the SAME tool differ only in phrasing, and the gate opens for one while withholding four tools for the other. DQ-T33.sharpened_by: The root cause is now known: the turn is not empty, it contains a stray `<tool_call|>` delimiter. So the product question is narrower than 'what do we show for an empty turn' — it is 'the model emitted a malformed call; do we retry it, surface the last tool error, or say something generic?'
DQ-T33.recommendation: RECOMMEND yes - surface the last tool error when the turn produces no text. A blank reply is indistinguishable to the author from a hung request, and the service already HAS the error it is withholding. 🔴 THE evidence FIELD OF THIS DQ IS EMPTY. This recommendation rests on the question as posed plus adjacent findings in this loop (a dead call recorded as a silent success; a silent turn is not a completion) - not on a measurement of this behaviour. Measure it before deciding.
DQ-T33.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.
DQ-T33.mechanism_now_known_2026_08_24:
THE DECISION HAS A MECHANISM UNDER IT NOW, WHICH SPLITS IT IN TWO. It was posed as 'what does the service show the author when a turn says nothing' - one question, answerable only in the abstract because the silence had no known cause. It now has one:

The model abandons the structured tool-call channel and emits ONLY the closing control token `<tool_call|>`. There is no call to salvage. The hold that would have caught it is keyed on the OPENING token, a different string, so the delimiter flushes into the reasoning channel and the pass ends as an ordinary 'stopped without a tool call'. `_is_bare_toolcall_marker_only` now names that state, with 14 tests and a proven-RED falsifier.

SO THERE ARE TWO SEPARABLE QUESTIONS, and only the second is really a product one:

  (a) WHAT THE SERVICE DOES. The model's INTENT was a tool call - it emitted the delimiter for one. Retrying that pass is ordinary engineering on a degenerate generation, not a choice about what the assistant may say. It is cost-bearing (one more provider call) and it changes turn behaviour, which is why it is not shipped unilaterally - but if (a) is answered 'retry', (b) may never fire in practice.

  (b) WHAT THE AUTHOR SEES if the retry also comes back degenerate. This is the original question and it stays the owner's. The constraint the loop already recorded still binds: putting words in the assistant's mouth here would be this loop's own 'prose is not the lever' mistake in service code.

RECOMMENDATION: answer (a) first. It is cheap, it is measurable (the log line now counts the population), and it is the half that could unblock settings_provider_inventory - which fails 1 run in 5 on precisely this.

DQ-T36.measured: 30 of the 65 blocked tools were never advertised (surfaced 0/N across clean runs, zero transport errors). DQ-T36.why_it_is_not_merely_a_reachability_ques: A budget-dropped tool is still reachable via tool_list -> tool_load, and the model DOES use that path (registry_get_workflow: 'I do not have access to its internal instructions without loading it first'). What is not survivable is the OTHER outcome: when the missing tool is a WRITE, the turn reports the write as DONE. world_map_update_marker 5/5, kg_triage_resolve 5/5 (which rendered the post-resolution state to make it convincing), plan_keep_material 4/5 with zero tool calls, world_map_remove_region 1/5. Same condition produced honest refusals elsewhere, so the model is not uniformly at fault and the surface is the variable.
DQ-T36.options_seen_none_chosen: (a) reserve a slot for any tool whose declared synonyms match the request, so a named tool is never silently absent; (b) leave selection as-is and make the ABSENCE explicit to the model, the way DQ-T3's withheld-stamp already does for gated tools; (c) leave both and rely on tool_list -> tool_load, accepting that a write tool may be missing from a write turn.
DQ-T36.note: Option (c) is the status quo and is measured to produce false success. It is listed so the decision is made rather than defaulted into.
DQ-T36.cycle: P1-SURFACE, cycle 1 of the resolution loop — 25 tools.
DQ-T36.measured_2026_08_22_cycle_2:
THE MECHANISM IS NOW MEASURED, not hypothesised, using the platform's own functions offline (scripts/toolloop/hotseed_starvation_probe.py imports _budget_names_impl / hot_tool_names / surface_hot_domains rather than reimplementing them). A turn's advertised set is: the hot seed (a surface's hot DOMAINS, filtered to a HOT_SEED_TOKEN_BUDGET of 2000 tokens) UNION the session's activated_tools UNION core/frontend UNION whatever answerable_tools forces on. On the studio surface that is 120 candidates keeping 21.

THE BUDGET IS THE CULLING MECHANISM AND IT SYSTEMATICALLY CUTS SUPPLIERS. It orders reads by ASCENDING schema size, which is inversely correlated with how central a tool is — tool_surface.py already says so in its own words: 'a primary read takes filters and documents them, while a peripheral one takes a single id ... Fitting the MOST tools is not fitting the RIGHT ones.' Measured casualties: composition_motif_search 900 tok, composition_arc_template_list 356, composition_authoring_run_list 223 — all STARVED, all list/search tools, all the supplier of a blocked tool.

THE SECOND HALF OF THE QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED IN THE CODE. A tool the request NAMES *is* guaranteed a place: answerable_tools forces a synonym match onto the wire 'whatever the budget' (tool_surface.py), capped at ANSWERABLE_MAX=8. So the guarantee exists — what was missing is that it is keyed on the AUTHOR's words, and a SUPPLIER is named by the REFUSAL rather than by the author. That gap is what cycle 2 fixed reactively (D-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-THE-TURN-CANNOT-SEE).

THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE IS NOW STALE. It says 30 of 65 blocked tools were never advertised. Swept 2026-08-22 across the 48 still-blocked: 46 are ANSWERABLE against their own recorded prompts, so their 'surfaced 0/N' predates cycle 1's 37 declaration widenings and has not been re-measured. The two that are not answerable are propose_edit (a real gap — it declares no synonyms) and tool_load (NOT a gap — no author asks to load a tool schema).
DQ-T36.recommendation_2026_08_22: Do NOT widen ALWAYS_HOT_READS to rescue the starved suppliers, and do not raise HOT_SEED_TOKEN_BUDGET. Both spend the authoring surface's prefix on every turn to fix a case that arises only after a refusal, and tool_surface.py's own docstring asks for evidence rather than intuition before adding to that set. The reactive arming shipped in cycle 2 costs nothing on turns that do not need it and is measured working live. What IS worth deciding: whether a required argument may ship with an EMPTY description (105 of 467 do, 75 of them id-shaped) — because that, not the budget, is what leaves a refusal with no tool to name.
DQ-T36.the_second_half_is_now_answered_in_code_:
'Should a tool the request NAMES be guaranteed a place?' - the platform shipped YES. R1 answerability forces a tool onto the wire when the request matches its declared synonyms, ahead of the budget, domain selection and the rail. Measured consequence: D-LAZY-TAIL-UNUSED's population went from 30 of 65 blocked tools surfacing 0/N to ZERO blocked tools, and its four false-success instances are gate-backed at 5/5 surfaced.

Left OPEN deliberately: the FIRST half ('what decides which tools are advertised') is still a real question - R1 is the last word on the surface but five other mechanisms narrow it first, and a DQ is the owner's to close, not mine.

DQ-T41.blocked_by: a product decision about which tool wins an ambiguous request, which is not mine
DQ-T41.question: When two tools tie on synonym match, should a DOMAIN-SPECIFIC tool take precedence over a GENERIC one — and should that precedence be a declared field or an implicit ranking rule?
DQ-T41.measured:
composition_generate: surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, ZERO errors. On its own prompt five tools are answerable and THREE tie at synonym length 13 — book_chapter_create, book_chapter_save_draft, composition_generate. The domain tool declares 'write chapter'; the generics declare 'write the chapter' and 'write chapter prose'. No precedence exists, so the tie is broken arbitrarily.

The worst outcome is not the miss. When the tie breaks toward book_chapter_save_draft the model supplies prose it wrote ITSELF (D-GROUNDED-REQUEST-ANSWERED-WITH-UNGROUNDED-PROSE), so an ambiguous ranking silently converts a grounded request into an ungrounded one.
DQ-T41.why_it_is_not_mine: Precedence changes which tool wins for EVERY ambiguous request, not just this one — it is a product decision about what the platform should do when a user's words fit two tools, and it can only be evaluated against the whole catalogue. Cycle 2's arming cannot help here and that is structural: arming is REACTIVE and fires on a refusal, so a tool the model never CALLS never produces one.
DQ-T41.recommendation:
DECLARE it, do not infer it. Today's lesson on settings_list_models is that two attempts to make a declaration louder were measured and refuted, and what worked was changing the MECHANISM. Lengthening composition_generate's synonym is the same refuted move. A `_meta.specificity` (or an explicit `supersedes: [tool]`) makes the intended winner reviewable and testable, where an implicit 'domain beats generic' heuristic is a rule nobody can see in the declaration and that silently reorders 315 tools.

DO NOT ship a tie-break without measuring the OTHER side: any rule that promotes composition_generate here demotes something else elsewhere, and this loop has no measurement of that population. Recall before precision — the same order that applies to a lint.
DQ-T41.scope_measured_2026_08_23:

DQ-T41.second_instance_2026_08_23:
A SHARPER CASE THAN composition_generate's, and it changes what the decision has to cover. There the three tied tools are peers. Here a GENERIC tool ties a DOMAIN tool by borrowing its words:

    'Cancel that job.'                     translation_job_control 10  |  jobs_cancel 10
    'Stop the translation for this book.'  translation_job_control 16  |  jobs_cancel 16

jobs_cancel declares 'stop the translation', 'cancel it', 'stop that one', 'cancel my task'. Its 'stop the translation' is translation_job_control's 'stop translation' with an article added - so the generic tool ties the specific one EXACTLY in the phrasing where the user names the domain.

A precedence rule stated as 'domain-specific beats generic' would resolve both instances. A rule stated as 'longer synonym wins' would resolve NEITHER, because both are exact ties - which is worth knowing before the mechanism is chosen.
DQ-T41.third_instance_and_a_recommendation_2026:
MEASURED: THE TIES THIS QUESTION IS ABOUT ARE MANUFACTURED BY THE MATCHER. See D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-NOT-GENUINE. Two mechanisms, both measured against the deployed code:
  * _answer_norm strips articles, so composition_generate's 'write chapter', book_chapter_create's 'write A chapter' and book_chapter_save_draft's 'write THE chapter' all become the same 13-character string — an exact three-way tie among tools that declared different things, and the article was how their authors told create from edit.
  * the match loop BREAKS on a tool's first matching synonym, so composition_generate's 'cowrite' — matched by exactly 1 tool in 315, and named outright in the prompt — never reaches the ranker at all.

RECOMMENDATION: rank by SPECIFICITY rather than LENGTH — how many catalogue tools match the same normalised synonym. It is computable from the catalogue at that moment, needs no new declaration, and resolves all three recorded instances, including jobs_cancel vs translation_job_control, WITHOUT needing a domain-beats-generic rule. A rule stated as 'longer synonym wins' resolves none of them, because every instance is an exact tie.

PREREQUISITE: collect a tool's BEST matching synonym instead of its first, or no tie-break can see the discriminating term.

DQ-T46.blocked_by: a cost decision about a listing surface, which is the owner's: verifying reachability means a cross-service call per listed job.
DQ-T46.question: Should `control_caps` promise only what the controlling tool can actually reach? Today it is computed from the job's STATUS and KIND alone (derive_control_caps(status, kind, retryable)), so jobs_list can offer 'cancel' on a job whose owning service will refuse - measured today on 14 of 14 controllable translation jobs, every one referencing a book that no longer exists.
DQ-T46.the_options:
(a) VERIFY - jobs_list asks the owning service whether each job is reachable. Honest, and it costs one cross-service call per listed job on a paginated list: the expensive option, and the one that makes the field a real promise.
(b) DOCUMENT - say in jobs_list/jobs_get that control_caps is derived from status and kind, and that the owning service is authoritative and may still refuse. Costs nothing and makes the field honest without making it reliable.
(c) NARROW THE REFUSAL instead - let the controlling tool say WHY, e.g. 'this job's book no longer exists'. Cheap, but it is exactly the H13 boundary I over-reached on earlier today: 'the book is gone' and 'you lost your grant' are different facts about a book, and distinguishing them is an existence oracle about someone else's book.

(a) is principled but pays a per-job cross-service call forever for a case that, in production, needs a DELETED BOOK to arise - the population measured here was manufactured entirely by this harness. DQ-T46.what_I_did_NOT_measure: How often a control_cap is offered and refused for reasons OTHER than a deleted book - a revoked grant, a job that finished between the list and the call. carried_observations.note: services/composition-service/app/services/plan_forge_service.py:885 (`validate`) reads `latest_artifact(book_id, run_id, 'package')` - the same single-artifact read that made plan_bootstrap_propose preview one arc of three (T1-D3). validate() feeds `run_rules(spec, package)`, so on a multi-arc run it plausibly validates the last arc's package against the whole spec. NOT investigated and NOT fixed: it is plan_validate's tool, and the cycle boundary says one tool at a time. For that tool's cycle.

The studio's manuscript panel reads '6 chuong' (6 chapters) and lists six treeitems for book 019ff497, where book-service holds ZERO chapters and composition holds 6 outline_node (planned, chapter_id NULL). The panel renders PLANNED nodes with the label and count of WRITTEN chapters, so an author cannot tell a plan from a manuscript. Measured 2026-08-13 alongside chapters=0.

The new-chat modal ([data-testid=new-chat-dialog]) does not trap input: with the dialog open, text typed into the chat composer underneath was accepted AND SENT to the existing session while the dialog stayed open and unsubmitted. Measured 2026-08-13 - it is why a run intended for a fresh session landed in a stale one carrying the model's earlier stuck conclusion. plan_bootstrap_propose.run_id is NOT declared in contracts/agent-runtime-tool-contracts.json, so D-FJ-11's invented-supplier-id check (which drops a `plan`-declared *_id holding a non-UUID before dispatch) never fires for it. Measured 2026-08-13: the model sent run_id='arc_1_compiled_id_placeholder', which passed the gateway, minted a Tier-A approval card, spent the author's approval, and only then hit the tool's own shape check. plan_compile.run_id IS declared; this sibling is not. Declaring it would refuse the placeholder before the gate.
